docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: All notable changes to linecaster. The format follows Keep a Changelog; each release lists upgrade notes first, then additions, changes, deprecations, removals and fixes. Versions follow the tags; the first is v0.1.0.

docs.title: Upgrade notes
docs.text:
• The pybookget extra is gone: linecaster reads IIIF Presentation and METS/MODS manifests itself (linecaster.formats.manifests, on lxml) and fetches over http(s) with its own HTTP layer (linecaster.net: httpx with HTTP/2 and fake-useragent, both core dependencies now). Who is affected: anything that asks for linecaster[pybookget] (a derivative's script or project, uv sync --extra pybookget, which fails; uv warns about the unknown extra). What to do: drop the extra (linecaster[ray,pybookget] becomes linecaster[ray]) and relock; a derivative that imports pybookget itself lists it as its own dependency. The relocked environments lose pybookget, pyrate-limiter and tenacity, and those that had no http(s) before (bind.py, launch.py, the test scripts) gain httpx's HTTP/2 packages (h2, hpack, hyperframe) and fake-useragent; torch is unchanged everywhere.
  • A reader's http settings (and HTTPFetcher(**config)) are the fields of linecaster.net.http.HTTPConfig, with the same defaults as before (HTTP_DEFAULTS), instead of any field of pybookget's Config. Who is affected: code that passes a pybookget-only field (show_progress, retry_multiplier, cookie_file, header_file, ...): it is now a TypeError. What to do: leave the field out. The wait after the n-th failed attempt is retry_wait_min * 2**(n-1) seconds, at most retry_wait_max, on the direct path as through proxies; with the defaults (retry_wait_min 2) that is the wait it was, and only a changed retry_wait_min waits otherwise.
  • The HTTP policy has a new schema, in three levels (http): every request at the root, the proxy path's own section proxies:, and hosts:. What blocks is declared once for both paths (block_on, default [429], statuses and html): direct a block pauses the worker's requests to the host, through proxies it leaves the proxy out there. Who is affected: every policy file with pause_on, blacklist_on, blacklist_ttl, blacklist_threshold, proxies_per_worker or proxies as a plain path: the run stops at startup with a PipelineConfigError that names the line to write. What to do: pause_on: [429, 503] becomes block_on: [429, 503]; blacklist_on: [403] becomes block_on: [429, 403] (the statuses of both in one list); proxies: proxies.txt becomes proxies: {file: proxies.txt}; proxies_per_worker: 1, blacklist_ttl: 72h and blacklist_threshold: 2 become proxies: {per_worker: 1, block_ttl: 72h, broken_after: 2}. pause_on: [] (429s retried on the direct path) becomes block_on: [], which now also leaves 429s through proxies to the retries; keep block_on: [429] and set max_retries if a 429 should only block through proxies.
  • A 429 through proxies blocks the proxy only while 429 is in block_on. Who is affected: a policy whose block_on leaves 429 out (it blocked the proxy whatever blacklist_on said). What to do: add 429 to block_on to leave the proxy out on a 429; without it a 429 is a retryable status, retried after the backoff through the next proxy.
  • Unexpected HTML (a 2xx response with an HTML page where an image, XML, JSON or a manifest was expected) is a failed attempt on both paths: it counts, is retried after the backoff, is traced 200-html, and after the last attempt the fetch fails with linecaster.net.http.UnexpectedHTML (through proxies as MaxRetriesExceeded's cause), which names the expected format and the content type. HTML is told by the body's first bytes (after a byte order mark, whitespace and comments): an HTML document, whatever its label; under text/html also an HTML element, plain text or nothing. Data a server mislabels as text/html (JSON, XML with or without a declaration, an image) still passes, in ResourceReader too. Before, through proxies it blocked the proxy for an hour without using up an attempt; on a direct connection an image failed at once as an unreadable image and a resource failed at once. ManifestReader now says what it expects too (the manifest, the page images, ALTO files), so an HTML page there is retried and fails as UnexpectedHTML instead of passing as a manifest or image that does not parse. Who is affected: runs whose hosts answer a block or a soft 404 with HTML and 200. What to do: for a host whose HTML pages are a block (a CDN's challenge), block_on: [429, html] at that host leaves the proxy out again (direct: the worker pauses); stop_on: [html] stops the run as before; max_retries: 0 fails such a page after one attempt.
  • A block without Retry-After lasts 60 s at first and twice as long on each repeat (for that host, and through proxies for that proxy, until a successful response there; linecaster.net.http.block_wait), at most the host's block_ttl through proxies (default 3600 s) and max_pause direct (default 6 h). Before, a blocked proxy was left out for blacklist_ttl (3600 s) at once, and a direct pause doubled from 60 s up to an hour. With Retry-After nothing changes. Who is affected: runs through proxies whose hosts send 429s without Retry-After (their proxies come back sooner and are retried there), and direct runs with long pauses (a single pause may now pass an hour). What to do: nothing to keep a polite run; no setting restores the flat hour through proxies, and block_ttl is the ceiling of the doubling (proxies: {block_ttl: 72h} for a host whose block lasts three days); max_pause bounds the pauses direct.
  • The doubling of a proxy's blocks (and of a broken proxy's time out) travels with the proxy through the broker: each mark records its last wait without Retry-After (last_wait) and is kept that long past its end (keep), so a worker that claims a released proxy continues the doubling (60, 120, 240 s across workers) instead of starting at 60 s; before, each worker kept its own and a proxy that changed hands started again. The doubling starts again after a successful response through the proxy from that host (its ended marks are deleted then), or when the next block comes more than the last wait after the last one ended (a quiet period; also on the direct path, per host, linecaster.net.http.doubling). The broker's layout, file names and format (linecaster.broker/1) are unchanged. Who is affected: runs through proxies whose hosts block without Retry-After (their proxies stay out longer when they change hands), and workers of 0.4.0 and of this version sharing a broker: 0.4.0 reads the new marks' ends as before, ignores the new fields and deletes a mark at its end (the doubling then starts again), and this version reads 0.4.0's marks and starts their doubling at 60 s. linecaster broker clean keeps a mark during its keep (status no longer counts it expired); clean --marks removes it, and the doubling starts again. What to do: nothing; proxies: {block_ttl: ...} remains the ceiling.
  • A broken proxy (a proxy error, no connection to it) is left out after 3 such errors in a row (broken_after; it was 1), first for 300 s (broken_ttl; it was 3600 s), doubling each time it breaks again before it carries an answer, at most block_ttl. Who is affected: runs through proxy lists with unreliable proxies (each costs up to three attempts before it is left out, and comes back sooner). What to do: proxies: {broken_after: 1, broken_ttl: 3600} restores leaving it out at its first error for an hour.
  • max_pause is one count on both paths, per worker and host (http, linecaster.net.http.PauseTotal): the time the worker's requests to the host have waited since the host's last successful response, direct in pauses, through proxies for a usable proxy; once the next wait would pass it, the run stops (StopRequests). Before, through proxies it limited each wait for a proxy alone and started again whenever one became usable, so a host that turned every proxy away over and over (a page that is always HTML under block_on: [429, html]) never ended the run. Who is affected: runs through proxies whose hosts block again and again without a successful response: they now stop after max_pause of waiting. What to do: raise max_pause for a host whose blocks may last longer in all (hosts: {images.example.org: {max_pause: 24h}}).
  • On the direct path a block pauses only the requests to the host that sent it (Pause per host, HTTPFetcher.pause_for(host), HTTPFetcher.pauses()); before, it paused every request of the fetcher, whichever host it went to (one fetcher serves every host without an HTTP policy, e.g. a manifest server and an image server). Who is affected: runs whose readers fetch from several hosts directly; code that used HTTPFetcher.pause (gone). What to do: nothing for runs; code uses pause_for(host).

  • The HTTP settings of a reader (http) and of HTTPFetcher are renamed with the policy: proxy_blacklist_threshold is broken_after, proxy_blacklist_ttl is block_ttl, proxy_blacklist_on and pause_on are block_on (which includes 429 by default rather than adding to it), proxies_per_worker is per_worker, pause_wait is first_wait, and pause_max_wait is gone (the doubling stops at max_pause); broken_ttl is new; stop_on and block_on take html. In linecaster.net.http, PAUSE_ON, PAUSE_FIRST_WAIT, PROXY_BLACKLIST_THRESHOLD and PROXY_BLACKLIST_TTL are BLOCK_ON, BLOCK_FIRST_WAIT, BROKEN_AFTER (3) and BLOCK_TTL, with BROKEN_TTL new; PAUSE_MAX_WAIT and ProxyBlocked are gone; Pause takes first_wait and max_total (no max_wait); pause_left() gives what began the pause in words (HTTP 429, an HTML page) instead of the status; ProxyPool.block takes the Retry-After seconds or None (the doubling) with cap and first, ProxyPool.broken takes after, first and cap; each is now note_block/note_broken (in memory, at once: the fetcher calls them on its event loop) followed by publish (the broker's mark and release, which the fetcher runs in a thread). HTTPPolicy.stops_on_html is gone (the fetcher stops on html itself), and HTTPPolicy.describe() takes no options (the run's options are the policy's base) and states every rule that holds per host and path, defaults and opt-ins alike. Who is affected: code that builds fetchers or readers with these settings, or uses these names. What to do: rename as above; http={"broken_after": 1, "broken_ttl": 3600} and http={"block_on": [429, "html"]} restore the earlier proxy behavior.

  • --http-policy holds for every input fetched over http(s): --manifests (the manifests, their images and OCR files) and --pages (the images it fetches again) take it too, as --items and --parquet did (ManifestReader(http_policy=...), PageRecordReader(http_policy=...); every reader goes through linecaster.net.policy.Fetchers, one fetcher per host's settings). Who is affected: runs with --manifests or --pages and a policy (refused at startup before) and their workers (with proxies in the policy, the default worker count follows them, as for the other inputs); ManifestReader now has one fetcher per host's settings and takes a random User-Agent per task and fetcher. The recipe item-texts@1's expanded pipeline gains http_policy: null (a catalog migration; its behavior is unchanged). What to do: nothing; a derivative that pinned the old pipeline hash of item-texts@1 reads the new one from the lock.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• docs/reference/http.md: the defaults, blocks on both paths, unexpected HTML, retries and deadlines, the trace entries and the HTTP policy's schema with its inheritance, and an example for a CDN-protected host.
  • HTTPFetcher takes clock, wall_clock and sleep, so tests check its waits without sleeping.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• The engine packages (linecaster-kraken, -paddlex, -tesseract, -surya, -indra, -services) 0.1.4 accept linecaster >=0.1,<0.6.
  • The direct path and the path through proxies are one retry loop (HTTPFetcher._attempts), with the counts, waits, Retry-After, deadline per attempt, 404 fallback, trace entries and errors each had before; the rate limits are linecaster's own sliding windows (linecaster.net.limits.RateLimiter).
  • --proxies says how a blocked and a broken proxy are left out now, and --http-policy lists the new fields.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• A status in stop_on is traced as that status (it was no-response).
  • The console's progress line could fail with a TypeError when a pause or the breaker ended while it read them (Pause.remaining, Breaker.next_try read their end once).
  • A blocked or broken proxy's marks are written to the broker in a thread, no longer in the fetcher's event loop, where a slow store (object storage) held up all of its requests.
  • A Retry-After of inf or nan is no Retry-After, and one beyond about three years, in seconds or as an HTTP-date, is that long; such a value made a proxy's block mark fail to be written.

docs.title: Upgrade notes
docs.text:
• linecaster.runtime.jobs.dependencies(commit, script) returns Dependencies (requirements, constraints, overrides) instead of a list of requirements, and HF Jobs resolve the versions of the script's lock instead of the newest ones allowed. Who is affected: code that calls dependencies() itself (a derivative's launcher) and Jobs that relied on getting newer versions than the lock's. What to do: pass the result to JobsExecutor or GPUJobsExecutor as it is (the pins apply), or its .requirements where a list is needed (datatrove's JobsPipelineExecutor, which then installs unpinned); relock a script to move its Jobs' versions.
  • linecaster's s3fs extra is gone: the core installs datatrove[io,s3] (datatrove's s3 extra is s3fs), so s3:// paths work in every environment. Who is affected: anything that asks for linecaster[s3fs] (a derivative's script, uv sync --extra s3fs): uv sync --extra s3fs fails, and uv warns about linecaster[s3fs]. What to do: drop the extra (linecaster[ray,pybookget,s3fs] becomes linecaster[ray,pybookget]) and relock. Environments that had no S3 before (bind.py, launch.py, the test scripts) now have s3fs, aiobotocore and botocore, and botocore's python-dateutil<3 moves python-dateutil from 4.0.0 to 2.9.0.post0 there.
  • pipelines/transcribe_modular.py no longer installs kraken (linecaster-kraken, the kraken fork, torch): it has PaddleX and Tesseract only. Who is affected: anyone running a kraken preset (kraken-ppocrv6-{tiny,small,medium}) or the squiddle recipe with that script or with uv run launch.py squiddle, in-process or with --backend served without --endpoint, and HF Jobs of that script with kraken presets. The run now stops before it starts with a CatalogError that says where kraken is. What to do: run the chain in an environment that adds kraken (your own script running transcribe_modular.v1 with linecaster-kraken), or keep this script and pass --backend served --endpoint URL with a server started from such an environment (that script's serve). An existing script environment keeps kraken installed until uv sync --script pipelines/transcribe_modular.py removes it.
  • --namespace has no default and is required with --on hf-jobs. Who is affected: every launch on Hugging Face Jobs that left it out. What to do: pass --namespace NS, the user or organization the Jobs run under and are billed to; it is not taken from the logged-in account.
  • pipelines/transcribe_modular.py: --naming squiddleocr is gone; --naming flat writes the per-page files in one folder and --suffix SUFFIX adds to each file's stem (with either naming). Who is affected: runs with --naming squiddleocr. What to do: --naming flat --suffix .paddle writes the same <page>.paddle.<ext> files.
  • The catalog holds no evidence records: linecaster is not a data repository. src/linecaster/catalog/data/evidence/ is gone, the catalog no longer reads or verifies an evidence/ folder (Directory.evidence is gone, and linecaster catalog verify no longer checks that evidence names a known edition), the generated preset and recipe pages have no Evidence table, the catalog index no CER column, and the docs and the presets' prose quote no measurements. The evidence format stays (linecaster.evidence/1, linecaster.catalog.Evidence, schemas/evidence-1.json) without the source board. Who is affected: code that read the shipped records or a catalog folder's (Catalog().dirs[0].evidence) or the numbers on the generated pages, and evidence records with source: board. What to do: keep evidence records in the evaluation's own repository and validate them with Evidence; give a leaderboard's numbers source: vendor-benchmark or card-claim (a claim), or measure them yourself (own-run). The measurements made so far stay in NOTES.md.
  • linecaster.runtime.jobs no longer has WheelJobsExecutor, wheel_volume, build_wheel, upload_wheel, bucket_parts, WHEEL_MOUNT or ENGINE_SCRIPT. They served derivatives that are retired. A derivative's pipeline gets its Jobs' dependencies from its own script: dependencies(commit, "<its script>.py").

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• The engine packages (linecaster-kraken, -paddlex, -tesseract, -surya, -indra, -services) 0.1.3 accept linecaster >=0.1,<0.5.
  • linecaster is stated as a generalist tool (CLAUDE.md, the architecture reference): it depends on no collection, site, institution or project, and names none. Help texts and docs use example.org, the tests library.test and example.org; docstrings, comments, NOTES.md and this changelog describe behavior and hardware instead of a derivative, a leaderboard or a machine.
  • The presets', recipes' and models' prose and provenance cite the model card or the vendor's documentation, with a departure from the card labelled linecaster's choice, and make no unmeasured claims (nothing "validated against a reference implementation's outputs", run on a sample or compared there). No functional field changed: every edition and hash stays.
  • The User-Agent stays datatrove's HF-Research/1.0, now stated as a decision (CLAUDE.md, USER_AGENT, the pipelines reference).
  • With --endpoint a pipeline no longer needs the served engines installed in its own environment: they run in the server's. pipelines/transcribe_modular.py --recipe squiddle --endpoint URL runs against a kraken server.
  • A source is declared by the package that needs it: linecaster-kraken declares the kraken fork, linecaster-paddlex lists opencv-contrib-python and points it at the stub. uv lock applies the sources of path and git dependencies, so the pipeline scripts no longer list pybookget, kraken, opencv-contrib-python or s3fs themselves; the locks keep every version.
  • linecaster.runtime.jobs.dependencies takes the installed packages' own sources from the script's lock (pybookget, the kraken fork at its locked commit, the OpenCV stub), so a Job gets them whether or not the script lists them.
  • Only linecaster-kraken pins torch; pipelines/transcribe_page.py drops its torch==2.14.0 override (surya-ocr allows >=2.7,<3; the lock keeps 2.14.0). tests/test_scripts.py fixes each lock's torch.

  • The compatibility reference states the versioning policy: while 0.x, a breaking change is a minor release (0.3 → 0.4), everything else a patch.

  • HF Jobs are reproducible: jobs.dependencies pins every package the script's lock takes from an index (name==version) as a constraint and carries the script's [tool.uv] override-dependencies; JobsExecutor runs each Job as a uv script whose inline metadata holds them (Dependencies.script), since uv run --with ignores constraints and overrides. --dry-run prints the three lists, and the run record keeps the new constraints and overrides next to dependencies.

  • --commit is optional with --on hf-jobs for a script outside the linecaster checkout that takes linecaster from a git tag, branch or rev (its Jobs install what its sources name); it stays required for linecaster's own scripts (jobs.needs_commit).

docs.title: Removed
docs.text:
• The evidence records in the catalog, the Evidence tables of the generated pages and the CER column of the catalog index; the evidence source board (upgrade notes).
  • linecaster.runtime.jobs: WheelJobsExecutor, wheel_volume, build_wheel, upload_wheel, bucket_parts, WHEEL_MOUNT and ENGINE_SCRIPT (upgrade notes).

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: • linecaster.runtime.jobs.dependencies reads git sources with a tag or branch (it raised KeyError: 'rev') and keeps their subdirectory (git+URL@REF#subdirectory=DIR), so a derivative's script pinned by tag runs on HF Jobs. A path source outside the linecaster checkout is a PipelineConfigError instead of a path relative to the checkout; markers are kept.

docs.title: Upgrade notes
docs.text: • The scripts no longer pin the numerically relevant versions (constraint-dependencies: ONNX Runtime, the CUDA libraries, cuDNN, transformers, tokenizers, Lightning, Pillow, SciPy, scikit-image). The locks still hold the same versions; a relock with --upgrade now moves them. HF Jobs (linecaster.runtime.jobs.dependencies) no longer add those pins to uv run --with, so a Job resolves their newest versions. torch stays at 2.14 (linecaster-kraken's pin).

docs.title: Removed
docs.text: • A derivative's goldens as the reference for the squiddle combination: tests/parity/compare_goldens.py, tests/parity/compare_exports.py and the parity pytest marker. They served the migration from that derivative; the last comparison is in NOTES.md.

docs.title: Upgrade notes
docs.text:
• A Ray launch (--on ray) now stops with a PipelineConfigError before it submits a task if no live node has what a task reserves (CPUs, memory, a GPU for a stage with models). Ray used to keep such tasks waiting without an error. A cluster that adds nodes on demand passes --no-fit-check (RayExecutor(check_fit=False)).
  • Worker counts derived "one per CPU", and the broker's random start among worker slots, count the CPUs the process may use (linecaster.runtime.cpus.available_cpus: a Ray task's CPUs, else the cgroup's CPU quota, else the affinity) instead of os.cpu_count(). In a container with a CPU limit they are now that limit, not the machine's CPUs.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• --mem-per-task-gb (RayExecutor(mem_per_task_gb=...)): the memory a Ray task reserves, whatever its CPUs; --mem-per-cpu-gb per CPU stays the default. --cpus-per-task and --mem-per-cpu-gb have help texts.
  • RayExecutor.check_cluster(nodes) and --no-fit-check: the launch check, which also logs how many tasks fit at once and warns when fewer than the run's tasks at once do.
  • linecaster.runtime.cpus: available_cpus(), cgroup_cpu_quota(), ray_task_cpus() and limit_threads(n). Each Ray task sizes OpenMP, BLAS, OpenCV and torch thread pools to its CPUs (variables already set are kept; the servers a task starts inherit them).
  • The README's Ray section says what a task reserves, how to start workers for it, and how to run on Kubernetes.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: • The harvest's help and the pipelines reference say that --retry-failed fetches only the failed pages of a book with --reuse, and every page of it without (since --reuse is off by default).

docs.title: Upgrade notes
docs.text:
• The pipeline scripts' code moved into the package: each script in pipelines/ runs the pipeline shape of its name in linecaster.pipelines (harvest, transcribe_modular, transcribe_vlm, transcribe_page, bind). Their command lines, help texts and pipeline_sha256 are unchanged; the run record's script hash changes with the script file. Code that loaded a script as a module imports its shape instead (from linecaster.pipelines import transcribe_modular).
  • linecaster.runtime.run.describe_script(script, argv) and load_script(script) are gone: run.describe(shape, argv, c=None, script=None) builds a shape in the describe mode. describe_recipe finds the recipe's shape by its pipeline id (linecaster.pipelines.shape), so it no longer needs the repository checkout.

  • linecaster.catalog.code.pipelines() imports the shapes instead of reading the scripts: a Pipeline's source is its script in the checkout (None without one) and its new field shape the shape's source file.

  • pipelines/transcribe_modular.py --files writes no per-page files for a page a block failed on (it was written with what the blocks before the failure made of it: lines without text, an empty md); OUT/rejects/ lists the page and the page records keep it with its errors, as before. The pipeline's hash changes with --files (--new-pipeline to resume into an OUT of an earlier launch), not without. Item texts (--item-texts) still include such pages, with whatever text they have.

  • PageFileWriter has a new parameter skip_failed (default False: failed pages are written as before). Its recorded parameters gain the key, so the pipeline_sha256 of every pipeline with a PageFileWriter changes; resuming into an OUT of an earlier launch needs --new-pipeline.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• PageFileWriter(skip_failed=True): no files for a page that carries errors; counted as skipped_failed.
  • linecaster.pipelines: the pipeline shapes as library code, with shapes() and shape(pipeline_id); a derivative's script imports one and runs it with run.main in its own environment, with its own defaults.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text: • The engine packages (linecaster-kraken, -paddlex, -tesseract, -surya, -indra, -services) 0.1.2 accept linecaster >=0.1,<0.4.

docs.title: Upgrade notes
docs.text:
• The generated docs (the block and catalog pages, docs/index.md, docs/changelog.md, docs/llms*.txt) are no longer in git: linecaster docs writes them when the site is built, and git ignores them. Run linecaster docs before mkdocs serve or mkdocs build. linecaster docs --check and linecaster.docs.check are gone (nothing to compare against), and so are the README's generated preset and block tables with their markers (linecaster.catalog.docs.readme_tables, readme_section, MARK_START/MARK_END, linecaster.docs.blocks.readme_table, and linecaster.catalog.docs.write's readme): the README links to the site's catalog and blocks pages instead. A derivative that called linecaster docs --check drops the call; none of the known derivatives does.
  • pipelines/harvest.py no longer lists each item's folder in OUT for images to reuse unless --reuse is given. On some object storage the listing took over a minute even for empty folders, so every item waited before its pages were fetched; only the items a stopped launch was in have anything to reuse. Without --reuse their pages are fetched again and the files overwritten. The flag changes the pipeline's hash: a resume into an OUT of an earlier launch needs --new-pipeline.
  • How many proxies of a list a worker holds is the new HTTP-policy key proxies_per_worker (per host or at the root; also HTTPFetcher's and ProxyPool's parameter): share (the default) a fair share of the free ones, rebalanced as before, except that a worker claims at most 2 when it looks for proxies and grows to its share only by rebalancing, so the first workers no longer take the proxies of those still starting; 1 one proxy per worker, which sends every request through it and, when it is blocked or broken, releases it and claims another free one at once (useful with output on local disk or few proxies, with a worker per proxy); or a whole number N, up to N per worker, claimed one by one. Hosts that use one proxy list must set the same value. The default was 1 on main for a few hours and is share again: with one proxy per worker, using 250 proxies took 250 workers, and 250 workers writing to object storage hung in their listings of OUT/images (below); a run that wants one proxy per worker sets proxies_per_worker: 1.
  • The default worker count of a pipeline without engines whose rate-limited hosts all go through proxies, on a local or Ray run, follows the proxies available (those in the file, less those blocked or broken in the broker for the run's hosts and those held by another run's live workers), at most one per task: sharing them fairly (share, the default) one worker per available proxy and at most one per CPU, where such a run kept one worker; with proxies_per_worker 1 or N one per available proxy divided by N (ceil(available / N)), not capped by the CPUs. With OUT on object storage (any fsspec protocol but a local one: s3://, gs://, hf://, az://, ...) the count stops at 64 (linecaster.runtime.run.OBJECT_STORAGE_WORKERS) in both modes: in one setup 250 workers writing to S3-compatible object storage hung where 64 ran cleanly. Give --workers for another count. The run states the count and why (250 proxies available, OUT on object storage → 64 workers, a fair share each). A host with rate limits and no proxy list keeps one worker; HF Jobs keep their rule (a worker is a Job).
  • linecaster.runtime.local.LocalExecutor's note may be a list of lines; linecaster.runtime.run.rate_note counts the proxies in use (1 of 2 proxies in use (1 proxy per worker)) when the workers hold fewer than the list.
  • A worker process no longer claims the lowest free worker slot of its machine: it takes a handed-over slot first, then the k-th free slot (one without a valid slot lease claimed more than a minute before, so a stopped run's slots are passed over and its peers' are not), k its executor's worker index (linecaster.broker.set_worker_index, set by LocalExecutor, RayExecutor and JobsExecutor; else random), and probes upward from there, so slot numbers no longer say in which order the processes came. Code that starts brokers itself and expects <machine>-0 first passes Broker(..., worker_index=(0, 1)).
  • A broker's renew logs a lost claim race (two claims at once both believed they won) at INFO, worker X lost a claim race for proxies/<id> to Y; it takes another; the WARNING ... lease on proxies/<id> expired (no renew within the lease time); it gives it up is only for a lease that really expired (its file gone or older than the lease time), which the worker now also gives up when nobody else has claimed the resource.
  • Proxies are shared through the broker (linecaster.broker, broker): --proxy-blocks FOLDER and an HTTP policy's root key proxy_blocks are gone; use --broker PATH and the root key broker (default OUT/logs/broker; runs pointed at one path share the proxies and their blocks). The old folder of block markers is not read; blocks found before are found again at the first request through each proxy. There is no alias.
  • With a proxy list the rate limits (--rate-limit, an HTTP policy's rate_limits for a host through proxies) hold per proxy, not per worker: each proxy is used by one worker at a time, which spaces its requests through the proxy by the strictest limit. A server sees up to the proxies times the limits, whatever the worker count, so a limit meant for all proxies together is now too high by the proxy count: give the limit one IP may send. Direct connections keep the limits per worker.
  • A host whose proxies are all blocked (or broken) no longer stops the run at once: its requests wait until a block ends or another worker gives a proxy back, up to the host's max_pause (6 h by default), and stop the run only when the first block ends later than that. A 429's Retry-After sets how long its proxy is blocked at the host, also when it is longer than blacklist_ttl (it was capped there).
  • The extra resilient-httpx is gone: a proxy list needs only linecaster[pybookget]. Scripts that list linecaster[...,resilient-httpx] drop it (pipelines/harvest.py does), or their install fails on the unknown extra. HTTPFetcher.proxies_in_rotation() and linecaster.net.http.proxy_rotation() are HTTPFetcher.proxy_counts() and proxy_counts() (held, blocked, free); HTTPFetcher's proxy_blocks and default_proxy_blocks are broker and default_broker; a request through proxies that used up its attempts raises linecaster.net.http.MaxRetriesExceeded (was resilient-httpx's, of the same name).
  • A 429 pauses the worker that got it instead of stopping the run or failing the page: an HTTP policy has a new per-host key pause_on (statuses that pause the worker's requests to the host until the response's Retry-After has passed, then retry the request; default [429]) and max_pause (default 6 h in all since the host's last successful response; beyond it the run stops). A policy with 429 in stop_on is refused (429 both in stop_on and pause_on): move it to pause_on (catalog.example.org: {direct: true, stop_on: [429, html]} becomes {direct: true, pause_on: [429], stop_on: [html]}), or keep it in stop_on with pause_on: [] to still stop the run on it; there is no alias. Without a policy the default applies as well: on a direct connection a 429 used to be retried per request by pybookget (each retry after the longer of its backoff and the Retry-After, at most 300 s, up to max_retries), the other requests going on meanwhile, and the page or resource failed with HTTPStatusError once its retries were used up; now the worker's requests to the host wait out the Retry-After (a minute doubling to an hour without one), the request is tried again without using up a retry, and the page does not fail. http={"pause_on": []} keeps the old behavior. Through a proxy list nothing changes: a 429 leaves that proxy out.
  • max_retries (http={"max_retries": ...}, an HTTP policy's) counts retries after the first attempt, as its name says, where it counted attempts: max_retries: n now makes n + 1 attempts, and 0 is a single attempt. The default is 4 (still 5 attempts). A setting written for the old meaning gets one attempt more; lower it by one to keep the old count. linecaster pins pybookget 1.2.0 (45814da), which counts this way too.
  • pp-doclayout-plus-l without an edition resolves to edition 2, which orders the regions with XY-Cut++ instead of plain XY-cut. A run that must keep the old order names pp-doclayout-plus-l@1.
  • pipeline_sha256 leaves an in-process engine's endpoint and timeout options out (ENGINE_OPERATIONAL: where its service is). A derivative's run whose engine has an option of either name gets another hash: a resume into its folder needs --new-pipeline. No released recipe is affected.
  • linecaster.testing.check_engine calls a page engine (recognition, unit page) with an empty transcription (no regions, no lines), not the sample layout's regions.
  • --rate-limit holds per worker (process), not per task: the tasks a worker runs one after the other share one fetcher and its limits (HTTPFetcher.shared), where each task started its limits afresh. A server sees the workers running at once times the limits, as before; the run now states it before it starts (run.rate_note).
  • --tasks and --workers default to an automatic choice (linecaster.runtime.run.allocate): a pipeline without engines (pipelines/harvest.py) runs tasks of about 1,000 pages (or 5 items) from its input, one worker with --rate-limit, one per CPU without; a pipeline with engines keeps one task, every task at once. Resuming a run started with the old default (--tasks 1) needs --tasks 1.
  • http(s) requests have a deadline per attempt (HTTP_DEFAULTS: pybookget's attempt_timeout=15 and attempt_min_rate=50_000, i.e. 15 s plus 1 s per 50 kB of Content-Length, counted after the rate limits): an attempt past it is cut and retried. A server that needs longer for a response without Content-Length needs http={"attempt_timeout": None} (or a longer one). linecaster pins pybookget bf8eee1, which has the setting.
  • --prefetch and the readers' prefetch= argument are gone: ManifestReader and ImageParquetReader request http(s):// pages ahead in a window that sizes itself; drop the option. linecaster.net.prefetched takes (entries, submit, cancel, future=, fetcher=).
  • ImageParquetReader and ManifestReader item tables divide rows, not files, over the tasks; ImageParquetReader no longer splits a task's rows by datatrove's ParquetReader.read_files_shard, so limit and skip apply before anything is fetched, and no Parquet file is a PipelineConfigError (was datatrove's RuntimeError). A table no longer needs splitting into one file per task.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Worker slots are claimed fast: processes started together (a local run's pool, Ray tasks, a multi-GPU Job's tasks) each take a different free slot (the k-th, k their linecaster.broker.set_worker_index), so they register in one claim each instead of racing for slot 0, then slot 1, ..., also when relaunched while a stopped run's slot leases are still valid; a run's first minutes no longer see early workers computing their share against the few registered so far. linecaster.broker.survey_kind lists who holds the resources of a kind (with their runs) and their live marks, from one listing.
  • An extra s3fs for s3:// paths in the linecaster command and code run in the project's environment (uv sync --extra s3fs, or --all-extras); the pipeline scripts bring their own. linecaster broker names a missing filesystem package in one line instead of a traceback.
  • The broker (linecaster.broker, broker): a shared folder, any DataFolder, through which workers across tasks, runs and machines agree on who holds which shared resource (leases, renewed within 180 s, claims decided by listing) and what is unavailable until when (marks per scope). A worker is a slot of its machine that outlives its processes: on Ray the next task on a machine takes over the slot the last one handed over, with its leases. Proxies are its first kind (linecaster.net.proxies.ProxyPool): each proxy has one worker at a time, each worker its fair share (rebalanced as workers join and leave), a block is a mark seen by whoever claims the proxy next, without the 30-s polling of the proxy-blocks folder it replaces, and the rate limits hold per proxy. The console shows the proxies held, blocked and free.
  • linecaster broker status PATH [--json], clean PATH [--leases] [--marks] and purge PATH (broker): what a broker's folder holds (workers, slots, per kind the resources held, free, blocked per scope, broken); removing what has expired (safe beside running workers), after a hard kill every heartbeat and lease (--leases: a relaunch gets slot 0 and the proxies at once instead of waiting up to 3 min for them to expire), every mark (--marks), or the whole layout (purge). Removing live files asks on a terminal and is refused without one (--yes, --dry-run). In code: linecaster.broker.survey_all, clean and purge.
  • XY-Cut++ reading order (Liu, Li and Wei, arXiv:2504.10258) for layout models without one: linecaster.data.geometry.xy_cut_plus_plus.xy_cut_plus_plus_order(boxes, labels, page_size), pure and deterministic, the paper's β, θ_v, τ_overlap, centering tolerance and edge weights as keyword arguments, its ambiguities resolved by the authors' Apache-2.0 implementation (NOTES.md, 2026-11-07). paddlex.layout.v1 takes it with the new option reading_order: xy-cut++ (default xy-cut, the plain XY-cut as before), and the new edition pp-doclayout-plus-l@2 sets it. place_unordered keeps plain XY-cut.
  • Nothing to size for a harvest: pipelines/harvest.py --parquet TABLE ... OUT --rate-limit 150/60 reads any page table as it is, in tasks of about 1,000 pages, with one worker that keeps the rate limits busy. linecaster.blocks.readers.tables divides Parquet tables over tasks by rows in equal shards (by row group); ImageParquetReader.auto_tasks() and ManifestReader.auto_tasks() suggest a task count from the input.
  • ImageParquetReader requests http(s):// images ahead, pages in the rows' order. linecaster.net.prefetched, the window both readers use, grows while the first request is out and none waits for the rate limits (HTTPFetcher.waiting), up to MAX_AHEAD, so one task keeps any rate limit busy.
  • HTTPFetcher.shared(**config): one fetcher per process and configuration, which the readers use, so the rate limits (and the window learned) hold across the tasks a worker runs one after the other; close_shared().
  • --parquet takes one .parquet file as well as a folder.
  • Resources: pipelines/harvest.py --items TABLE --item-key COL fetches items' remote files as served (ResourceReader, ResourceFilesWriter, ResourceRecordWriter), from URL templates (--resource KIND=URL with {item}) or a resource table (--url-key, --kind-key, --name-key): raw copies at OUT/<kind>/<item>/<name>.<ext>, a fetch record each in OUT/resources/<rank>.jsonl.gz, one item per task, --max-items, reuse, rejects, --retry-failed. Each response is checked (XML, JSON, images; an HTML page where another format was expected fails and counts toward the breaker).
  • The HTTP policy: --http-policy FILE (linecaster.net.policy.HTTPPolicy) gives the run's requests their settings from one YAML file, for every host at its root and per host under hosts: (an entry replaces the root's fields it names; the run's own options go between the two): rate limits, proxies or a direct connection, User-Agent, deadline, retries (max_retries), the proxy blocks folder (root only) and stop_on statuses (and html) that stop the run without a retry; each host's settings their own fetcher. Readers take it as http_policy=. For --items and --parquet. RejectWriter takes any unit.
  • A failed fetch says what failed: retries used up through proxies raise MaxRetriesExceeded naming the last error (after 5 attempts: HTTP 520, ... ReadTimeout (no message)), an empty pool AllProxiesExhausted with a message, and httpx's silent timeouts get one; and the fetch's record (attempts, tries, waits) goes with the exception into the failed page's trace (linecaster.net.http.failed_fetch), where it was dropped.
  • Outages are waited out: each fetcher has a breaker (linecaster.net.http.Breaker), which also opens after as many server errors in a row as a request has retries; a request whose retries ran out in a pause waits it out and tries again (at most BREAKER_WAITS times), so a request alone no longer fails before the breaker sees the outage. When at least half of the attempts in the last minute (20 at least) got a server error (5xx), requests pause; a probe goes out after a minute, then after waits that double up to ten minutes, and the first answer that is not a server error ends the pause. The pages wait instead of failing, and the progress line says paused: server errors. Cloudflare's 520-524 are retried like 502-504 (pybookget 91d39e4).
  • With --proxies a server error is retried through another proxy without blacklisting the one it came through (resilient-httpx blacklist_on={429}, storytracer's fork 1.5.0 at f706598): only a 429, a timeout or a connection or proxy error counts against a proxy, so an outage no longer empties the pool.
  • With --proxies (or a host's proxies), an HTML page where another format was expected is that proxy's block: the proxy is left out and the item goes on through the next one (linecaster.net.http.ProxyBlocked; HTTPFetcher.submit(..., expect=)), with no breaker pause. Without proxies such a page fails as before. The HTTP policy sets how long a blocked proxy is left out and after how many failures (blacklist_ttl: 72h, blacklist_threshold; durations in s, m, h or d). A host with no proxy left stops the run (StopRequests, a ServerError) naming when the first returns, where every following item failed with AllProxiesExhausted.
  • The HTTP policy can name statuses besides 429 that leave the proxy they came through out (blacklist_on: [403], resilient-httpx's blacklist_on); they are retried through the next proxy instead of failing the item.
  • Proxy blocks are shared through a folder of markers (--proxy-blocks FOLDER or the HTTP policy's proxy_blocks, default OUT/logs/proxy-blocks; linecaster.net.proxy_blocks), as datatrove shares finished tasks: each block is a marker written once and never changed, and every fetcher reads a host's markers at its first request there and every 30 s after. Every worker in every deployment mode, and every later run pointed at the same folder, leaves the blocked proxies out; a restarted run no longer sends requests into the blocks it found. linecaster pins resilient-httpx 1.6.0 (storytracer's fork, cdebe7d, block_proxy).
  • Through proxies, only a proxy's own failures leave it out: a block (a 429, a status in blacklist_on, an HTML block page) or a broken proxy (PROXY_ERRORS: a proxy error, no connection to it). A timeout, mostly a slow server, is retried through another proxy and leaves this one in, where it was left out for an hour (or a host's blacklist_ttl). A block no longer uses up one of the request's attempts, and the next proxy is tried without a backoff wait; the pool bounds the blocks. linecaster pins resilient-httpx 1.7.0 (storytracer's fork, bc9de0a: blocks_count_as_attempts, block_exceptions, blacklist_on_exception).
  • --on ray: a pipeline without engines (pipelines/harvest.py) runs on datatrove's RayPipelineExecutor, so on CPU-only Ray workers (--cpus-per-task, --mem-per-cpu-gb); every single-stage pipeline asked for a GPU per task.
  • A Ray run stops as a local one does (linecaster.runtime.ray.RayExecutor, also under RayGPUExecutor): an error that is not the pages' (a host's stop_on, a server, the configuration) in one task writes a stop marker to the logging folder (stopped.json), every later task ends before its pipeline starts, and the launch fails with that error. datatrove only ended the task and started the next, whose first request went straight into the block (a JSON API run sent about 990 requests into a host's 429 block that way). A launch with unfinished tasks fails too, where the Ray job ended as succeeded with "Only 8/1000 tasks completed".
  • --address joins the Ray cluster it names (linecaster.runtime.run.connect_ray: auto, HOST:6379, ray://HOST:10001); it was read but not used, so a run only found a cluster started on its own machine.
  • A task that fails no longer stops a local run with several workers (datatrove's pool stopped at the first exception, and the launch then hung): it is logged, the others go on, it runs again on the next launch, and the summary counts the unfinished tasks. Configuration, catalog and server errors, and 20 failed tasks in a row in one worker, still stop the run. kill -USR1 <pid> writes every thread's stack to the terminal.
  • --retry-failed (local): finished tasks that left rejects run again; with harvest.py their images that are there are read back and only the failed pages fetched, and the task's rejects file is written anew.
  • A proxy answered with a 429 or 503 whose Retry-After is shorter than the blacklist TTL (3600 s) is left out only that long (resilient-httpx's blacklist_ttl_from_retry_after, from storytracer's fork, pinned at 238582e as resilient-httpx 1.4.0); everything else keeps 3600 s.
  • pipelines/harvest.py runs one item per task (task_per_item of ImageParquetReader and ManifestReader): every item whole in its task, a task that fails costs one item. Items are grouped by their --item-key value, so a table whose item rows are apart still gives one task per item (tables.item_runs). Other pipelines keep their task sizes. A harvest run folder started with the 1,000-page tasks has another task count: run into a new folder.
  • A resumed harvest does not fetch images again that an earlier launch wrote: ImageParquetReader and ManifestReader take reuse_folder (harvest.py: OUT/images), list an item's folder once when they reach it (linecaster.blocks.readers.existing.ExistingImages; names and sizes) and read a page whose file is there from the storage instead of fetching it from the source. Only pages of items whose task was interrupted are read back (with one item per task, at most one item per worker and restart), so storage egress stays small. Its record is complete (sha256, width, height) and says image.extra.reused; ImageFilesWriter leaves the file as it is; the reader counts it in pages, media_size (the bytes it read) and reused; the console counts it as done, apart from the downloads and their rate. Not with --existing-ocr. ImageFilesWriter writes local files as <name>.part and renames them when whole.
  • The console's size on a restart starts with the finished tasks' images: their readers' media_size from datatrove's stats files (linecaster.runtime.local.size_before), read in batches in the background while the run starts (size … until then).
  • --proxies FILE: http(s) requests through a list of proxies (one per line: a URL, or host:port[:user:pass] as Webshare lists them), with resilient-httpx (the extra resilient-httpx): each attempt through the next proxy, a proxy that fails an attempt left out for an hour (PROXY_BLACKLIST_THRESHOLD 1, PROXY_BLACKLIST_TTL 3600 s), the attempt retried through another. Each proxy's client is pybookget's, so the rate limits (shared by all proxies), the deadline per attempt and the trace records hold as without; retries follow pybookget's counts and waits, without Retry-After. The progress line shows the proxies in rotation; credentials are never logged, and the run record keeps the file's name, not its lines.
  • --user-agent TEXT and --random-user-agent (a random browser User-Agent from pybookget's fake-useragent, a new one for each task, HTTPFetcher.new_user_agent) for every http(s) request. The default User-Agent is datatrove's, HF-Research/1.0 (linecaster.net.http.USER_AGENT), where it was linecaster (+https://github.com/storytracer/linecaster).
  • The console of a local run (linecaster.runtime.console, linecaster.runtime.local.LocalExecutor): one line naming the pipeline, a live progress line for the whole run (pages of the total, rate, size, failed pages, task, time left), a line per finished task and a summary, in human units; a progress log line every 30 s off a terminal. datatrove's pipeline listing (with the builder's boundary steps) and stats blocks go only to the task logs. The completion markers are listed once per launch instead of looked up task by task. With several workers the worker processes report their counts to the console (a multiprocess manager's dict), and every worker's task lines show. On a terminal the progress line is pinned to the top row and everything else scrolls below it (a scroll region, console.Pinned), so log lines and output from worker processes or libraries never break it.
  • ImageParquetReader and ManifestReader pass pages on as their http(s) requests finish, not in row order, so a slow or retried request delays only its own page (prefetched(..., ordered=False)); pages read without a request keep their order. Requests in flight are capped at the rate limits times the deadline per attempt (HTTPFetcher.max_ahead). In a 2,000-page smoke run the oldest request, being retried, held the window full of finished pages for minutes (94 pages/min against 150).
  • Fetch records and traces carry each attempt's outcome (tries, the span attribute http.tries): a status for a response read whole, <status>-cut for one the deadline cut, no-response for a timeout or a connection error.
  • --max-pages N (--parquet, IMAGES; max_pages of ImageParquetReader and ImageFolderReader): the first N pages of the input for the whole run, in the same automatic tasks, so a smoke test is the real setup stopped early (--limit counts per task).

  • A response that trickles no longer holds a task: the deadline per attempt (above) cuts it and fetches it again, usually through another proxy exit. In a smoke run one such response took 150 s while the 199 pages behind it waited; the trace shows a cut attempt as http.attempts 2.

  • Four more page readers, each run on a 60-page sample (NOTES.md): model entries surya-ocr-2.5, indra-ocr, oxr-1.0, falcon-ocr (Falcon OCR pinned at the revision its vendor image ships) and their presets surya-ocr-2.5@1, indra-ocr@1, oxr-1.0@1, falcon-ocr@1 (step recognition, unit page).

  • Page engines: PageRecognizer runs an engine whose unit is the page on the InProcess or Served backend (or a page engine's preset by name), besides a chat VLM on Chat. Engine packages linecaster-indra (indra.recognition.v1: the indra-ocr package on the CPU), linecaster-surya (surya.recognition.v1: the surya-ocr package's full-page path attached to vLLM) and linecaster-services (falcon.recognition.v1, oxr.recognition.v1: clients of Falcon-OCR's and OXR's page pipelines behind their own HTTP APIs).
  • ServiceServer (servers): starts the service a page preset's serve block names, last in the pipeline: vllm serve on the fetched model pin, or a vendor image's entrypoint (serve.server: vendor with command, health, weights_dir, new optional fields of the preset schema), ready once its health URLs answer.
  • pipelines/transcribe_page.py (transcribe_page.v1): a page engine per page, with the service its preset names unless --recognition-endpoint names a running one; launch.py runs a page engine's preset there.
  • linecaster.testing: FakePageEngine (fake.recognition.page.v1) and fake_service(), an HTTP service on loopback answering given routes. tests/test_page_engines_catalog.py checks the page engines in the environment of pipelines/transcribe_page.py.
  • Versioned docs: the docs workflow publishes the site with mike to the gh-pages branch, served by GitHub Pages: every release tag as version <major>.<minor> (latest the newest release, the default); mike joins the dependency group docs.
  • pytest-xdist joins the dependency group dev: uv run pytest -n auto runs the tests on every core, as CI does; a plain uv run pytest stays serial. CI keeps uv's cache between runs.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• The engine packages (linecaster-kraken, -paddlex, -tesseract, -surya, -indra, -services) 0.1.1 accept linecaster >=0.1,<0.3; the engine API only gained the optional image_input.
  • The docs site publishes releases only; the reference for main is built in a checkout (linecaster docs, then mkdocs serve).

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• The run's description of its HTTP policy includes the run's own --rate-limit, --proxies and --random-user-agent, which hold between the file's root and its hosts' entries; before, a file without rate limits read "no rate limit" although the options' limits applied.
  • A blocked or broken proxy is marked in the broker and logged once per block: the requests already on their way through it come back blocked too and go on through another proxy without a mark, a message or a failure of their own (before, each rewrote the mark and logged the block again).
  • ServiceServer notices a service that exits while it boots at once, instead of at its next look at the health URLs (every 2 s).
  • A resumed harvest's listing of an item's folder in OUT/images (the images already written, to reuse) could hang forever on object storage, and with it the worker: with 250 workers writing to S3-compatible storage only 28 got to fetch. The readers now wait at most linecaster.blocks.readers.existing.LISTING_TIMEOUT (60 s) for it (fsspec is given the timeout too, so it cancels the listing on its IO loop); one that times out or fails is a WARNING (listing <folder> for files to reuse took over 60 s; its pages are fetched again) and a stat (reuse_listing_timeouts, reuse_listing_errors), and the item's pages are fetched again (their files are overwritten, which is safe).
  • A page could fail with HTTP 520 during an outage the breaker had seen: when the request's last server error opened the breaker and another request's probe was answered (closing it) before that error got back to the fetch, the fetch found the breaker closed and gave up. It now tries again whenever the breaker opened during its attempts (Breaker.openings).
  • The rate limits started afresh with every task (each made its own fetcher), so a worker's next task could send a whole window's requests at once; and ImageParquetReader never closed its fetcher, leaving a thread per task. The readers share one fetcher per process and configuration (HTTPFetcher.shared).
  • ImageParquetReader: an image that cannot be read (an http(s) error after the retries, a missing file, bytes that are not an image) no longer fails the task. The page comes without image and with the error in doc.metadata["errors"] (field image, raw_value its URI), so the page records and rejects keep it and a rerun of the task does not fail on the same dead link again; the reader has an error budget (max_page_errors, set by --max-page-errors), so a server that is down still fails the task. ImageFilesWriter passes a page that carries errors and no image through without writing a file. A row with neither image bytes nor a path still fails the task.

docs.title: Upgrade notes
docs.text:
The first release, after the refactoring of November 2026 in six phases; each phase's renames are listed here, and all of them in one table at the end of these notes. There are no compatibility aliases: old imports, flags and ids fail.

Phase 1: layout and names

  • Packages: linecaster.transcription, linecaster.page → linecaster.data (data model) and linecaster.formats (ALTO, PAGE, hOCR; formats.docling was linecaster.document); text.py, unicode.py, reflow.py, retyper.py → linecaster.text.variants, .unicode, .recomposition, .typography; images.py, plots.py → linecaster.images; run, jobs, ray_executor, provenance → linecaster.runtime.* (run.rows() → run.pages()); linecaster.models → linecaster.adapters; blocks/http.py → linecaster.net; blocks by family under linecaster.blocks.<family> (old modules filters, media, models, serve, texts, document, readers, writers are gone); specs/ → docs/reference/.
  • Blocks: PageStep → PageBlock, ModelStep → ModelBlock, WorkingImages → ImageConverter, AttachImage → ImageFetcher, LayoutStep → LayoutDetector, LinesStep → LineDetector, AssignLinesToRegions → LineAssigner, RecognitionStep → LineRecognizer, ChatRegionStep → RegionRecognizer, ChatPageStep → PageRecognizer, TablesStep → TableRecognizer, FormulasStep → FormulaRecognizer, NormalizeUnicode → UnicodeNormalizer, Typography → Typographer, ComposePage → Composer, ValidatePages → PageValidator, RejectSink → RejectWriter, RecipeStamp → RecipeStamper, ServeModels → ModelServer, ServeChatModel → ChatModelServer, PageRowReader → PageRecordReader; writers: PageFilesWriter + PageExportsWriter → PageFileWriter (text_fallback=False is the old PageExportsWriter), ItemExportsWriter → ItemDocumentWriter, ItemTextJsonlWriter + ItemTextFilesWriter → ItemTextWriter(format=...). Datatrove display names changed with them (stats and logs).
  • Engines: …Model → …Engine (KrakenRecognitionEngine, PaddleLayoutEngine, ...); ids unchanged. Adapters: ChatModel → ChatAdapter, each VLM adapter X → XAdapter.
  • Pipeline scripts: transcribe_chain.py → transcribe_modular.py; ids chain.v1 → transcribe_modular.v1, vlm.v1 → transcribe_vlm.v1, new harvest.v1, bind.v1.
  • Flags: --recognizer → --recognition; --vlm, --vlm-endpoint → --recognition, --recognition-endpoint; --texts → --item-texts; --exports DIR → --files DIR --formats md,txt,json --naming flat --suffix .paddle --furniture (in today's terms); --rows → --pages.
  • Stored output: the default transcription ocr → ocr_new; page records in OUT/rows/ → OUT/pages/; item text fidelity normalised → normalized; typography measurement levelled → leveled. Page records written before phase 1 keep ocr; read them with transcription="ocr".
  • Catalog: no step page (page presets are step recognition, unit page, under presets/recognition/); entries are <id>.yaml with prose in <id>.md; YAML is read as YAML 1.2 with ruamel.yaml (replaces PyYAML); lock format linecaster.lock/2. Edition numbers are unchanged; 20 hashes were recomputed (the page presets and squiddle@1), so files stamped by a recipe carry the new hash; old hashes still resolve (previous_sha256).
  • American spelling throughout (e.g. normalize, NORMALIZE_MAP, quantize_confidence, COLORS).

Phase 2: contracts and the builder

  • Pipeline scripts check their pipeline before they launch: a pipeline whose contracts do not fit exits with code 2 and lists every problem. Own blocks without a contract() pass unchecked.
  • With --tasks over 1, a binder after the page blocks (--item-texts) cuts the run into two stages: page records in item shards (OUT/pages/<shard>/), then the item stage; their logs are OUT/logs/pages/ and OUT/logs/items/. One stage logs to OUT/logs/ as before.
  • --dry-run prints the plan under plan and the Mermaid graph after the JSON.
  • A page an in-process block fails on no longer fails the task: it carries the error (doc.metadata["errors"]: block, step, preset, type, error; served failures in the same shape, no longer {step, error}), later model blocks pass it on at once, and it is written to OUT/rejects/<rank>.jsonl and kept in the page records. More failures than --max-page-errors (1 % of a task's pages, counting at least 100) fail the task.
  • ImageConverter(output_folder, rejects_folder, ...) → ImageConverter(output_folder, ...) and PageValidator(rejects_folder, required, prefix) → PageValidator(required): they record why on the page and pass it on (no longer dropped); the RejectWriter (now a writer block, RejectWriter(output_folder, prefix=""), which the builder puts before the first writer of a run) writes the rejects. A derivative that used either adds a RejectWriter where it wants the file, or lets the builder add one.
  • Library code raises linecaster.errors (PipelineConfigError, CatalogError, PageError, ServerError) instead of SystemExit, ValueError, KeyError, RuntimeError and TypeError for configuration, catalog, page and server errors (e.g. an unknown preset is a CatalogError, an unknown block option a PipelineConfigError); pipeline scripts raise PipelineConfigError from pipeline().
  • runtime.jobs.dependencies(commit) without a script raises; give the pipeline's script, runtime.jobs.ENGINE_SCRIPT (the modular pipeline's engines) or engines=False (linecaster alone).
  • The run record's schema is linecaster.run-record/1 (was linecaster.run/1): pipeline lists the stages with every block's to_dict() and contract (was a list of block entries; the separate stages is gone), and pipeline_sha256 is new. A run into an OUT whose record has another pipeline_sha256 (or none: a record from before) is refused unless --new-pipeline; another --tasks always is.
  • Page records carry schema: linecaster.page/1 in their row. Records without one (written before phase 1) are read with ocr as ocr_new, and a pages/ folder without records is read from its sibling rows/: no transcription="ocr" needed any more.
  • Engines load in warm_up() before the first page, not on it: a page's measured seconds no longer include loading; the load time is the block's warm_up_seconds stat. ModelServer and ChatModelServer start their servers in warm_up() (stat warm_up_seconds, was the boot time stat).
  • engine_spec(ref) and preset_models(models) take installed=True; tests that replace engine_spec accept it.
  • On HF Jobs the tasks log JSON lines (LINECASTER_LOG_JSON=1, runtime.jobs.JobsExecutor; the run record's executor is JobsExecutor).
  • Every run is traced (OpenTelemetry, a new required dependency: opentelemetry-api, -sdk, -exporter-otlp-proto-http): OUT/traces/ appears in every run folder, and a sampled page's record carries metadata.trace_id. Every stage with a run folder now has observers, so its pipeline has boundary steps.
  • Observers: on_task_end(error=None) (was on_task_end(); an own observer adds the parameter), and new hooks on_task_event, on_leave, environment(). Stream blocks notify request (with a carrier) after prepare, and done with tokens and finish_reason; PageRecognizer notifies prepare once (was twice).

Phase 3: rule-based steps, recomposition, binding

  • Text without geometry (lines without boxes, e.g. a delivered plain text): a paragraph now continues across a page break only after a division mark; before, the simple line flow joined such pages whenever the text did not end a sentence.
  • linecaster.blocks.writers.item_texts(doc, variants, transcription, token_counter) renders an item record's text variants as datatrove documents, for derivatives writing them in a format of their own; ItemTextWriter uses it.
  • linecaster.catalog.schema.RULE_STEPS lists the rule-based steps, to tell a recipe's rule-based slots from its model slots.
  • Data model: ModelInfo → StepInfo (new field engine, the engine's code id, filled by the model blocks, linecaster serve and the chat adapters), Transcription.model → Transcription.steps, ChatAdapter.model_info() → step_info(). New: Transcription.paragraphs (Paragraph, ParagraphRow, ParagraphRef, Decision), Line.normalized, and the measurements vocabulary linecaster.data.MEASUREMENTS (the keys a step writes; an engine package in this repository adds a new key there first, a test checks it).
  • Page records are linecaster.page/2 (steps instead of model, paragraphs, normalized). PageRecordReader reads linecaster.page/1 records and those from before phase 1 as /2; code that reads the JSON itself reads steps.
  • The page files' step records (ALTO processingStepSettings, PAGE Labels, hOCR linecaster-step-<n>, METS agents) carry engine for steps an engine ran.
  • Catalog: the steps image, normalization, typography, recomposition, composition with built-in engines in linecaster.engines, in-process only (linecaster serve refuses them); presets may name by_script strategies; capabilities.unit may be item and produces names parts (PARTS). preset-1.json gains them; no released hash changes. engine_spec(ref, installed=True, served=False) and preset_models(models, installed=True, served=False): tests that replace engine_spec accept served.
  • regex is a new core dependency (Unicode scripts).
  • The rule-based blocks take a preset or an engine spec, with options over it: Typographer() → Typographer("ratios@1"); Composer(text="reflow", sections=..., rtl=...) → Recomposer("unicode-recomposition@1", options={"rtl": ...}) + Composer("docling-composition@1", options={"sections": ...}), and text="lines" is a Composer without a Recomposer before it (the document is composed from paragraphs when there are, else from lines); ImageConverter(output_folder, effort=80) → ImageConverter(output_folder, "working-image@1", options={"effort": 80}). New blocks Recomposer (composition, unit="page"|"item") and CharacterNormalizer (text); Composer also takes unit="item".
  • DocumentBuilder(name, text=..., sections=..., rtl=..., stats=...) → DocumentBuilder(name, sections=...): it no longer recomposes, it composes a page's paragraphs when it has them (add_page(..., page_id=...) names the page for paragraphs continued across pages); build_docling(...) loses text, rtl and stats; formats.docling.TEXT_MODES is gone. In linecaster.text.recomposition, join_paragraphs → join (the joined text, the separator and the decision on the division mark), new break_reason, kept_reason, mark_decision, Thresholds (the geometric thresholds and the convention marks, parameters of reflow_rows, Margins.of, continues, ...); Row.bbox may be None (text only). text.typography.retype takes ratios (Ratios) and records no step (the engine does); typography.SETTINGS is gone.
  • Page records and page files: with a recomposition (--recomposition, the squiddle recipe) the transcription carries its paragraphs (with their decisions); the typography step is recorded by its engine (name and engine typography.ratios.v1, preset ratios@1 and its hash, every option as settings, seconds and datetime), and the recomposition and composition steps have step records of their own. The documents and their exports are unchanged.
  • Binding: BindItem and ItemTexts are removed. BindItem(text="reflow", sections=S) → Binder() + Recomposer("unicode-recomposition@1", unit="item") + Composer("docling-composition@1", unit="item", options={"sections": S}) (text="lines": without the Recomposer); the item documents are the same, the item document's metadata is the item record plus docling, region_of, item_id (no page_ids, pages, text_mode, sections). ItemTexts(variants=V, token_counter=F) → Binder() + Recomposer(..., unit="item") + CharacterNormalizer("latin-historic@1", unit="item") + ItemTextWriter(DIR, variants=V, token_counter=F): the writer renders the variants from the item record (one row per item and variant, the same columns). ItemDocumentWriter gains by_format (<format>/<item>.<ext>).
  • The readable variants (readable_txt, readable_md) are made from the item's recomposition and normalization (Paragraph.normalized) instead of text.variants' own line flow, so they change (paragraph breaks, kept hyphens; NOTES.md has the comparison). linecaster.text.variants: join_lines, page_blocks, item_blocks, continues, HYPHENS and SENTENCE_END are gone; variants(pages, page_ids=None) needs recomposed, normalized pages; body_blocks and Block.normalized are new. The normalization engines also set each table cell's normalized.
  • pipelines/transcribe_modular.py: --text lines|reflow → the slots --typography, --recomposition, --normalization and --composition (presets; an empty slot leaves the step out: --text lines is no --recomposition). Without a recipe the rule-based steps run only when picked (before: typography and composition always). --item-texts needs --recomposition and --normalization (the recipe squiddle has them). --set takes the rule-based steps too (--set composition.sections=true).
  • pipelines/bind.py (bind.v1, now with recipes): Binder → item recomposition → normalization → item composition, texts in OUT/texts/<variant>/ (JSONL; --files also one file per item there, was OUT/files/<variant>/) and item documents in OUT/documents/<format>/; slots --recomposition, --normalization, --composition (the new recipe item-texts@1 fills them), --variants, --formats, --furniture, --dividers, --no-texts, --no-documents, --set.
  • squiddle@1 names the rule-based presets (ratios@1, unicode-recomposition@1, latin-historic@1, docling-composition@1) instead of the option text: reflow: a catalog migration, so its hash changed (files stamped by it carry the new one) and the lock's previous_sha256 lists both earlier hashes (previous_sha256 may now be a list, oldest first; Resolved.previous_sha256 is a tuple).
  • The builder carries the parts across a binder and a splitter (an item record holds its pages), apart from image and the item's document; the role splitter is new. Recomposer's contract replaces paragraphs too (it makes them anew). RecipeStamper has unit any (it stamps the pages of item records).

Phase 4: backends and families

  • VLMs are the Chat backend (linecaster.backends.Chat(preset, endpoint=None, served_name=None, max_window=32, initial_window=4, read_timeout=600.0, api_key=None, headers=None, prefer="page")): PageRecognizer(spec, Served(endpoint, model=name, max_window=W, ...)) → PageRecognizer(Chat(spec, endpoint, served_name=name, max_window=W, ...)), the same for RegionRecognizer(spec, backend, labels=..., pad=...) → RegionRecognizer(Chat(...), labels=..., pad=...); either also takes a chat preset's ref (PageRecognizer( "dots-ocr"): on the task's ChatModelServer, port 8000). The adapter is block.adapter (was block.spec), the served name Chat.served_name (was the Served backend's model). Without an endpoint Chat asks http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1. The page records are unchanged.
  • The run record: a chat block's parameters are backend ({"backend": "chat", "adapter", "preset", "preset_sha256", "model", "revision", "served_name", "endpoint", ...}) instead of spec and a served backend; pipeline_sha256 covers the adapter, preset edition and hash, model and revision (no longer the served name), so a run of transcribe_vlm.py into an OUT of before is refused unless --new-pipeline.
  • ModelBlock streams for every served block, and a block names its requests with _rows, _unit, _request, _parse and _done (an own served block that overrode _run_served or RegionRecognizer._run_regions uses them). Model blocks also take a preset ref as their backend (LayoutDetector("pp-doclayoutv3@1"): in-process).
  • SingleRegionLayout is removed: SingleRegionLayout() → LayoutDetector("single-region@1") (the built-in engine layout.single-region.v1; label and region_id are its options). The region is the same; the page now records a layout step for it (engine, preset, settings, seconds, datetime), which page files list too, and the block reads the page image instead of the record's size. ModularTranscriber(lines, recognition) needs its layout: ModularTranscriber(lines, recognition, "single-region@1").
  • pipelines/transcribe_modular.py needs --layout like --lines and --recognition: a run without one is --layout single-region. Presets of built-in engines stay in-process with --backend served (runtime.run.engines), and the pipelines' serve leaves them out.
  • ManifestReader(existing_ocr=True) only fetches the library's OCR, as a document media with metadata["format"] (alto, hocr); its contract adds transcription_file (a new page-level part) instead of ocr_original:*. The TranscriptionConverter reads it into ocr_original: the builder puts one right after such a reader when no block reads the file, and pipelines/harvest.py has its own, so OUT/ocr/ and the page records are as before. Its hash changes (a new block), so a harvest into an OUT of before needs --new-pipeline. A file that cannot be read is now the page's error (it goes to rejects/; before, the page went on without it and ocr_failed counted it); a failed download is still counted as ocr_failed. hOCR files that state another image size are scaled to the page image (before: read as they were).
  • PARTS gains transcription_file (no released hash changes).
  • A new extra, [pypdfium2], for the PdfReader; the locks list it.

Phase 5: docs

  • linecaster catalog docs [--out docs/catalog] [--readme README.md] → linecaster docs [--out docs] [--readme README.md] [--check]: --out is now the docs folder (the catalog's pages go to <out>/catalog/). It also writes the block pages, the README's block table (between <!-- blocks:start --> / <!-- blocks:end -->), the site's docs/index.md and docs/changelog.md, and docs/llms.txt / docs/llms-full.txt; --check writes nothing and exits with 1, naming each file that differs. linecaster catalog no longer has the action docs.
  • Generated pages start with a comment saying so; their links to files outside docs/ (sources, pipeline scripts, model cards) go to GitHub. The evidence tables have two more columns, Hardware and Backend.

Phase 6: tests and engine hygiene

ImageConverter without keep_bytes removes image: a pipeline in which a later block reads the image (without an ImageFetcher in between) no longer passes the builder's check; it failed on its first page before.
  • RegionRecognizer(pad=None): an explicit pad wins over the adapter's region_pad, which is the default (else 8). Callers that passed pad with a preset that has a region_pad (minicpm-ocr-1.0: 0, lightonocr-2-1b-regions: 8) now get their pad. The run record names pad: null when none is given, so pipeline_sha256 of a pipeline with a RegionRecognizer changes (no released recipe has one): resuming into an older run folder needs --new-pipeline.
  • Engine packages are version 0.1.0 and depend on linecaster>=0.0.1,<0.2; they import from linecaster only linecaster.data and linecaster.engines.api. A derivative's own engine package should do the same.
  • Tests: pytest runs with --strict-markers; tests/conftest.py's make_transcription is linecaster.testing.sample_transcription.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• PageRecordReader(fetch_images=True), ImageFetcher and ImageConverter dropped the fragment of page.image.uri and fetched the whole file: for a PdfReader page (file.pdf#page=n) the PDF, for an ImageParquetReader row with embedded bytes the Parquet file. A PDF page is now rendered as PdfReader renders it (at the record's metadata["pdf"]["dpi"]), a Parquet row's image read (columns id and image), and any other fragment is the page's error (field image), never the wrong bytes (linecaster.blocks.readers.fragments).
  • ImageConverter without keep_bytes declared only metadata replaced although the page leaves without its image bytes: its contract now removes image, so the builder no longer treats the image as available after it.
  • ImageFilesWriter rewrites page.image.uri and extra (to name the copy) without declaring it: its contract now replaces metadata.
  • RegionRecognizer replaces the transcription's earlier lines but declared lines only as added: its contract now replaces lines and text, so it may follow a line step.
  • RegionRecognizer ignored an explicit pad when the adapter has a region_pad.
  • RegionRecognizer failed the task on a page without image bytes; the page now carries the error (found by check_block).

  • PageValidator(required=("image",)) declared that it reads the image bytes, although it checks the page record's image entry: a page field is now read as metadata, so the validator may follow an ImageConverter that removes the bytes.

  • PageParquetWriter writes a fixed schema: datatrove took a file's columns from its first row, so a page's errors were dropped when the first page of a file had none. Page records in Parquet now always have an errors column (null without errors).

  • Tracing holds no page documents: a page a block drops no longer stays in memory, with its image, until the task ends; its trace ends when the next page enters that block.
  • A sampled page's metadata.trace_id is derived from the run and the page id, so a rerun of a run writes the same page records.
  • runtime.jobs.dependencies() reads the pipeline script and its lock as they are at the commit the Jobs install, not as the checkout holds them (with a warning when the commit is not in the checkout).

docs.title: Blocks
docs.text: Every public block, by family: one page each with its contract, backends, options, behavior and where it comes in a pipeline. Terms are the glossary's; contracts and the builder are in pipelines.

docs.title: Readers
docs.text:
linecaster.blocks.readers

Block What it does ImageFolderReader Reads one page per image file of a folder or bucket. ImageParquetReader Reads one page per row of Parquet files with an image column. ManifestReader Reads one page per image of each item's manifest: IIIF Presentation 2 or 3, or METS with MODS (also inside an OAI-PMH response). PageRecordReader Reads the page records an earlier run wrote (JSON Lines or Parquet), so a pipeline can add one more part. PdfReader Reads one item per PDF file, one page per PDF page in order, each rendered to a lossless WebP image. ResourceReader Fetches the remote files of items as they are served, one document per resource, one item per task.

docs.text:
linecaster.blocks.layout

docs.title: Lines
docs.text:
linecaster.blocks.lines

docs.title: Recognition
docs.text:
linecaster.blocks.recognition

Block What it does FormulaRecognizer Recognizes every formula region as LaTeX by a formula engine. LineRecognizer Recognizes the text of every line by a line recognition engine. PageRecognizer Recognizes every page with a chat VLM or a page engine, whose output becomes the page's transcription. RegionRecognizer Recognizes each layout region of every page with a chat VLM, one request per region crop. TableRecognizer Recognizes the structure of every table region by a table engine.

docs.text:

ImageFetcher Loads each page's image again from its address, for the blocks that need pixels. docs.title: Binding
docs.text:
linecaster.blocks.binding
