docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
linecaster.blocks.validation

Block What it does PageValidator Marks the page records that do not validate against Page or lack a required part with an error each. RecipeStamper Stamps the recipe edition a run follows on every step of every transcription, of a page or of each page of an item record.

docs.title: Servers
docs.text:
linecaster.blocks.servers

Block What it does ChatModelServer Starts a chat VLM server (vLLM or SGLang) inside the task for its Chat backends, through saturate's Engine. ModelServer Starts linecaster serve inside the task for its served model blocks, through saturate's Engine. ServiceServer Starts the service a page engine's preset names inside the task, and stops it when the task's pages are through.

docs.title: Writers
docs.text:
linecaster.blocks.writers

Block What it does ImageFilesWriter Writes each page's image bytes as they came, one file per page. ItemDocumentWriter Writes the document of each item record, one file per format: Markdown, text, HTML, DocLang, JSON. ItemTextWriter Writes the text variants of each item record as JSON Lines or as files. PageFileWriter Writes one file per page and format: ALTO, PAGE-XML, hOCR, text, Markdown, HTML, DocLang, JSON and more. PageJsonlWriter Writes the page records as JSON Lines, one file per task, or into item shards for a later stage. PageParquetWriter Writes the page records as Parquet, one file per task. RejectWriter Writes every page that carries errors to the task's rejects file and passes every page on. ResourceFilesWriter Writes each resource's bytes as they came, one file per resource. ResourceRecordWriter Writes each resource's record (doc.metadata["resource"], with its errors) as a JSON line, to <output_folder>/<rank>.jsonl.gz: one file per task, a failed resource included (error, errors).

docs.text:
linecaster.blocks.composites

Block What it does ModularTranscriber Reads a page's lines the modular way: layout, lines on the whole page, line assignment, line recognition.

docs.title: Base classes
docs.text:
linecaster.blocks.base: what the blocks above are built on; no pages of their own.

Class What it is for Composite Groups blocks under one name with an outward contract of its own. Contracted Gives a block the default contract(), read from its class attributes. ModelBlock Runs one model step's engine on every page, through its backend, and adds its part to the transcription. PageBlock Processes a stream of pages, one datatrove document per page, as the base of the page blocks. RuleBlock Runs a rule-based step's built-in engine on every page, in the pipeline's process, as the base of the rule blocks.

docs.title: Binder
docs.text:
Block · binding · linecaster.blocks.binding

Binds each item's page records, in order, into one item record.

Unit page → item Role binder Reads - Adds - Replaces - Comes after - Comes before - Used in bind.v1, transcribe_modular.v1 Source binder.py

The comes-after and comes-before rows are derived from every block's contract.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Type Default Description count_key str 'item_page_count' the page metadata key that holds the item's page count; a page without it waits for the end of the input.

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
The item record is one datatrove document (doc.id the item id, doc.metadata["item"], linecaster.blocks.base.item) holding its pages in order (Page.sequence, then page id); a page without an item is an item of its own. The item-unit blocks after it (Recomposer, CharacterNormalizer and Composer with unit="item") and the item writers read it; the Splitter turns it back into pages. It changes the stream's unit from pages to items and touches no part: the item record holds its pages as they came, every transcription with every part (the builder's checks carry them past the binder), but not the page images' bytes.

A task must see whole items: linecaster's run layout buckets page records by item (one item in one file), and the pages of an item must arrive in one task (with several tasks the builder cuts the pipeline here: the page records in item shards, then a stage over whole shards). An item is emitted once all its pages have arrived (when its pages' metadata give the count) or when the input ends (stat incomplete_items: items the input ended in before their count).

flowchart LR

docs.title: Splitter
docs.text:
Block · binding · linecaster.blocks.binding

Splits each item record into its page records again, in the item's order, with what the item-level blocks added.

Unit item → page Role splitter Reads - Adds - Replaces - Comes after - Comes before - Used in - Source splitter.py

The comes-after and comes-before rows are derived from every block's contract.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Type Default Description primary str 'ocr_new' the transcription whose text becomes each page document's text.

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text: Each page is a page document again (doc.id the page id, doc.metadata["page"], doc.text the text of primary) carrying what the item-level blocks added to it: the paragraphs of an item-level Recomposer (continued across pages, the references naming the other page), the normalized texts, the step records. It changes the stream's unit from items to pages. The item's own parts (its document) stay with the item; the pages carry no image bytes (PageRecordReader fetches them again by URI). A stream entry that is no item record is counted (no_item) and not passed on.

docs.title: Composer
docs.text:
Block · composition · linecaster.blocks.composition

Composes the DoclingDocument of a page or an item by a composition engine.

Unit page Role transform Reads ocr_new:lines, ocr_new:regions Adds ocr_new:document Replaces - Backends in-process only (a built-in engine) Catalog step composition Presets docling-composition@1 Comes after LayoutDetector, LineDetector, RegionRecognizer, ModularTranscriber Comes before ItemDocumentWriter Used in bind.v1, transcribe_modular.v1 Source composer.py

The contract is that of Composer(preset='docling-composition@1'); the comes-after and comes-before rows are derived from every block's contract.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Type Default Description preset required the composition engine: a preset (e.g. docling-composition@1) or an InProcess engine spec. transcription str 'ocr_new' the transcription to compose. unit str 'page' page (a document per page) or item (a document per item record, after a Binder). options dict[str, Any] \| None None engine options over the preset's, e.g. {"sections": True}; None: the preset's.

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
Text regions are composed from their paragraphs when a Recomposer made them, else from their lines as laid out (a diplomatic document). Reads regions and lines (and the paragraphs when there are); adds document; stat documents (pages) or items.

unit="page": one document per page, named after the page id, in the transcription's docling; the map from each Docling item to its layout region ("<page_no>:<region id>") in transcription.extra["docling_region_of"], for the Markdown dividers of the page writers. unit="item": one document per item record (linecaster.blocks.base.item), page n its n-th page, paragraphs continued across pages (an item-level Recomposer before it): doc.metadata["docling"], ["region_of"] and ["item_id"], doc.text its plain text (with furniture), as ItemDocumentWriter writes them. Each page's transcription records the step.

Assigns the lines detected on the whole page to the layout regions and orders them row by row.

docs.text:
Each line goes to the region it overlaps most; lines outside every region (a page number the layout model missed, marginalia) become their own text regions (orphan_<n>), one per visual row, slotted into the reading order; duplicates are dropped. Afterwards the list order of lines is the order a recognizer follows (regions in the layout step's order, orphan rows last, rows within each region), reading_order is the reading rank (regions by reading order, then rows), and line ids are <region id>_l<n>.

Reads lines and regions; adds line_regions; replaces regions (the orphan regions), reading_order and lines (ids and order). Lines inside skipped regions are dropped (stat lines_in_skipped_regions); stat orphan_rows counts the rows that became regions.

Block · readers · linecaster.blocks.readers

Reads one page per row of Parquet files with an image column.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Type Default Description data_folder DataFolderLike required the folder (local path, fsspec URI or DataFolder) of the Parquet files. paths_file DataFileLike \| None None datatrove's ParquetReader arguments. glob_pattern str \| None '**/*.parquet' datatrove's ParquetReader arguments. recursive bool True datatrove's ParquetReader arguments. limit int -1 pages per task, as datatrove's count documents; they apply before anything is read or fetched. skip int 0 pages per task, as datatrove's count documents; they apply before anything is read or fetched. batch_size int 64 the rows read at once from a file. id_key str 'id' the column with the page id. A table without it names its pages <item>_<0001> from item_key and sequence_key, which it then needs. image_key str 'image' the column with the image. item_key str \| None None the column with the page's item_id; default: pages without item. sequence_key str \| None None the column with the page's position in its item (Page.sequence). image_folder DataFolderLike \| None None the folder relative image paths are read from; default data_folder. read_metadata bool False the other columns go into the page's metadata; without it only the named columns are read. file_progress bool False datatrove's ParquetReader arguments. doc_progress bool False datatrove's ParquetReader arguments. default_metadata dict \| None None goes into every page's metadata. shuffle_files bool False read the files of a task's shard in random order. http dict \| None None linecaster.net.http.HTTPConfig fields (rate limits, retries) for http(s):// image paths. Their images are requested ahead of the page being given on, as many as keep the rate limits busy (linecaster.net.http.prefetched), and pages go on as their images arrive: a slow request (one being retried) delays only its own page. Rows read without a request (bytes, files) keep their order. max_pages int \| None None only the first max_pages rows of the input, for the whole run: the tables are read as if they ended there, divided over the tasks (and auto_tasks counted) the same way; default: every row. task_per_item bool False the tasks divide the items (the item_key values, needs it; an item's rows need not be together), not the rows, and auto_tasks is one task per item: each item whole in its task, a task that fails costs one item (pipelines/harvest.py). Default: rows in equal shards. reuse_folder DataFolderLike \| None None where ImageFilesWriter writes the images (pipelines/harvest.py: OUT/images): a page whose file is already there is read from it instead of from the source (linecaster.blocks.readers.existing: one listing per item), so a resumed harvest does not fetch it again; its record is complete and says image.extra["reused"]. A copy that cannot be read is fetched from the source. An item's listing that takes over LISTING_TIMEOUT (60 s) or fails is a warning and a stat (reuse_listing_timeouts, reuse_listing_errors), and its pages are fetched again. Default: none. http_policy str \| None None an HTTP policy file (linecaster.net.policy): settings for every host of the image URLs under http's, a host's own over both.

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
The rows of all files, in order, are divided over the tasks in equal shards, read by row group (linecaster.blocks.readers.tables), so any table works with any number of tasks; an item's pages can land in two tasks where a shard ends. auto_tasks is the task count for shards of about PAGES_PER_TASK pages, which linecaster.runtime.run uses for a pipeline without engines. Each row adds image and metadata (the page record). The image column holds the image as Hugging Face's Image feature stores it ({"bytes", "path"}: the bytes when present, else the path), as plain bytes, or as a path: absolute (any fsspec URI or an http(s):// URL) or relative to image_folder. A row with neither bytes nor a path fails the task (a PageError: the table is wrong).

An image that cannot be read (an http(s) error after its retries, a missing file, bytes that are not an image) makes a page without image whose doc.metadata["errors"] says why (field image, raw_value the image's URI), so the task goes on: later model blocks pass the page by, ImageFilesWriter writes no file for it, and the page records and rejects keep it. More such pages than max_page_errors (a share of the task's pages, judged from page 100 on, ErrorBudget) fail the task, so a server that is down does not mark every page failed.

docs.text:
Block · readers · linecaster.blocks.readers

Reads one page per image of each item's manifest: IIIF Presentation 2 or 3, or METS with MODS (also inside an OAI-PMH response).

Unit page Role reader Reads - Adds image, metadata Replaces - Comes after - Comes before LayoutDetector, LineDetector, FormulaRecognizer, LineRecognizer, PageRecognizer, RegionRecognizer, TableRecognizer, ImageConverter, ImageFetcher, TranscriptionConverter, ImageFilesWriter, ResourceRecordWriter, ModularTranscriber Used in - Source manifests.py

The comes-after and comes-before rows are derived from every block's contract.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Type Default Description data_folder DataFolderLike '.' the folder (local path, fsspec URI or DataFolder) of the manifests or item tables, and the base of relative links; default the current folder. paths_file DataFileLike \| None None datatrove's BaseDiskReader arguments. glob_pattern str \| None None the entries to read; default **/*.{json,xml} (manifests), **/*.parquet with manifest_key. recursive bool True datatrove's BaseDiskReader arguments. limit int -1 pages per task, as datatrove's count documents; they apply before downloading. skip int 0 pages per task, as datatrove's count documents; they apply before downloading. manifest_key str \| None None the column of an item table that holds each item's manifest link; default: the entries are manifests. item_key str \| None None the column of an item table that holds each item's id; needs manifest_key. Default: the id from the manifest entry. read_metadata bool True an item table's other columns go into the metadata of each of the item's pages. manifest_format str \| None None iiif or mets forces the format; default: told apart by content. item_id_pattern str \| None None a regular expression whose first group, found in the manifest entry, is the item id (instead of the last path segment); an entry it does not match is a PipelineConfigError. existing_ocr bool False also fetch each page's own OCR file (transcription_file). manifest_folder DataFolderLike \| None None where every manifest read is saved as fetched, <item_id>.json / .xml; default: not saved. http dict \| None None linecaster.net.http.HTTPConfig fields and HTTPFetcher settings over linecaster.net.http.HTTP_DEFAULTS (rate_limits of this task, timeout, proxy, iiif_format, iiif_quality, mets_image_groups, ...). file_progress bool False datatrove's BaseDiskReader arguments. doc_progress bool False datatrove's BaseDiskReader arguments. default_metadata dict \| None None goes into every page's metadata. shuffle_files bool False datatrove's BaseDiskReader arguments. task_per_item bool False auto_tasks gives one task per item (pipelines/harvest.py); default about ITEMS_PER_TASK items per task. reuse_folder DataFolderLike \| None None where ImageFilesWriter writes the images (pipelines/harvest.py: OUT/images): a page whose file is already there is read from it instead of from the source (linecaster.blocks.readers.existing); the manifest is still read. An item's listing that takes over LISTING_TIMEOUT (60 s) or fails is a warning and a stat (reuse_listing_timeouts, reuse_listing_errors), and its pages are fetched again. Not with existing_ocr (its OCR files would need fetching anyway). http_policy str \| None None an HTTP policy file (linecaster.net.policy): settings per host, with http between its root and its hosts, for every request (manifests, images, OCR files).

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
Entries:

  • without manifest_key: manifests: the files under data_folder matching glob_pattern, or the lines of paths_file (a manifest URL, or a path relative to data_folder), distributed over tasks in turn ([rank::world_size]) the way datatrove distributes files;
  • with manifest_key: Parquet item tables (the files matching glob_pattern, or a paths_file listing them), one item per row: its manifest link in manifest_key (a URL, an absolute fsspec path, or a path relative to data_folder), its id in item_key (optional), and, with read_metadata, every other column in the metadata of each of its pages. The rows of all tables, not the files, are divided over the tasks in equal shards (linecaster.blocks.readers.tables), so one table works with any number of tasks.

auto_tasks is the task count for about ITEMS_PER_TASK items per task, or one item per task with task_per_item (pipelines/harvest.py), which linecaster.runtime.run uses for a pipeline without engines.

A manifest is one entry, so an item's pages stay in one task (whole_items). An entry that is a IIIF Collection stands for its manifests, each an item named by its own link (a table's item_key does not apply to them); a collection listed in it, or a paged one, raises NotImplementedError (one level).

Each page adds image and metadata; with existing_ocr also transcription_file. Pages: item_id from item_key, else from the manifest entry (manifest_item_id: the last path segment that is not a generic manifest name); sequence the page's 1-based position among the manifest's pages with an image; page_id <item_id>_<sequence:04d>; image.uri the URL the image came from. metadata["manifest"] keeps the format, the manifest's URL, id, label, rights, required statement, identifiers and descriptive metadata, the page's own id and label, and the image request. Images are requested at full size (IIIF through the image service, iiif_format/iiif_quality in http; METS from the first image file group in mets_image_groups), with the fallback URL on 404.

With existing_ocr, a page's own OCR (ALTO or hOCR the manifest links: METS FULLTEXT, IIIF seeAlso / rendering) is fetched too, as a second media of the document (type document, metadata["format"] alto or hocr): a TranscriptionConverter after the reader reads it into the transcription ocr_original (the builder puts one there when the pipeline has none), and ImageFilesWriter(ocr_folder=...) writes the bytes.

A manifest that cannot be read or parsed, an image or OCR file that fails after its retries, or a response that is not an image is logged and counted (manifests_failed, pages_failed, pages_not_images, ocr_failed), and the task goes on.

Pages are requested ahead, across manifests, as many as keep the rate limits busy (linecaster.net.http.prefetched), through one HTTPFetcher.shared per process and host's settings (linecaster.net.policy.Fetchers: http, and with http_policy the policy's for each URL's host, for the manifests, the images and the OCR files alike), so the rate limits hold across the tasks a worker runs one after the other; they go on as their images arrive, so a slow request delays only its own page (an item's pages can leave out of order; sequence keeps their place).

docs.text:

docs.text:
Block · readers · linecaster.blocks.readers

Reads the page records an earlier run wrote (JSON Lines or Parquet), so a pipeline can add one more part.

Unit page Role reader Reads - Adds *, image, metadata Replaces - Comes after - Comes before LayoutDetector, LineDetector, FormulaRecognizer, LineRecognizer, PageRecognizer, RegionRecognizer, TableRecognizer, ImageConverter, ImageFetcher, TranscriptionConverter, ImageFilesWriter, ResourceRecordWriter, ModularTranscriber Used in bind.v1 Source records.py

The contract is that of PageRecordReader(data_folder='out/pages'); the comes-after and comes-before rows are derived from every block's contract.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Type Default Description data_folder DataFolderLike required the folder (local path, fsspec URI or DataFolder) of the page records. glob_pattern str '**/*.jsonl*' the record files to read; default JSON Lines (**/*.jsonl*), **/*.parquet for Parquet. fetch_images bool True read each page's image again (the part image); without it the pages carry no image. uri_map dict[str, str] \| None None image URI prefixes rewritten before reading (e.g. a Hub path to a local copy of the same files). item_shards bool False the records are item shards (<shard>/<rank>...), each read whole by one task. http dict \| None None linecaster.net.http.HTTPConfig fields for http(s):// image URIs. provides None the parts the records carry ("ocr_new:lines", "ocr_original:*", or Parts), for the builder's checks; default: anything (*; reads after this reader are not checked). The builder sets it when it starts a stage from the page records of an earlier one. http_policy str \| None None an HTTP policy file (linecaster.net.policy): settings per host for those URIs, with http between its root and its hosts.

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
Each pipeline of a workflow reads the previous one's pages/ folder (linecaster's page writers) and adds its part. The records bring metadata and, with fetch_images, image: page records never carry the image bytes, so they are read again from page.image.uri through datatrove DataFolders (http(s):// through linecaster.net.http); a URI with a fragment names a part of its file (file.pdf#page=<n>: that page rendered, file.parquet#<page_id>: that row's image, linecaster.blocks.readers.fragments), and one that cannot be resolved is the page's error (field image, stat image_errors), never the whole file. A page's errors come back as doc.metadata["errors"], so later model blocks pass it by.

Rows of an earlier format are read as today's (upgrade, by the row's schema): rows without schema name linecaster's transcription ocr (read as ocr_new), linecaster.page/1 rows a transcription's steps model (read as steps); a folder .../pages that holds no records but has a sibling rows (the folder's earlier name) is read from there.

Files are distributed over tasks in turn. With item_shards the page records were written into item shards (PageJsonlWriter(item_shards=N)): the shard folders are distributed instead, each read whole, so a task sees every page of its items (whole_items). No shard folder is a PipelineConfigError.

Recognizes every page with a chat VLM or a page engine, whose output becomes the page's transcription.

Unit page Role model Reads image Adds ocr_new:markdown, ocr_new:text Replaces - Backends chat (Chat), in-process (InProcess), served (Served), a preset ref (id@edition) builds one Catalog step recognition Presets chandra-ocr-2@1, deepseek-ocr@1, deepseek-ocr-2@1, dots-mocr@1, dots-ocr@1, glm-ocr@1, lightonocr-2-1b@1, lightonocr-3-0.8b@1, lightonocr-3-4b@1, nemotron-3.5-parse@1, olmocr-2-7b-1025-fp8@1, ovisocr2@1, ovisocr3@1, paddleocr-vl-1.6@1, qianfan-ocr@1, qwen3.5-9b@1, smoldocling-256m-preview@1, unlimited-ocr@1, unlimited-ocr-2@1 Comes after ImageFolderReader, ImageParquetReader, ManifestReader, PageRecordReader, PdfReader Comes before CharacterNormalizer, UnicodeNormalizer, PageFileWriter Used in transcribe_page.v1, transcribe_vlm.v1 Source chat.py

The contract is that of PageRecognizer(backend='lightonocr-2-1b@1'); the comes-after and comes-before rows are derived from every block's contract.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Type Default Description backend Chat \| InProcess \| Served \| str required a Chat backend, an InProcess or Served backend of a page engine, or a preset's ref: a chat preset's (or a model's Hugging Face id: its page preset) for Chat on the task's ChatModelServer, a page engine's for its engine in the pipeline's process; a preset of another unit or any other backend is refused (PipelineConfigError). transcription str 'ocr_new' the transcription the completion becomes. primary str \| None None the transcription whose text becomes the datatrove document's text; None: transcription. skip_on_error bool True pass pages that carry errors through unprocessed. prepare_workers int 4 threads that build requests ahead of admission (decode, resize and PNG-encode the image; Pillow releases the GIL). name str \| None None the block's name in stats and logs; None: "page (<model>, served <endpoint>)".

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text: On the Chat backend (served only) a stream transform: one request per page, built by the preset's adapter from the page image, the completion parsed into a text-only transcription that replaces transcription. The completion is kept verbatim (extra["raw"]); its finish_reason and token counts go to extra and the step's measurements, and a completion cut off at max_tokens is counted (stat finish_length). On the InProcess or Served backend it runs a page engine (an engine of the recognition step whose unit is the page: a vendor package, or a client of a vendor's service) as every model block runs its engine: the engine gets the page image and returns the page's transcription. Either way it reads the page image and adds text and what the preset produces (lines, markdown, html, ...); the StepInfo records the preset edition and its hash. A failed request or call is the page's error.

Unit page Role model Reads image, ocr_new:regions Adds ocr_new:html, ocr_new:latex, ocr_new:lines, ocr_new:text Replaces ocr_new:lines, ocr_new:text Backends chat (Chat), a preset ref (id@edition) builds one Catalog step recognition Presets lightonocr-2-1b-regions@1, minicpm-ocr-1.0@1 Comes after ImageFolderReader, ImageParquetReader, ManifestReader, PageRecordReader, PdfReader, LayoutDetector, ModularTranscriber Comes before LineAssigner, LineRecognizer, CharacterNormalizer, UnicodeNormalizer, Composer, Recomposer, Typographer, ItemTextWriter, PageFileWriter Used in transcribe_vlm.v1 Source chat.py

The contract is that of RegionRecognizer(backend='minicpm-ocr-1.0@1'); the comes-after and comes-before rows are derived from every block's contract.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Type Default Description backend Chat \| str required a Chat backend, or a chat preset's ref (a model's Hugging Face id picks its region preset) for one on the task's ChatModelServer; any other backend is refused (PipelineConfigError). transcription str 'ocr_new' the transcription it reads the regions of and adds the lines to. labels frozenset({'caption', 'code', 'footnote', 'list_item', 'page_footer', 'page_header', 'reference', 'section_header', 'table', 'text', 'title'}) the region labels it reads (default: text-like regions and tables, no pictures or formulas). pad int \| None None pixels around each region's box at the page scale; None: the adapter's region_pad, else 8. primary str \| None None the transcription whose text becomes the datatrove document's text; None: transcription. skip_on_error bool True pass pages that carry errors through unprocessed. prepare_workers int 4 threads that build the requests (crops, PNG encoding) ahead of admission.

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text: The same saturate machinery as PageRecognizer, results collected per page; any layout step can come before it. Reads the page image and regions; adds lines, text and what the preset produces, and replaces lines and text (the transcription's earlier lines, with their text, are replaced). Crops are cut at the scale the model expects for a whole page (the adapter's page_longest: the page is scaled so its longest side has that length, and the region is cut from it, pad px around the region's box at that scale), so a small region is not blown up; the adapter decides which regions it reads. Every read region gets one line: the region's box and polygon, the completion as its text (verbatim; extra keeps raw and finish_reason), in reading order; the transcription's earlier lines are replaced. The StepInfo records the preset edition, the settings with pad, page_scale and labels, and the token counts, regions and failed. A page whose regions all failed is the page's error, and so is a page without image bytes (stat errors); a page without readable regions passes through unchanged (stat pages_without_regions).

docs.text:
Block · servers · linecaster.blocks.servers

Starts a chat VLM server (vLLM or SGLang) inside the task for its Chat backends, through saturate's Engine.

Unit any Role server Reads - Adds - Replaces - Comes after - Comes before - Used in transcribe_vlm.v1 Source serve.py

The contract is that of ChatModelServer(spec='lightonocr-2-1b@1'); the comes-after and comes-before rows are derived from every block's contract.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Type Default Description spec required the chat preset's adapter (linecaster.adapters.chat_model) or the preset's ref (id@edition). port int 8000 the port the server listens on; Chat without an endpoint asks on 8000. host str '127.0.0.1' the address the server binds to; default loopback only. gpu_memory_utilization float \| None None the share of GPU memory the server may take (for SGLang --mem-fraction-static); default the preset's flags alone. The deployment's choice. extra_args list[str] \| None None more server flags, after the preset's. vllm str 'vllm' the vLLM command (default vllm on PATH, e.g. from the job image or a uv run --with vllm==... environment). boot_timeout int 1800 seconds the server may take to answer. outside_venv bool False start the server without this interpreter's virtual environment (VIRTUAL_ENV unset, its bin taken off PATH), for a job image whose own Python has the server while the pipeline runs in a uv environment on top (HF Jobs); the server's helpers (ninja, python) then come from the image. python str 'python3' the Python that has SGLang (default python3, looked up on the server's PATH, then in the usual image locations).

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
The command comes from the chat preset's serve block (server, flags, environment, packages), whose server picks it:

  • "vllm": vllm serve <spec.model> --host HOST --port PORT <spec.vllm_args(...)> (behind bash -c when the preset has a setup script);
  • "sglang": PYTHON -m sglang.launch_server --model-path <spec.model> --host HOST --port PORT --enable-metrics <spec.sglang_args(...)> (metrics on: saturate reads SGLang's queue gauges).

The server starts in warm_up() and is ready when it answers a trial chat request (saturate's alive-only gate); it stops when the task's pages are through. Before it starts, the preset's server_packages are installed into the server's Python (uv pip install --python <that Python> ...), and for a preset with revision_flag: false (the server cannot be given --revision and loads the default branch) the block refuses to start unless the default branch's files equal the pinned revision's (check_default_branch); the preset's server_env goes into the server's environment. With OTLP configured, vLLM traces too (tracing_args). A server that does not start fails the task (ServerError).

Its role is server and its unit any: it touches no part. Like ModelServer, it goes last in the pipeline (after the writer): datatrove chains generators, and only the last one lives until every page is written.

docs.text:
Block · servers · linecaster.blocks.servers

Starts the service a page engine's preset names inside the task, and stops it when the task's pages are through.

Unit any Role server Reads - Adds - Replaces - Comes after - Comes before - Used in transcribe_page.v1 Source service.py

The contract is that of ServiceServer(preset='falcon-ocr'); the comes-after and comes-before rows are derived from every block's contract.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Type Default Description preset str required the page preset whose serve block names the service (id or id@edition); a chat preset (ChatModelServer starts its server), or a preset without such a block, is refused (PipelineConfigError). port int 8000 the port vLLM listens on (server: vllm); a vendor's entrypoint uses the image's own ports. host str '127.0.0.1' the address vLLM binds to; default loopback only. vllm str 'vllm' the vLLM command (default vllm on the service's PATH: the job image's). boot_timeout int 1800 seconds the service may take until it is ready.

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
The preset's serve block says what runs:

  • server: vllm (an engine package that attaches to vLLM, e.g. surya-ocr): the model pin is fetched (every pinned file checked) and served from that folder, vllm serve <folder> --host HOST --port PORT <flags> --served-model-name <the model's Hugging Face id>, ready once /health and /v1/models answer 200;
  • server: vendor (a vendor's page pipeline in its own image, e.g. Falcon-OCR, OXR): with weights_dir the model pin is downloaded there first (every pinned file checked); then command, the image's entrypoint, starts the service, ready once every health URL has answered 200, in order.

The service runs in its own process group with the preset's env, without the pipeline's environment (PIPELINE_ENV, and this interpreter's bin off PATH), so the image's own Pythons and servers run as the image has them. A service that exits or is not ready within boot_timeout fails the task (ServerError). Its role is server and its unit any: it touches no part. It goes last in the pipeline (after the writer): datatrove chains generators, and only the last one lives until every page is written. A vendor's entrypoint listens on the ports the image sets (one service per machine).

    B --> a0["any stream"]

docs.text:
Block · writers · linecaster.blocks.writers

Writes each page's image bytes as they came, one file per page.

Unit page Role writer Reads image Adds - Replaces metadata Comes after ImageFolderReader, ImageParquetReader, ManifestReader, PageRecordReader, PdfReader Comes before - Used in harvest.v1 Source images.py

The contract is that of ImageFilesWriter(output_folder='out/images'); the comes-after and comes-before rows are derived from every block's contract.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Type Default Description output_folder DataFolderLike required the folder (local path, fsspec URI or DataFolder) the images go to. ocr_folder DataFolderLike \| None None where a library's own OCR that came with the page (a document media, as ManifestReader's existing_ocr adds it) is written the same way, <ocr_folder>/<item_id>/<page_id>.xml (ALTO) or .html (hOCR), when the page has its ocr_original transcription; that transcription's source.extra["file"] then names the copy. Default: not written.

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text: Files go to <output_folder>/<item_id>/<page_id>.<ext> (any fsspec folder; <page_id>.<ext> for pages without an item), the extension from the image's format. It reads image and replaces metadata: the page's image.uri then names the written file and image.extra["source_uri"] where it came from, so page records written after this block point at the copy (PageRecordReader fetches it from there), and ImageFolderReader(output_folder, item_from_parent=True) reads the folder as it is. Pages pass through; a page that carries errors and no image (e.g. its download failed) passes through unchanged, with no file written; a page read from the file an earlier launch wrote (image.extra["reused"], a reader's reuse_folder) gets its record as written, the file left as it is. A local file appears only once it is whole (written as <name>.part, then renamed), so a reader never takes a half-written file for a done page.

docs.title: PageFileWriter
docs.text:
Block · writers · linecaster.blocks.writers

Writes one file per page and format: ALTO, PAGE-XML, hOCR, text, Markdown, HTML, DocLang, JSON and more.

Unit page Role writer Reads ocr_new:lines, ocr_new:text Adds - Replaces - Comes after LineDetector, LineRecognizer, PageRecognizer, RegionRecognizer, ModularTranscriber Comes before - Used in transcribe_modular.v1 Source files.py

The contract is that of PageFileWriter(output_folder='out/files'); the comes-after and comes-before rows are derived from every block's contract.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Type Default Description output_folder DataFolderLike required the folder (local path, fsspec URI or DataFolder) the files go to. formats tuple[str, ...] ('hocr', 'alto', 'page', 'txt') the formats to write, keys of PAGE_FILE_EXTENSIONS; an unknown one is a PipelineConfigError. transcription str 'ocr_new' the transcription written. suffix str '' added to each file's stem, before the extension (".paddle": <page_id>.paddle.md). furniture bool False keep page headers and footers in md, txt and html. bucket_by_item bool True one folder per item; False writes <page_id><suffix>.<ext> flat, in one folder. Pages without item_id are always written flat. detail str 'word' word (lines and words) or line (text per line) for hOCR, ALTO and PAGE. dividers bool False put --- between layout regions in md. text_fallback bool True a page without a document still gets md and txt from Transcription.text; False writes them only from a document (the block then reads document). skip_failed bool False write no files for a page that carries errors (doc.metadata["errors"]); the default writes them as for any page.

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
Files go to <output_folder>/<item_id>/<page_id><suffix>.<ext> (any fsspec folder: local, s3://, hf://buckets/...). It reads the parts its formats are written from (FORMAT_PARTS: lines for hOCR, ALTO and PAGE, text for md and txt, document for HTML, DocLang and JSON, image for plots) and adds nothing; pages pass through, so writers can be chained. A page without the transcription is counted (no_transcription) and passed on; with skip_failed, so is a page an earlier block failed on (skipped_failed): its files would hold what the blocks before the failure made of it, while the RejectWriter lists it and the page records keep it with its errors.

  • hocr, alto, page: linecaster's serializers (to_hocr/to_alto/to_page) at the page image's size; detail="line" leaves the words out (text per line);
  • md, txt, html, doclang, json: the DoclingDocument's exports (linecaster.formats.docling.export) when the transcription has one (Composer); without one, md and txt fall back to Transcription.text (lines in reading order, tables as Markdown/HTML; counted as <format>_from_page_text) and the others are skipped (counted as no_document);
  • transcription: the Transcription itself as JSON;
  • plot: a JPEG of the page image with the regions and lines drawn in (linecaster.images.plots).

    B --> a0["page stream"]

Engine · recognition · package linecaster

Base class of a chat-VLM adapter. A subclass sets adapter (its registry name) and implements request; parse has a text-only default. Every value comes from the preset:

docs.title: composition.docling.v1
docs.text:
Engine · composition · package linecaster

Composes a page's DoclingDocument from its regions, paragraphs or lines, and tables.

The document is built by linecaster.formats.docling.DocumentBuilder: titles and section headers at their heading levels, text items with Docling's labels, page headers and footers in the furniture layer, tables with their cells, formulas, pictures with the text read inside them, optionally one section group per heading; the map of items to regions in extra["docling_region_of"]. A text region is composed from its paragraphs when a recomposition made them (one item per paragraph, continued paragraphs in one item), else from its lines as laid out (one item per region, one row per line: diplomatic composition).

The page unit is the call (the document in Transcription.docling); an item's document (all its pages, in order, paragraphs continued across pages) is item_document. Each call records a StepInfo.

Args: **options: the engine's options, the fields of its Options model (described there); a preset's options construct it.

Class linecaster.engines:DoclingCompositionEngine Source composition.py Reads pages Produces document Scripts all Runs in the pipeline's process

docs.title: recomposition.unicode.v1
docs.text:
Engine · recomposition · package linecaster

Recomposes the rows of each text region into paragraphs from geometry and Unicode's character properties.

linecaster.text.recomposition: the rows of each text region joined into paragraphs, the typesetter's division marks removed, from geometry and Unicode's character properties (line, word and sentence breaks), never from a language name; the document's own words decide the one ambiguous case (a hyphen that may belong to the word). A paragraph left open at the end of a text region continues in the next one, and at the foot of a page on the next page of the item (a region of digits only between them, a page number, does not close it); the pages of an item share the lexicon, growing page by page in order. Without geometry (a text-only transcription) a region is one paragraph, decided by the character rules alone. Covers every script whose text runs in horizontal lines.

Each decision is recorded on its paragraph (Paragraph.decisions); a continuation links the two paragraphs (continues, continues_from) and removes the division mark it decided on from the first one's text.

Args: **options: the engine's options, the fields of its Options model (described there); a preset's options construct it.

docs.title: chandra-ocr-2

Model · Chandra 2 · AI Pubs Open RAIL-M License (Modified)

Chandra 2 is Datalab's page OCR model: it turns page images and PDFs into Markdown, HTML or JSON with layout information (tables, formulas, forms with checkboxes, handwriting, images with captions). The card claims support for 90+ languages but gives no list, and names no base model. License: the card front matter says openrail; the weights are under a modified OpenRAIL-M license (the "AI Pubs Open RAIL-M License (Modified)", copied as upstream/af93b47dba1b47b6640c86ccf487ed2260ab9a09/LICENSE): free for research, personal use and small start-ups below a funding/revenue threshold, not for use in competition with Datalab's API; other commercial use needs a separate license. The code (the chandra-ocr package) is Apache-2.0. The upstream card is in upstream/af93b47dba1b47b6640c86ccf487ed2260ab9a09/README.md.

Model · DeepSeek-OCR 2 · Apache-2.0

DeepSeek-OCR 2 ("Visual Causal Flow", arXiv 2601.20552) is DeepSeek AI's successor to DeepSeek-OCR, with a new visual encoding and dynamic resolution (up to six 768x768 crops plus one 1024x1024 global view). The prompts are the same: <|grounding|>Convert the document to markdown. for Markdown with grounding markers, Free OCR. for text without layout. It needs trust_remote_code (custom code). The card says "multilingual" without a list and names no base model. docs.title: falcon-ocr
docs.text:
Model · Falcon OCR · Apache-2.0

Falcon OCR is TII's early-fusion vision-language model for document OCR (plain text, LaTeX for formulas, HTML for tables), a crop model by design: whole pages go through the vendor's pipeline service (a layout model, then one request per crop with a category prompt, and the vendor's Markdown assembly) in the vendor image ghcr.io/tiiuae/falcon-ocr. The image ships its own copy of the weights (/models/Falcon-OCR). This pin is the revision those files are: in the vendor image the preset serves (ghcr.io/tiiuae/falcon-ocr@sha256:2ec80252..., the preset's serve.image), every file of /models/Falcon-OCR has the git blob of this revision, model.safetensors its sha256 (checked 2026-11-06; NOTES.md). The repository's later revisions (Falcon OCR v1.5, 2026-09-11) have other weights. The card at this revision names no parameter count or language list (the newer card says 270M parameters). License: Apache-2.0 (the card's front matter; the repository has no license file). The upstream card is in upstream/177110bf36f6fd492428215baf76d0618854bed3/README.md.

Source tiiuae/Falcon-OCR License Apache-2.0

docs.title: glm-ocr
docs.text:
Model · GLM-OCR · MIT

GLM-OCR is Z.ai's (zai-org) 0.9B OCR model for complex documents, on the GLM-V encoder-decoder architecture: a CogViT vision encoder, a light connector and a GLM-0.5B language decoder (arXiv 2603.10910). It recognizes text, formulas and tables (Markdown output) and does schema-driven information extraction to JSON. Upstream runs it in a two-stage pipeline: PP-DocLayoutV3 layout analysis, then parallel recognition of the regions. The card names no base checkpoint. License: MIT for the model; PP-DocLayoutV3 in the full pipeline is Apache-2.0. The upstream card is in upstream/ca5d8b3e287e52589e37c28385d9655ee4372f9d/README.md.

docs.title: indra-ocr
docs.text:
Model · Indra OCR · AI Pubs Open RAIL-M License (Modified)

Indra OCR is Datalab's CPU OCR pipeline: small ONNX models (detector, orientation, script classifier, four line recognizers, layout and reading order; 7.3M parameters in all, about 1.25M in the Latin recognizer rec.onnx) run by ONNX Runtime through the indra-ocr package, which writes Markdown, text or JSON with boxes. The pin is the model set v1.1.0, the tag indra-ocr 1.1.2 is built against (indra_ocr/models.py: HF_REVISION). The card reports 95 measured languages; languages says mul because the card's front matter mixes ISO 639-1 and 639-3 codes. License: the card front matter says openrail; the weights are under a modified OpenRAIL-M license (the "AI Pubs Open RAIL-M License (Modified)", copied as upstream/bd02167fdf2005a19962cc15188f8496a2c87d3b/LICENSE): free for research and personal use, and for organizations below USD 20,000,000 of revenue and of funding; not for use by anyone offering a product or service that competes with Datalab's; other commercial use needs a separate license. The code (the indra-ocr package) is Apache-2.0. The upstream card is in upstream/bd02167fdf2005a19962cc15188f8496a2c87d3b/README.md.

docs.title: kraken-ppocrv6-medium
docs.text:
Model · PP-OCRv6 (medium) · Apache-2.0

Benjamin Kiessling's PP-OCRv6 (medium) line recognizer for kraken (ALMAnaCH, Inria Paris), as mirrored byte for byte on the Hugging Face Hub by Small Models for GLAM; the canonical release is the Zenodo record 10.5281/zenodo.21788410, which is provenance only: linecaster always downloads from the mirror (Zenodo throttles). License, languages (44 plus mul) and scripts are the card's.

The card describes the model as trained from scratch by kraken's author on line images of historical, contemporary and born-digital documents, handwritten and printed, on an architecture adapted from PaddlePaddle's PP-OCRv6 (128 px line height, uncapped line width, Adam+Muon); it is not a conversion of PaddleOCR's PP-OCRv6_medium_rec weights, so derived_from names only the mirror relation. kraken's own code runs it (kraken.recognition.v1), on torch; the model was trained in bf16-mixed, which is why linecaster's presets run it in bf16-mixed on CUDA.

Model · LightOnOCR-3-4B · Apache-2.0

LightOnOCR-3-4B is the largest model of LightOn's LightOnOCR-3 family of end-to-end OCR models. docs.text:
Model · MiniCPM-OCR 1.0 DSpark · Apache-2.0

MiniCPM-OCR 1.0 DSpark is OpenBMB's DSpark speculative-decoding draft head for MiniCPM-OCR 1.0: a small 5-layer draft model (296,837,889 parameters, BF16) that proposes tokens the main model verifies. It is not an OCR model on its own and must be paired with the matching minicpm-ocr-1.0 checkpoint (vLLM usage in the card). Its d2t tensor is delta-encoded and must be converted to absolute ids before use. The card front matter gives openbmb/MiniCPM-OCR-1.0 as base model (relation finetune). License: Apache-2.0. The upstream card is in upstream/31e3feaf80e0061cd6aa73db23480d2d691d6452/README.md.

docs.title: minicpm-ocr-1.0
docs.text:
Model · MiniCPM-OCR 1.0 · Apache-2.0

MiniCPM-OCR 1.0 is OpenBMB's 1.3B OCR model, the first OCR-specific model of the MiniCPM-V/o family: text, tables, formulas, charts, seals and key information extraction, with Chinese and English as the primary languages. Upstream's parsing pipeline pairs it with PP-DocLayoutV3 and assembles Markdown in reading order (tables as HTML, formulas as LaTeX); field extraction returns JSON. The card says it is trained for OCR on top of MiniCPM-V 4.6 (SigLIP vision encoder + Qwen3.5 language model). A DSpark speculative-decoding draft head is published separately (minicpm-ocr-1.0-dspark). License: Apache-2.0. The upstream card is in upstream/a59a4acf215e34c6d73149e9eafdb88ed2086e39/README.md.

docs.title: nemotron-3.5-parse
docs.text:
Model · Nemotron 3.5 Parse · OpenMDW-1.1

Nemotron 3.5 Parse is NVIDIA's document image parser: one string per page with text, semantic layout classes, bounding boxes and reading order (Markdown text by default; upstream helpers render Markdown with HTML tables, or LaTeX/HTML/JSON/CSV tables). It combines a C-RADIOv4-SO400M vision encoder with a 10-layer mBART decoder, about 0.631B parameters; the card names no base checkpoint. The card reports multilingual evaluation (10 Indic languages; 163 language/script entries in 26 script groups on synthetic pages) but no list of supported languages, so languages is mul and scripts is empty. License: OpenMDW License Agreement 1.1 for the weights (copied as upstream/62cb1e4ba153d113ff64aaf2be6e068c377cf53c/LICENSE); the bundled tokenizer is MIT. OXR-1.0 is SoMark's document parsing model (1.3B parameters by the card) inside a page pipeline: a D-FINE layout model (layout_analysis/last.pth in this repository) finds the regions, the OXR VLM reads each region and sets the reading order, and the vendor's oxr API assembles the page as Markdown and JSON. The pipeline runs in the vendor's all-in-one image (docker/Dockerfile.allinone of github.com/SoMarkAI/OXR), which reads the weights from a folder; the preset downloads this pin there. The card names no language list. License: the "OXR License" (copied as upstream/c708407f9d2b4df658f2543d9132b62bb7221df4/LICENSE): Apache-2.0 with additional terms that take precedence; commercial use without a separate license only below USD 2,000,000 of total funding and of annual revenue, and never for a hosted API service that competes with SoMark's. The upstream card is in upstream/c708407f9d2b4df658f2543d9132b62bb7221df4/README.md.

Surya OCR 2.5 is Datalab's page OCR model: one 689M-parameter vision-language model (Qwen3.5-style architecture) that does layout and OCR in one pass, run through Datalab's surya-ocr package (its full-page path, with a block mode for pages whose full-page answer fails). The card reports 91 languages on an internal benchmark and lists no fixed set. License: the card front matter says openrail; the weights are under a modified OpenRAIL-M license (the "AI Pubs Open RAIL-M License (Modified)", copied as upstream/00c843e9cae45611dca0a6dc2c9bbbf2dadaaed3/LICENSE): free for research and personal use, and for organizations below USD 5,000,000 of revenue and of funding; not for use by anyone offering a product or service that competes with Datalab's; other commercial use needs a separate license. The code (the surya-ocr package) is Apache-2.0. The upstream card is in upstream/00c843e9cae45611dca0a6dc2c9bbbf2dadaaed3/README.md.

Model · Unlimited-OCR 2 · MIT

Unlimited-OCR 2 ("Unlimited OCR Works 2") is Baidu's successor to Unlimited-OCR: Sparse Reference Sliding Window Attention (SR-SWA) keeps decoding cost and memory nearly constant with document length, so whole documents of hundreds of pages can be parsed in one pass. docs.title: bind.v1
docs.text:
Pipeline · bind.py · shape linecaster.pipelines.bind

The item stage (binding): an item's pages (book, issue, manuscript) bound into one item record, recomposed as one (paragraphs continued across page breaks), normalized and composed into the item's document; one text per item and text variant, and the item document in each format. It reads the page records of a transcribe run; written in item shards (--item-shards N), each task reads whole shard folders, so it sees every page of its items. No engine or GPU is needed: the steps are rule-based, each a preset (--recipe item-texts fills them).

uv run pipelines/bind.py OUT1/pages OUT2 --recipe item-texts
uv run pipelines/bind.py OUT1/pages OUT2 --recomposition unicode-recomposition --normalization latin-historic \
    --composition docling-composition
uv run pipelines/transcribe_modular.py IMAGES OUT1 ... --tasks 4000 --item-shards 64
uv run pipelines/bind.py OUT1/pages OUT2 --recipe item-texts --tasks 64
... --set composition.sections=true          # an option over the preset's
... --no-documents                           # texts only (then --composition is not needed)
... --on hf-jobs --namespace NS --commit <sha> --flavor cpu-upgrade --tasks 64

Texts in OUT2/texts//.jsonl.gz (with --files also OUT2/texts//.txt|.md), item documents in OUT2/documents//.. linecaster.runtime.run has the options every pipeline shares (IMAGES is the page records folder here).

docs.title: harvest.v1
docs.text:
Pipeline · harvest.py · shape linecaster.pipelines.harvest

The harvest stage: items' page images (and, with --existing-ocr, the library's own OCR) from their manifests (IIIF or METS; a folder, a list of links, or item tables with --manifest-key), or from http(s) image URLs in a page table (--parquet), downloaded once into item folders, with page records that keep where everything came from. No engine or GPU is needed; the transcribe stage then reads the page records without waiting on the libraries' servers. With --items it fetches items' other remote files (resources: catalogue records, API JSON, manifests) as served, from URL templates (--resource KIND=URL with {item}) or a resource table, into OUT///. with a record each in OUT/resources/.jsonl.gz; --http-policy gives settings for every host and overrides per host (rate limits, proxies or direct, retries, statuses that stop the run). 

uv run pipelines/harvest.py --manifests items.parquet --manifest-key manifest_url --item-key item_id OUT \
    --rate-limit 5/1 --existing-ocr
uv run pipelines/harvest.py --items pages.parquet --item-key lccn OUT --http-policy http-policy.yaml \
    --resource marcxml=https://catalog.example.org/{item}/marcxml
uv run pipelines/harvest.py --parquet pages.parquet --item-key book --sequence-key page --image-key url OUT \
    --rate-limit 150/60 --rate-limit 3/1
uv run pipelines/harvest.py ... SMOKE --rate-limit 150/60 --rate-limit 3/1 --max-pages 2000     # a smoke test
uv run pipelines/transcribe_modular.py --pages OUT/pages OUT2 --recipe ...                 # keeps the metadata
uv run pipelines/transcribe_modular.py OUT/images OUT2 --item-from-parent --recipe ...   # or the plain folder

OUT/images//. as the server sent them; with --existing-ocr OUT/ocr//.xml|.html; the manifests as fetched in OUT/manifests/.json|.xml; page records in OUT/pages/.jsonl.gz (image.uri the copy, image.extra.source_uri the source, metadata.manifest the item's and page's manifest data, the transcription ocr_original with the existing OCR).

Nothing needs sizing: --rate-limit holds per worker, and with it one worker runs the tasks (the run states what a server sees before it starts). Each item is a task (a --parquet page table with --item-key: a run of rows with the same item, whatever the files; --manifests: a manifest or a row of an item table; without --item-key tasks of about 1,000 pages), so an item is whole in its task and a rerun into the same OUT repeats at most the item each worker was in (datatrove's resume is per task); with --reuse, its pages whose images are already in OUT/images are read from there instead of fetched again (one listing of the item's folder; their records are complete and say image.extra.reused); without it (the default) they are fetched again and their files overwritten. The worker's requests ahead (manifests' pages and http(s) images alike) grow until the rate limits are kept busy, and the limits hold across its tasks. --tasks and --workers still override; with --workers N a server sees N times --rate-limit, so give each worker its part. With --proxies the limits hold per proxy instead, and the workers (of this run, and of other runs given the same --broker) share the proxies through the broker (default OUT/logs/broker), each proxy used by one worker at a time and left out where it was blocked; each worker holds a fair share of them (an HTTP policy's proxies: {per_worker: 1} for one each, or N). The run's workers follow the available proxies (those not blocked and not held by another run): one per proxy up to one per CPU, with 1 or N one per proxy divided by N (not capped by the CPUs: the workers wait on the network), at most one per task and at most 64 with OUT on object storage (s3://, gs://, hf://, ...), which it states before it starts. --max-pages N runs the first N pages of the input in the same automatic tasks, a smoke test of the real setup (--limit counts per task, as in datatrove). An outage of the server pauses the requests until it answers again; a book that fails anyway runs again on the next launch, and --retry-failed also runs the finished books with failed pages again: with --reuse only their failed pages are fetched (the others are read from OUT/images), without it every page of those books is fetched again. linecaster.runtime.run has the options every pipeline shares.

Option Values Default Description --reuse flag before fetching an item, list its folder in OUT and read the files an earlier launch wrote instead of fetching them again (one listing per item; off by default, since on some object storage a listing is slow even for an empty folder)

docs.title: transcribe_modular.v1
docs.text:
Pipeline · transcribe_modular.py · shape linecaster.pipelines.transcribe_modular

The modular pipeline: smaller models, picked step by step from the catalog's presets (linecaster models): a layout (a layout model, or single-region for the page as one region), text lines and a line recognizer, optionally table and formula models after; then Unicode NFC and the rule-based steps, each a preset too: typography (--typography), recomposition (--recomposition; without one the page stays as laid out) and page composition (--composition). Page records in OUT/pages; with --files per-page files in the --formats asked for (<item>/<page><suffix>.<ext>, or with --naming flat <page><suffix>.<ext> in one folder; --suffix SUFFIX, e.g. .paddle), with --item-texts one text per item in each text variant (an item stage: the item recomposed as one, normalized by --normalization). The script's environment has PaddleX and Tesseract; kraken's presets (the squiddle recipe's recognition) run in an environment that adds kraken (a script of your own that runs this shape with linecaster-kraken), or here with --backend served --endpoint against a server started from one.

uv run pipelines/transcribe_modular.py IMAGES OUT --layout single-region --lines pp-ocrv6-medium-det \
    --recognition paddlex-ppocrv6-medium
uv run pipelines/transcribe_modular.py IMAGES OUT --recipe squiddle --endpoint URL   # every slot from the recipe
... --typography ratios --recomposition unicode-recomposition --composition docling-composition
... --item-texts OUT/texts --recomposition unicode-recomposition --normalization latin-historic
uv run pipelines/transcribe_modular.py IMAGES OUT --layout pp-doclayoutv3 --lines pp-ocrv6-medium-det \
    --recognition tesseract-best-latin --tables slanet-plus --formulas pp-formulanet-plus-l
... --set recognition.batch_size=4          # an option over the preset's
... --set composition.sections=true         # also for the rule-based steps
... --backend served                        # a server in the task
... --files OUT/files --formats md,txt,json --naming flat --suffix .paddle --furniture   # <page>.paddle.md, ...
uv run pipelines/transcribe_modular.py serve --layout pp-doclayoutv3 ...    # linecaster serve with the presets named
uv run pipelines/transcribe_modular.py ray start --head --num-gpus 8        # then --on ray --tasks 64
... --on hf-jobs --namespace NS --commit <sha> --tasks 64

linecaster.runtime.run has the options every pipeline shares; --recipe fills the slots.

docs.title: transcribe_page.v1
docs.text:
Pipeline · transcribe_page.py · shape linecaster.pipelines.transcribe_page

A page engine reads the whole page (PageRecognizer on its engine): a vendor's package in the pipeline's process (Indra OCR), a vendor's package attached to a vLLM server (Surya OCR), or a client of a vendor's page pipeline behind its own HTTP API (Falcon-OCR, OXR). Each task starts the service the preset names (ServiceServer, last in the pipeline: vllm serve on the pinned checkpoint, or the vendor image's entrypoint) unless --recognition-endpoint names a running one. Page records in OUT/pages; the engine's raw output is in each page's transcription.

uv run pipelines/transcribe_page.py IMAGES OUT --recognition indra-ocr --tasks 8 --workers 8   # CPU, in-process
uv run pipelines/transcribe_page.py IMAGES OUT --recognition surya-ocr-2.5        # needs `vllm` (0.25.1) on PATH
uv run pipelines/transcribe_page.py IMAGES OUT --recognition falcon-ocr           # inside the vendor's image
uv run pipelines/transcribe_page.py IMAGES OUT --recognition oxr-1.0 --recognition-endpoint http://127.0.0.1:8000

--recognition takes a page engine's preset (linecaster models; id or id@edition); chat presets run in pipelines/transcribe_vlm.py. A vendor's service runs inside the vendor's image (the preset's serve.image): the pipeline runs there too, in its own uv environment, and the service in the image's own environments (ServiceServer leaves the pipeline's out of its environment). Its entrypoint listens on the image's ports, so one task per machine starts it; more tasks share one service with --recognition-endpoint. On HF Jobs the Job's image is the preset's serve.image unless --image is given; it needs uv (the vLLM and OXR images have it, the Falcon-OCR image does not).

docs.title: transcribe_vlm.v1
docs.text:
Pipeline · transcribe_vlm.py · shape linecaster.pipelines.transcribe_vlm

A vision-language model reads the page: the whole page (PageRecognizer) or, with a --layout preset, each region it finds (RegionRecognizer, a region preset), on the Chat backend. Each task starts vLLM or SGLang for the model itself (ChatModelServer, last in the pipeline) unless --recognition-endpoint names a running server; with --layout it also serves the layout model (--backend, --endpoint as for any engine). Page records in OUT/pages; the model's raw answer is in each page's transcription.

uv run pipelines/transcribe_vlm.py IMAGES OUT --recognition dots-ocr                     # needs `vllm` on PATH
uv run pipelines/transcribe_vlm.py IMAGES OUT --recognition dots-ocr --recognition-endpoint http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1
uv run pipelines/transcribe_vlm.py IMAGES OUT --layout pp-doclayoutv3 --recognition minicpm-ocr-1.0
uv run pipelines/transcribe_vlm.py IMAGES OUT --on hf-jobs --namespace NS --commit <sha> --recognition unlimited-ocr-2

--recognition takes a chat preset of the catalog (linecaster models; id or id@edition) or a Hugging Face id (that model's page preset, with --layout its region preset where it has one). On HF Jobs the server runs in the Job's image: the one the preset was validated with (its serve.image) unless --image is given. It has uv, Python 3.12 and vllm on PATH, so the pipeline runs in the uv environment the executor builds (linecaster alone for page presets; with --layout also linecaster-paddlex for the layout model), and ChatModelServer starts the image's own server. SGLang presets and region reading start it outside that environment (outside_venv), so neither the image's Python nor its CUDA libraries see the pipeline's packages. vLLM takes --gpu-memory-utilization of the GPU (0.8, linecaster's default; SGLang: the preset's own share); with --layout the layout server loads into the rest after vLLM's memory profiling.

docs.title: docling-composition
docs.text:
Preset · edition 1 · composition · core

A DoclingDocument per page or item, in reading order. Titles and section headers become headings at the typographer's levels, text regions text items with Docling's labels (from their paragraphs when a recomposition made them, else as laid out, one row per line), page headers and footers go into Docling's furniture layer, tables keep their cells and spans, formulas their LaTeX, pictures the text read inside them.

  • sections false: no section groups. With it, every heading opens a section that holds everything up to the next heading (JSON and DocLang gain the tree; Markdown and text read the same).

docs.text:
Preset · edition 1 · image · core

The working image: any page image Pillow decodes, as 8-bit sRGB (its ICC profile applied, alpha flattened onto white) in lossless WebP at full resolution, method 0, exact, so the pixels the models see are the delivered ones. Pages over WebP's size limit (16,383 pixels a side) or Pillow's decompression-bomb threshold are refused from the header, before decoding, and go to rejects/.

  • effort 80: libwebp's lossless compression effort (Pillow's quality); it changes the file size and the time, never the pixels.

docs.title: pp-doclayout-plus-l
docs.text:
Preset · edition 2 · layout · experimental

PP-StructureV3's layout model. It gives boxes only, no polygons and no order; the engine orders the regions with XY-Cut++ (reading_order: xy-cut++, linecaster.data.geometry.xy_cut_plus_plus): titles, figures, tables, captions, footnotes and text running across columns are masked, the remaining text is cut at whitespace gaps (vertical cuts first unless the cross-column text dominates), and the masked regions are matched back by label priority and distance; page headers lead and page footers close the page. Post-processing as PP-StructureV3 configures it, written out: per-class score thresholds (0.3 for paragraph titles and formulas, 0.4 for text, 0.45 for seals, 0.5 elsewhere), layout NMS, large box merging.

Labels: PaddleX's labels are mapped to DoclingDocument labels as linecaster_paddlex.layout.LABEL_MAP does; number (a page number) is not in labels: because the engine places it by position: page_header when its center lies in the top header_zone (15 %) of the page, else page_footer. seal stays seal, which is not a DoclingDocument label (the serializers write it as a picture). Regions contained in another by more than max_containment (80 %) of their area are dropped.

Edition 2 (2026-11-07): reading_order: xy-cut++. Edition 1 ordered the regions with plain XY-cut (the engine's default, xy-cut), horizontal cuts first; it stays resolvable from the lock.

docs.title: pp-doclayoutv3
docs.text:
Preset · edition 1 · layout · core

The squiddle combination's layout step: PP-DocLayoutV3 (PaddleOCR-VL-1.5's layout model) on ONNX Runtime. Unlike PP-DocLayout_plus-L it predicts region polygons and the reading order itself: PaddleX returns the boxes sorted by the model's order, so the list position is the reading order (furniture included) and no XY-cut is needed.

Post-processing as PaddleOCR-VL-1.5's pipeline configures it, written out here so the edition does not depend on code defaults: score threshold 0.3 for every class, PaddleX's layout NMS, and per-class box merging (large for chart, display and inline formula, doc and paragraph title: classes 3, 5, 6, 15 and 17 of the model's 25; union elsewhere). These are what PaddleLayoutEngine(model_name="PP-DocLayoutV3") uses by default.

Labels: PaddleX's labels are mapped to DoclingDocument labels as linecaster_paddlex.layout.LABEL_MAP does; number (a page number) is not in labels: because the engine places it by position: page_header when its center lies in the top header_zone (15 %) of the page, else page_footer. seal stays seal, which is not a DoclingDocument label (the serializers write it as a picture). Regions contained in another by more than max_containment (80 %) of their area are dropped.

docs.title: latin-historic
docs.text:
Preset · edition 1 · normalization · core

Character normalization for historic print in Latin script, the mapping table of the readable item texts: long s to s, the ligatures (ﬀ, ﬁ, ﬂ, ﬃ, ﬄ, ﬅ, ﬆ) spelled out, r rotunda to r, a superscript e over a, o or u to the umlaut. æ, œ, ø, å and ß stay, the text stays NFC (never NFKC) and spelling is never modernized. It fills Line.normalized and Paragraph.normalized; the as-written texts are not touched.

docs.title: chandra-ocr-2
docs.text:
Preset · edition 1 · recognition · core

chandra-ocr-2 as the vendor's own vLLM client runs it, chandra-ocr v0.2.0 (chandra/model/vllm.py: generate_vllm), with the ocr_layout prompt of the CLI. Where linecaster departs from the client, the item says so.

  • The page image, then the ocr_layout prompt (verbatim from chandra/prompts.py at v0.2.0, hash-checked).
  • RGB, the vendor's scale_to_fit (pixel count clamped to 3072 x 2048 and up to 1792 x 28, both sides snapped to multiples of 28, LANCZOS), PNG.
  • Sampling: temperature 0.0, top_p 0.1, max_tokens 12384 (the vendor's MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS); the chat template opens an empty <think></think>, so thinking needs no switch.
  • One attempt per page (linecaster's choice): the vendor client retries a page up to six times at a raised temperature when it detects a repetition loop; here a loop shows as a loop.
  • Serve flags: --max-model-len 20480 (linecaster's choice, where the vendor's launcher has 18000: 6144 visual tokens at the cap + 12384 + the prompt do not fit in 18000), the vendor's --mm-processor-kwargs pixel bounds and --dtype bfloat16, one image and no video per prompt, no multimodal processor cache, no prefix caching; no --trust-remote-code. vLLM 0.26.0 (linecaster's choice; the vendor's launcher pins 0.17.0).
  • The model answers with HTML layout blocks (<div data-bbox=.. data-label=..>), stored verbatim; converting them to Markdown (the vendor's parse_markdown) is left to whoever reads the output. --gpu-memory-utilization is the deployment's choice.

Preset · edition 1 · recognition · core

DeepSeek-OCR-2 in grounded document mode, following the model card and the uv-scripts recipe deepseek-ocr2-vllm.py (the DeepSeek-OCR and DeepSeek-OCR-2 presets differ only in the checkpoint).

  • The prompt <|grounding|>Convert the document to markdown. as a text part after the image (the card's raw <image>\n<|grounding|>... prompt becomes image + text; the chat template inserts the image token).
  • No resolution mode is passed (no mm_processor_kwargs), so vLLM's default applies: Gundam (base 1024, tiles of 640, crop mode, up to 6 crops), the mode the card recommends for documents.

  • Serve flags: --max-model-len 8192 (the native context), --trust-remote-code, no prefix caching, no multimodal processor cache, one image per prompt.
  • The completion is stored verbatim, grounding markup included; linecaster.adapters.deepseek_ocr.strip_grounding removes it for whoever wants the text alone. --gpu-memory-utilization is the deployment's choice.

docs.title: falcon-ocr
docs.text:
Preset · edition 1 · recognition · experimental

Falcon-OCR's whole-page product: the vendor's pipeline service (layout detection, one request per crop with a category prompt, the vendor's Markdown assembly) in the vendor's image, one page per request to POST /falconocr/parse. The engine (falcon.recognition.v1, package linecaster-services) is its client in the pipeline's process.

  • The service: ServiceServer starts the image's own single-GPU entrypoint (/app/entrypoint_single.sh: vLLM with the model on port 8000, the pipeline on 5002, both on GPU 0 of the container) and waits until both answer /health. The image's entrypoint binds both to every address of the container. The weights are the image's own (/models/Falcon-OCR, the model pin's files); the image digest fixes what runs.
  • The request: the page as RGB, scaled down (LANCZOS) so its longest side is at most 2,048 px, JPEG quality 95, as a data URI (linecaster's choice of payload), with skip_layout false (the vendor's full-page path; the direct VLM path is off-label).
  • Kept verbatim: markdown_result (extra["raw"], the text) and the layout regions (json_result). The service reports no finish reason, so no loop can be counted; its output tokens are the step's completion_tokens. The Markdown can contain leaked >>UNUSED_N<< vocabulary tokens; removing them is left to whoever reads the output.
  • The image has Python 3.10 and no uv: on HF Jobs the pipeline cannot run inside it as it is (not tried).

Apache-2.0. Not run on HF Jobs.

docs.title: indra-ocr
docs.text:
Preset · edition 1 · recognition · experimental

Indra OCR as its package runs it: indra-ocr (1.1.2) on the CPU, in the pipeline's process, each page through the package's own image path (Converter.convert(path), the call the indra-ocr command makes), so decoding to grayscale, orientation, deskew, detection, recognition, layout and reading order are the package's. The engine is indra.recognition.v1 (package linecaster-indra).

  • Settings: indra_ocr.load()'s defaults, written out: mode auto (an image is OCR'd), furniture false (page headers and footers dropped from the Markdown), math false, dpi 200 (PDFs only), one ONNX Runtime thread per task (the package's own workers are single-threaded, one per core: run as many tasks as cores).
  • The models: the pin of datalab-to/indra-ocr at the tag v1.1.0, the model set indra-ocr 1.1.2 is built against (indra_ocr/models.py: HF_REVISION), every pinned file checked.
  • The page goes to the package as its file's bytes, as the reader brought them (the engine's image_input is bytes), as the indra-ocr command reads a file; the package decodes it in grayscale with OpenCV. The pipeline script resolves OpenCV 4.11 (surya-ocr's pin, in the same environment).
  • Kept verbatim: the package's Markdown (extra["raw"], the text), with its layout blocks, rotation and skew. A page the package reports as failed is the page's error; an empty Markdown (a blank leaf) is a transcription without text.

Weights: modified OpenRAIL-M (see the model's page).

docs.title: minicpm-ocr-1.0
docs.text:
Preset · edition 1 · recognition · experimental

MiniCPM-OCR 1.0 as a region reader, run the way OpenBMB's SDK (minicpm-ocr 1.0.1) runs it: the SDK finds PP-DocLayoutV3 regions, crops each one from the full-resolution page and sends the crop with the prompt for its region type. Here the layout comes from linecaster's layout step and RegionRecognizer sends the crops.

  • Prompt and token cap per region type from the SDK's DEFAULT_PROMPT_MAP["element_prompts"], looked up by the layout model's own label (PP-DocLayoutV3's class name, the SDK's vocabulary): Text Recognition: for text-like regions, Table Recognition: (8192 tokens), Formula Recognition: for display formulas, Chart to Table:, Seal Recognition:; unknown types get the SDK default (Text Recognition:, 8192). Caps are clamped to max-model-len - 512 as the SDK does (no effect at 40960).
  • Request: the crop, then the prompt; mm_processor_kwargs {"downsample_mode": "4x", "max_slice_nums": 9}; thinking off; temperature 0.01, top_p 0.001, top_k 1, repetition_penalty 1.0, no_repeat_ngram_size 100; PNG.
  • Every region is read but the image types (image, header_image, footer_image); charts and seals are read (the SDK's chart and seal recognition are on).
  • Crop: from the full-resolution page (no page scaling, no padding), the box truncated to whole pixels as PaddleX's CropByBoxes does, pixels outside the region's polygon white.
  • Serve flags from OpenBMB's SDK tutorial, served as minicpm-ocr; DSpark speculative decoding with the matching draft model (minicpm-ocr-1.0-dspark, 15 speculative tokens; --no-speculative in the recipe turns it off).
  • vLLM nightly 5d35ce3 (0.32.1rc1.dev602+g5d35ce393) with transformers at OpenBMB's pin, the image named in serve.image. ninja must be on PATH or the engine fails at startup.
  • linecaster.adapters.minicpm_ocr.assemble_markdown assembles the page with the SDK's own code (extra linecaster[minicpm-ocr]), keeping footnote and aside_text.

Not reproduced: the SDK's PaddleX box filtering (filter_overlap_boxes) and its merging of aligned text blocks into one composite crop (merge_blocks); linecaster's layout step runs PP-DocLayoutV3's ONNX export with its own containment suppression. Experimental.

docs.title: nemotron-3.5-parse
docs.text:
Preset · edition 1 · recognition · core

Nemotron 3.5 Parse as its model card serves it (docs/serving.md, "Generation contract" and the H100 vllm serve block).

  • The control-token prompt </s><s><predict_bbox><predict_classes><output_markdown><predict_text_in_pic> as a text part FIRST, then the page image (the vendor client).
  • RGB at the original size, PNG (the server-side processor fits it to 2048 x 1664; a client-side resize would resample twice).
  • Sampling: temperature 0.0, top_k 1, repetition_penalty 1.1, max_tokens 8744, skip_special_tokens false (the reply's coordinate and class tokens are kept).
  • Serve flags, the card's H100 block: --max-model-len 16384 --trust-remote-code --dtype bfloat16 --distributed-executor-backend uni --max-num-seqs 192 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384, no prefix caching, one image per prompt, --attention-config '{"flash_attn_version": 3}'. FlashAttention 3 is a Hopper kernel: an Ada or Ampere GPU (L4, A10G) cannot run these flags as they are.
  • The architecture (RadioMBartPrefixForCausalLM) is not in vLLM 0.26.0's registry. NVIDIA serves it through a vLLM general plugin (nemotron-parse 3.5.0.post7) shipped in the model repo; the adapter's serve_setup installs it into the vLLM image's own Python before vllm serve (the package source and NVIDIA's inference constraints from the model repo at the pinned revision, the lock's own nemotron-parse line dropped; the install fails if vLLM moved off 0.26.0). The plugin's one-token MTP speculative decoding stays on, as the card serves it. The image is vllm/vllm-openai:v0.26.0 by its amd64 digest.
  • The completion (coordinate tokens, <class_*> tokens and Markdown text) is stored verbatim; linecaster.adapters.nemotron_parse35.to_markdown renders it as the vendor's render_markdown from the model repo does.
