docs.title: oxr-1.0
docs.text:
Preset · edition 1 · recognition · experimental

OXR-1.0's whole-page product: the vendor's all-in-one service (D-FINE layout, the OXR VLM per region and its reading order, the vendor's oxr API assembling the page), one page per request to POST /v1/parse/sync. The engine (oxr.recognition.v1, package linecaster-services) is its client in the pipeline's process.

  • The service: an image built unmodified from the vendor's docker/Dockerfile.allinone at github.com/SoMarkAI/OXR@c1a1dcb3 (on the vendor's pinned vllm/vllm-openai:v0.25.1; the vendor's plugin and entrypoint require vLLM 0.25.1 and Transformers 5.13.1), by digest. ServiceServer downloads the model pin to /models/oxr-model (every pinned file checked, rather than mounting the weights) and starts the image's entrypoint, which serves vLLM on 8080 and the layout model on 8081 (loopback) and the API on 8000 (OXR_API_HOST 127.0.0.1); the API answers /docs once both model services are ready.
  • The request: the page as RGB, lossless PNG at its own size, as the multipart file, with api_key and one output_formats field each for markdown and json (httpx's encoding of a list). No feature_config or element_formats: the vendor's defaults (page headers and footers dropped, the overlap clean-up full_overlap_dedupe off).
  • Kept verbatim: the API's Markdown (extra["raw"], the text), its blocks (JSON) and warnings. An answer with a non-zero code is the page's error. The service reports no finish reason or token counts (its per-region cap is 8,192 tokens in the vendor's configuration). The Markdown links the figure crops as images; removing the links is left to whoever reads the output.

License: the OXR License (Apache-2.0 with additional terms; see the model's page). Not run on HF Jobs.

Preset · edition 1 · recognition · core

Qwen3.5-9B as a page reader, built from the model card and the checkpoint's config: greedy decoding with the card's penalties.

  • The page image, then the prompt Transcribe all of the text in this image. (linecaster's choice, a neutral prompt: the card documents no OCR prompt).

docs.title: surya-ocr-2.5
docs.text:
Preset · edition 1 · recognition · experimental

Surya OCR 2.5 as its package runs it: the surya-ocr package (0.23.0, the release that shipped with the checkpoint) and its full-page path, the call its surya_ocr command makes (RecognitionPredictor(manager)([page], full_page=True)), with the package's parser, blank-region filter and block-mode fallback. The engine (surya.recognition.v1, package linecaster-surya) reimplements none of it.

  • The server: the package would start vllm/vllm-openai:v0.25.1 with docker run. ServiceServer starts vllm serve on the pinned checkpoint instead (fetched, every pinned file checked, and served under the package's model name datalab-to/surya-ocr-2.5), with the flags the package's launcher passes for VLLM_GPU_TYPE=a100-80 (an A100 80 GB): --max-num-seqs 104 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384, the package's dtype, model length, memory share, prefix caching and image limits; no MTP flag (the checkpoint has no MTP head). The engine attaches through SURYA_INFERENCE_URL, the package's own attach path. The image is the package's pin, by digest.
  • Every package setting is its default: full-page mode, 12,288 full-page tokens, guided layout JSON, SURYA_FULLPAGE_REGEN off (Datalab's own benchmark harness turns it on; the preset keeps the shipped default). The page goes in as an RGB image at its own size; the package scales it to fit 3072 x 2048 px.
  • The package and vLLM need separate environments (surya-ocr pins OpenCV 4.11, vLLM needs 4.13 or later): vLLM is the image's, surya-ocr the pipeline script's. surya-ocr declares pillow<11; the pipeline script overrides it with linecaster's Pillow pin (12.3.0).
  • Kept verbatim: the page's blocks as JSON (extra["raw"]: label, raw label, reading order, HTML, skipped, error, confidence, box). Rendering them to Markdown (with chandra's HTML converter, page headers and footers kept) is left to whoever reads the output. finish_reason is length when the page keeps a capped block's partial HTML; a failed block request is the page's error.

Weights: modified OpenRAIL-M (see the model's page). Not run on HF Jobs.

docs.title: unlimited-ocr-2
docs.text:
Preset · edition 1 · recognition · core

Unlimited-OCR-2 on Baidu's patched SGLang, following the model card. No vLLM support exists for it.

  • Server: SGLang in the image's own Python (lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.20-cu130), with Baidu's wheel (sglang-0.5.20.dev10+g8d62f5fb9c, read from the model repo at the pinned revision) installed --no-deps and fastokens==0.3.2 first; served as Unlimited-OCR-2; the card's launch environment and flags, plus --enable-metrics (saturate reads SGLang's queue gauges). SGLANG_UOCR_EANABLE_DOC_LIMIT is upstream's spelling. serve.version is the wheel's version, which is the SGLang that runs.
  • No --revision: with it, Baidu's SGLang skips its tokenizer fix-up and fastokens refuses the tokenizer at boot, so the server loads the default branch. The default branch has moved on from the pinned commit (README and a newer wheel only), so the serve block checks that every file on the default branch other than README, .gitattributes, wheel/ and the paper PDF equals the pinned revision's (git blob ids).
  • The image, then <PAGE><image>Multi page parsing. (card-verbatim, the same prompt for one page as for many); full resolution, the same passthrough rule as v1.
  • max_tokens 8000, temperature 0.0, skip_special_tokens false, images_config {"crop_mode": true} (gundam, the card's single-page default), and the card's no-repeat n-gram guard as an SGLang custom logit processor (DeepseekOCRNoRepeatNGramLogitProcessor, by its dill pickle reference) with its parameters.
  • The completion (<BLOCK>type[x1, y1, x2, y2]<FORK>text blocks) is stored verbatim; Baidu's own Markdown converter is left to whoever reads the output. A response without content is an error.
  • The card's flags are for an 80 GB A800 (--mem-fraction-static 0.7, CUDA graphs up to 16384 prefill tokens); they also run on a 96 GB card.

docs.title: unicode-recomposition
docs.text:
Preset · edition 1 · recomposition · core

The rows of each text region joined into paragraphs, from geometry and Unicode's character properties, never from a language name; the squiddle combination's recomposition.

  • Paragraph breaks: a row indented by indent (0.8 em) from the start margin, a gap above it of about a blank line (more than gap_leading 0.6 of the leading and gap_height 0.5 of the taller row), or, in justified text (at least justified_rows 3 rows, justified_share 0.6 of them ending within end_margin 0.6 em of the end margin), a row before it that stopped short_row 1.5 em and short_row_width a quarter of the width short.
  • Division marks (Unicode's hyphens by Line_Break, and convention_marks, the not sign some transcription conventions write) after a letter at a row end are removed unless the next row starts with a capital or a digit, a Hebrew letter is not followed by Hebrew, or the document attests the hyphenated form and not the joined one. The lexicon is the item's own words, growing page by page.
  • Rows join without a space where UAX #14 allows a break without one (ideographs, Thai), else with one.
  • A paragraph without sentence-final punctuation that ends with a division mark or reaches the end margin continues in the next text region whose first row is not indented and starts with a letter, and, recomposing an item, on the next page; a region of digits only between them (a page number) does not close it.
  • Without geometry (a text-only transcription) a region is one paragraph.
Step recomposition (reads items) Engine recomposition.unicode.v1 Produces paragraphs

docs.title: slanet-plus
docs.text:
Preset · edition 2 · tables · core

PaddleX's table_recognition_v2 pipeline on every table region, fed with the page's own lines and their recognized text instead of its own OCR (use_ocr_model=False with an external OCR result); the cells come back with our text in PaddleX's HTML. The squiddle combination's table step.

  • SLANet_plus end to end for both table classes (e2e: structure and cell boxes from SLANet_plus's own prediction, the RT-DETR cell detectors unused), linecaster's choice where PP-StructureV3 uses SLANeXt_wired with a cell detector for what the classifier calls wired.
  • crop_pad 8: the table region's crop is grown by 8 px on every side (linecaster's choice).
  • The pipeline's other models are its submodels, by PaddleX name: the wired/wireless classifier (PP-LCNet_x1_0_table_cls, which picks the branch) and the two cell detectors (loaded by the pipeline, unused with e2e), each a pin of its model entry, so their files are part of the edition's hash.

Edition 2 (2026-11-03): the same models at the same revisions, moved from the option submodel_revisions (edition 1) to submodels, so their file hashes count too. Edition 1 was dropped from the lock when the catalogs were merged into one (2026-11-04), before any run recorded it. - Unruled rows come back as one cell per column with every PaddleX table model.

docs.title: ratios
docs.text:
Preset · edition 1 · typography · core

The hierarchy of a page from its own type sizes, every rule a ratio to the body size (the median row height of the page's text regions); the squiddle combination's typography.

  • levels: a heading whose rows are at least 2.5 times the body size is level 1, 1.7 times level 2, else level 3.
  • demote 1.2: a section header set in about the body size is text (layout models often call a bold run-in heading a section header).
  • split 1.6, max_headline_rows 3: up to three leading rows of a text region this much taller than the rows after them and the body size are a headline the layout model merged into the text; they become a section header of their own.
  • page_number_min_conf 0.75: a page-number region read with a lower mean character confidence (or empty) is an ornament or a blob, and is removed (recorded in extra["retyper_dropped"]).
  • Drop capitals (a layout model's drop-capital class) are joined to the first line of the text region they belong to.

docs.title: item-texts
docs.text:
Recipe · edition 1 · pipeline bind.v1 · core

The item stage's default combination: each item's pages recomposed as one item (unicode-recomposition: paragraphs continued across page breaks, the item's own words as the lexicon), normalized for reading (latin-historic: long s, ligatures, r rotunda and superscript e folded) and composed into the item's document (docling-composition). It writes the text variants verbatim_txt, readable_txt and readable_md and the item document in md, txt and json.

  • The readable texts come from the recomposition since phase 3 of the refactoring; before, a simpler flow joined each region's lines.
  • For historic print in Latin script; other scripts are recomposed by the same Unicode rules, and the normalization leaves their characters as they are.
uv run launch.py item-texts IMAGES OUT
Slot Preset recomposition unicode-recomposition@1 normalization latin-historic@1 composition docling-composition@1

docs.title: squiddle
docs.text:
Recipe · edition 1 · pipeline transcribe_modular.v1 · core

OCR for historical print from small models. PP-DocLayoutV3 finds the regions and their reading order, PP-OCRv6 medium detection finds the lines on the whole page, kraken's PP-OCRv6 medium recognizer reads them (batch 8, bf16 on CUDA), SLANet_plus rebuilds tables and PP-FormulaNet_plus-L reads formulas as LaTeX; rule-based steps make the typography, recompose the text into paragraphs (ratios, unicode-recomposition) and compose the page document (docling-composition); the readable item texts (--item-texts) are normalized with latin-historic.

  • The recomposition changes paragraphs, not lines: a comparison of the lines is the same with or without it.
  • Until phase 3 of the refactoring the recipe named the rule-based steps through the option text: reflow; naming their presets changes neither the pipeline nor its outputs, so the edition was migrated (its earlier hashes stay in the lock as previous_sha256), not renumbered.
  • A derivative that runs this recipe with other models runs a variation, not the recipe.

Slot Preset layout pp-doclayoutv3@1 lines pp-ocrv6-medium-det@1 recognition kraken-ppocrv6-medium@1 tables slanet-plus@2 formulas pp-formulanet-plus-l@1 typography ratios@1 recomposition unicode-recomposition@1 normalization latin-historic@1 composition docling-composition@1

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: What linecaster is made of and how a run fits together. Terms are the glossary's; contracts, the builder, failures and the run record are in pipelines, models, presets, recipes and engines in the catalog, the page record in the data model.

docs.title: What linecaster is
docs.text: An open, modular text-recognition suite for print and handwriting (OCR and HTR, old and new documents). It combines layout, line, text, table and formula recognizers with post-processing (dehyphenation, recomposition, normalization) into reproducible datatrove pipelines that turn page images into text: the text as written, readable variants next to it, ALTO, PAGE-XML and hOCR on request. It is a generalist tool: built on protocols (HTTP, S3/fsspec, OAI-PMH, IIIF), formats (ALTO, PAGE-XML, hOCR, Parquet, JSON Lines) and standards (METS/MODS, Unicode), it depends on no collection, site, institution or project. Everything that produces text from images lives here; evaluations and project pipelines (derivatives) are built on top of it.

docs.title: Packages
docs.text:
Package Holds linecaster.data the data model: Item, Page, PageImage, Transcription, Text, StepInfo, the measurements vocabulary linecaster.formats ALTO, PAGE-XML and hOCR out and in; the DoclingDocument exports linecaster.text the text transforms: Unicode, typography, recomposition, the text variants linecaster.images the working image, plots linecaster.engines the built-in engines: the rule-based steps and the single-region layout linecaster.blocks the blocks by family (blocks) linecaster.backends InProcess, Served, Chat linecaster.adapters one adapter per VLM family, ADAPTERS linecaster.serve linecaster serve linecaster.net http(s) fetching (linecaster.net.http), the HTTP policy, the proxy pools (http) linecaster.broker the broker: leases, marks and worker slots in a shared folder; linecaster broker linecaster.runtime the builder, the pipelines' command line, executors, the run record, Jobs helpers, secrets, logs linecaster.pipelines the pipeline shapes, one per pipeline script (pipelines) linecaster.catalog the catalog: its entries, schemas, lock, fetching pins, the docs of its entries linecaster.tracing tracing (OpenTelemetry) and linecaster traces linecaster.docs linecaster docs: the generated pages linecaster.testing test helpers: sample pages, fake engines (fake.<step>.v1, the page engine fake.recognition.page.v1), a fake chat server, a fake HTTP service, the conformance checks check_engine and check_block, the pytest markers

The first five load neither datatrove nor saturate, nor linecaster's blocks or runtime (tests/test_import_rule.py), so derivatives can use the data model and the formats without the pipeline machinery. datatrove and saturate are required dependencies, datatrove with its io and s3 extras (s3:// paths work everywhere), and so is httpx (http(s):// through linecaster.net); engines, Ray and PDFium are not (engine packages and extras).

docs.title: Blocks and backends
docs.text:
A block is a datatrove PipelineStep with a contract; a pipeline is a list of blocks run by a datatrove executor. Each family is a subpackage of linecaster.blocks (blocks has a page per block).

Model blocks (ModelBlock: LayoutDetector, LineDetector, LineRecognizer, TableRecognizer, FormulaRecognizer, PageRecognizer, RegionRecognizer) each have a backend:

  • InProcess("pkg:Class", **kwargs) (or a preset ref) loads the engine in the worker, in warm_up() before the first page; a loaded engine is never pickled. In-process is always available and is the parity reference.
  • Served(endpoint, model=name) and Chat(preset, endpoint) (a VLM) stream pages through saturate (AdaptiveClient and through()): a window of pages in flight, adapted to the server's queue gauges and 429s; results passed on as they finish; secrets as EnvVar. The streaming exists once, in ModelBlock.

A page that failed a step carries doc.metadata["errors"], passes later model steps at once and goes to rejects/; more failures than the error budget fail the task (pipelines). Library code raises linecaster.errors, never SystemExit.

Rule blocks (RuleBlock: Typographer, Recomposer, Composer, CharacterNormalizer; and ImageConverter) run a built-in engine of a rule-based step in the pipeline's process, picked by a preset.

docs.title: One page per request
docs.text: A request carries one page; engines batch only within a page (kraken batches a page's lines). A page's result depends only on the page, never on what else is in flight, so runs are deterministic whatever the executor, the number of tasks or the backend.

docs.title: Servers
docs.text:
• linecaster serve hosts engines: stateless (no state between requests), one worker per model (several replicas per model were measured at +7–10 % and removed; NOTES.md), each with a bounded queue (--max-queue; a full queue answers 429 with Retry-After). Routes: POST /v1/linecaster/{step} (the image and the transcription so far in, the transcription with its part added out), GET /v1/models, /health and vLLM-shaped /metrics (the gauges saturate reads). Built-in engines are not served: they run in the pipeline's process.
  • VLMs run behind OpenAI-compatible servers (vLLM, SGLang, hosted endpoints): PageRecognizer and RegionRecognizer on the Chat backend, on /v1/chat/completions, served only. PageRecognizer also runs a page engine (an engine whose unit is the page) on the InProcess or Served backend: a vendor's package in the worker (Indra OCR), a vendor's package attached to a vLLM server (Surya OCR), or a client of a vendor's page pipeline behind its own HTTP API (Falcon-OCR, OXR). A VLM is a catalog preset (engine chat.v1; its data: revision, prompt, sampling, serve block) plus an adapter in linecaster.adapters.ADAPTERS (its code: the request, the parsing; chat_model(<preset>)).
  • Servers inside a task (one GPU per HF Job): the server blocks ModelServer (linecaster serve) and ChatModelServer (vLLM or SGLang) start the server through saturate's Engine and go last in the pipeline, after the writer: datatrove chains generators, and only the last one lives until every page is written. Each task starts its own servers. ModelServer(script=...) starts a pipeline script's serve with uv run --script. ServiceServer starts the service a page preset's serve block names: vllm serve on the pinned checkpoint (fetched and checked) for an engine package that attaches to vLLM, or a vendor image's entrypoint (with the weights downloaded to the folder it reads first), ready once its health URLs answer; it runs without the pipeline's environment, in the image's own. A vendor's entrypoint listens on the image's fixed ports: one service per machine.

docs.title: Engines
docs.text: An engine is a class with a versioned id (catalog). Engine packages live in engines/<engine>/, each its own package: linecaster-kraken, linecaster-paddlex, linecaster-tesseract, and the page engines' linecaster-indra, linecaster-surya and linecaster-services (the clients of Falcon-OCR's and OXR's services). An engine class (<Provider><Step>Engine) has engine_id (the entry point's name in linecaster.engines), step, capabilities (unit, produces), an Options model (its keyword arguments; a preset's weights besides), load() and __call__(image, transcription, **params) -> Transcription (the page image as an RGB array, or the image file's bytes for an engine whose image_input is "bytes", and the transcription so far, returned with its part added). Engines with weights load exactly the pin (weights, linecaster.catalog.fetch). PaddleX's models load from the pinned snapshot (create_predictor(model_dir=...)); small-models-for-glam/kraken-blla-base (the BLLA base model of September 2026) is pinned in linecaster_kraken.models, and no engine uses it. Engine packages carry code only; their presets and models are in linecaster's catalog. They import from linecaster only linecaster.data and the engine API (linecaster.engines.api: the Engine protocol, Capabilities, the weight helpers), have versions of their own with a range of linecaster releases, and their tests in engines/<engine>/tests/ (catalog).

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
uv run pytest runs the core's tests, one after the other; uv run pytest -n auto (pytest-xdist, in the dev group) runs them on every core. Tests marked gpu or network (linecaster.testing.markers: gpu, network, slow; --strict-markers) skip where the device or the network is missing. The CI workflow (.github/workflows/ci.yml, CPU only, no secrets, uv's cache kept between runs) runs uv sync --locked --all-extras (the extras' readers are tested and documented too), uv run pytest -n auto -m "not gpu and not network", linecaster catalog verify, linecaster docs and the site's strict build (the generated pages are not in git, so CI writes them and a broken reference in them fails the build). The docs workflow (.github/workflows/docs.yml) writes them too and publishes the site with mike on the gh-pages branch, which GitHub Pages serves (https://storytracer.github.io/linecaster/): a release tag v<major>.<minor>.<patch> as version <major>.<minor>, with latest (the site's default) moved to it; nothing else is published. The engines' environments are too large for it (torch): their tests (engines/<engine>/tests/) and the PEP 723 test scripts (tests/test_engines_catalog.py, tests/test_page_engines_catalog.py, tests/test_line_recognizers.py) run locally. Every built-in engine and every public block passes the conformance checks of linecaster.testing (check_engine: the engine protocol; check_block: the contract against what the block does to sample pages, to_dict(), pickling, warm_up(), failed pages).

An engine package's tests run in an environment that has the engine: uv run tests/test_engines_catalog.py engines/<engine>/tests. tests/test_engines_catalog.py is also linecaster's only environment with kraken (with PaddleX and Tesseract, for the catalog's line-recognizer presets): a test script, not a pipeline script, since no pipeline of linecaster's names a model choice. A kraken chain runs in an environment that adds kraken (a derivative's own script running transcribe_modular.v1), or in pipelines/transcribe_modular.py with --backend served --endpoint against a server started from one; with --endpoint the served engines need not be installed in the client's environment. To preview the site from a checkout: uv run linecaster docs, then uv run --group docs mkdocs serve.

docs.title: Pipeline scripts
docs.text:
There are no environment folders: a pipeline is a self-contained uv script in pipelines/ (a PEP 723 block, a <script>.py.lock next to it, uv run <script>) that runs one pipeline shape with slots, one script per shape, never one per machine. The shape is library code, linecaster.pipelines.<name> (its options, engines, blocks, pipeline id and slots), so a derivative's script can run it in its own environment with its own defaults (pipelines):

Script Pipeline id Does harvest.py harvest.v1 downloads page images (and a library's OCR, manifests) once into item folders, plus page records transcribe_modular.py transcribe_modular.v1 lines and a recognizer, optionally layout, tables, formulas, then post-processing; every step a preset the user picks; PaddleX and Tesseract, no kraken transcribe_vlm.py transcribe_vlm.v1 a VLM per page or per layout region transcribe_page.py transcribe_page.v1 a page engine per page, with the service its preset names bind.py bind.v1 item texts and item documents from page records

linecaster.runtime.run.main gives every pipeline the same command line: --on local|ray|hf-jobs, --backend in-process|served, --endpoint (a running server), serve (linecaster serve with the script's models), ray (Ray's CLI from the script's environment). Slots have no default presets: every slot is picked, or a recipe fills them (--recipe); launch.py runs a recipe or a page preset by name (catalog). Each script's page in the catalog's docs lists its slots and options.

Script environments: the repository is not a uv workspace (engine pins conflict). A script lists what it needs itself: linecaster with the extra every pipeline uses (ray for --on ray and ray start) and its engine packages; s3:// paths need no extra (the core installs datatrove's s3 extra, s3fs). A source is declared by the package that needs it, and uv lock applies the sources of path and git dependencies too: the kraken fork by linecaster-kraken, and stubs/opencv-contrib-python (the headless build of the version PaddleX pins; one cv2) by linecaster-paddlex. tests/test_scripts.py checks sources, locks and wheels for both machines (uv's required-environments does not work in scripts).

torch is never a dependency of the core. Only linecaster-kraken pins it (torch==2.14.0: kraken's upper bound is <=2.14, and the PyPI 2.14 wheels are the CUDA 13 build on Linux, aarch64 and x86_64), and only environments with linecaster-kraken are bound by that pin; the others take what their own dependencies allow. Each lock's torch is fixed in tests/test_scripts.py (TORCH), so it changes only on purpose:

Environment torch Why tests/test_engines_catalog.py 2.14.0 linecaster-kraken's pin pipelines/transcribe_page.py, tests/test_page_engines_catalog.py 2.14.0 surya-ocr's (>=2.7,<3), not pinned: the version it was locked at tools/cuda_probe.py 2.14.0 its own pin: it probes the CUDA build of linecaster-kraken's torch on a Jobs host pipelines/transcribe_modular.py, transcribe_vlm.py, harvest.py, bind.py, launch.py, tests/test_line_recognizers.py, linecaster's own (uv.lock) none no engine there needs it

docs.title: Executors and Jobs
docs.text:
--on Executor local datatrove's LocalPipelineExecutor ray RayGPUExecutor for stages with servers and single-stage pipelines with engines (one task per GPU), RayExecutor (datatrove's RayPipelineExecutor) otherwise, on CPUs (an item stage, a harvest; extra [ray]); both stop the run at an error that is not the pages', fail a launch that left tasks unfinished, and check first that a live node can run a task hf-jobs JobsExecutor: datatrove's JobsPipelineExecutor with JSON-lines logs; GPUJobsExecutor for multi-GPU flavors

datatrove's JobsPipelineExecutor is experimental and dill-pickles the pipeline, so the launching machine and the Jobs run the same Python minor version (3.12). uv run outside a project drops [tool.uv.sources]: linecaster.runtime.jobs.dependencies(commit, script) spells out a pipeline's dependencies and sources as URLs, the installed packages' own sources from the script's lock (the commit must be pushed), and pins every other package at the lock's version; each Job runs a uv script that carries the pins and the script's overrides, which uv run --with would ignore (pipelines).

Workers that share something beyond their tasks (a proxy list, whose proxies each worker may use only while no other does) agree through the broker, a folder any executor's workers can reach, on any storage datatrove supports: leases say who holds what, marks what is unavailable until when, and a worker is a slot of its machine that outlives the processes (on Ray every task is one) that take it over.

docs.title: The run layout
docs.text:
One job is one pipeline for one batch on one executor; resume is datatrove's, per task, so tasks stay small. A pipeline reads the previous folder and writes complete page records with one more part filled in:

Folder Holds originals/ the delivered images and files; never modified OUT/pages/ page records (PageJsonlWriter, PageParquetWriter), bucketed by item id: a whole item in one file, so no joins OUT/rejects/ every page that carries errors (RejectWriter, put before the first writer by the builder): key, field, error, raw value OUT/logs/ datatrove's completion markers, logs and stats; OUT/logs/broker/, the broker by default OUT/traces/ the traces (tracing) OUT/run.yaml the run record (pipelines)

PageRecordReader reads page records of linecaster's writers, fetching images again by URI (uri_map for local copies). Checks like PageValidator record on the page why it failed.

Readers follow datatrove's conventions (BaseDiskReader: data_folder, paths_file, glob_pattern, limit/skip per task; files distributed over tasks in turn, Parquet tables by rows in equal shards, linecaster.blocks.readers.tables, so a table needs no splitting): ImageFolderReader (image files), ImageParquetReader (an image column: bytes, an HF image struct or a path), ManifestReader (IIIF or METS, parsed by linecaster.formats.manifests, its files fetched through linecaster.net.http; a manifest, or a row of a Parquet item table, is an entry, so an item stays in one task; a IIIF Collection entry is its manifests, one level; existing_ocr fetches a library's OCR as a document media, which a TranscriptionConverter reads as ocr_original, the builder adding one when missing), PdfReader (PDF files as items, pages rendered with pypdfium2, extra [pypdfium2]) and PageRecordReader. Readers that fetch over http(s) request ahead in a window that grows while no request waits for the rate limits (linecaster.net.http.prefetched), through one fetcher per process and configuration, so the limits hold across a worker's tasks; ImageParquetReader and ManifestReader suggest a task count from their input (auto_tasks), which a pipeline without engines runs with (pipelines).

The workflow is harvest → transcribe → bind: pipelines/harvest.py downloads images (and OCR, manifests) once into item folders plus page records, the transcribe pipelines read those with --pages, pipelines/bind.py makes item texts and documents. An item's pages can land in different tasks; item-level steps are a second stage over item shards (--item-shards N writes OUT/pages/<shard>/<rank>, pipelines/bind.py reads whole shards), as datatrove's own multi-stage pipelines read per-bucket folders (pipelines).

docs.title: Broker
docs.text:
The broker is a shared folder through which workers across tasks, runs and machines agree on who uses which shared resource and what is unavailable until when. It is any datatrove DataFolder (a local folder, S3, any fsspec path) that every worker can reach: no server, no lock service, no queue. Workers write small JSON files, list the folder and read the modification times the storage reports. The code is linecaster.broker; proxies are the first kind of resource it coordinates (linecaster.net.proxies).

Terms are the glossary's: broker, lease, mark, worker identity (worker slot).

docs.title: Why
docs.text: A worker that keeps something to itself (a rate limiter, a list of blocked proxies) is right only if no other worker uses the same thing. Servers count requests per IP, so per proxy, and block per IP; a run has many workers (local processes, Ray tasks, HF Jobs) on several machines, and several runs may use the same proxies. The broker gives each proxy one owner at a time, so what the owner enforces for it holds for everyone, and makes a block that one worker found visible to whoever uses that proxy next.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
<broker>/
  broker.json                          {"format": "linecaster.broker/1", "created": ...}
  workers/<worker>.json                heartbeat: machine, slot, run, started, renewed
  slots/<machine>/<n>/leases/...       the worker slots of a machine
  <kind>/<resource id>/
    leases/<claimed>-<worker>.json     who holds it, since when
    marks/<scope>/<until>-<n>.json     what holds for it until when

The layout is versioned (broker.json's format) and neutral: a kind of resource is a folder name and its resources are ids, so a new kind needs no change of the protocol. File names are deterministic (times, worker ids, counters; no random parts).

Kind Resource id Leases Marks slots <machine>/<n> the process that is worker <machine>-<n> now none proxies a hash of the proxy's host and port (linecaster.net.proxies.proxy_id); no credential reaches the folder the worker that sends requests through the proxy a block at a host (scope: the host, until the block ends); a broken proxy (scope *, every host)

docs.title: Protocol
docs.text:
Liveness. A lease or a heartbeat is valid while its file was written within the lease time (LEASE_TTL, 180 s), by the modification time the storage lists. A worker renews every 60 s (RENEW_SECONDS): it rewrites its lease files and its heartbeat. A worker that crashes stops renewing, and its leases expire on their own. The age of a file is the reader's clock against the storage's, so the writers' clocks do not matter, and machines whose clocks are kept by NTP agree.

Claims. There is no exclusive create on object storage, so a claim is decided by listing:

  1. list the resource's leases/; if another worker's lease is valid, the claim fails (expired leases found on the way are deleted);
  2. write the own lease, <claimed>-<worker>.json, the claim's time in its name;
  3. list again: the earliest valid lease wins, by the time in its name, then by the worker id; a loser deletes its own lease.

Two workers that claim at once mostly both see both leases in step 3 and agree on the winner. When one listed before the other's write had landed (object storage takes a moment), both may believe they won; the next renew settles it: the holder whose lease is not the earliest valid one gives the resource up and logs at INFO worker X lost a claim race for proxies/<id> to Y; it takes another (a proxy pool then claims a replacement at once). A holder's lease keeps its claim time across renews, so it stays the earliest. A holder that went without a renew for longer than the lease time (a stalled process) finds at its next renew that its lease file is gone (deleted as expired by another worker) or older than the lease time; it gives the resource up and logs a WARNING, lease on proxies/<id> expired (no renew within the lease time).

Marks. A mark holds for a resource in a scope (a host, or * for every scope) for ttl seconds from its file's modification time. It is written once and never changed; whoever sees it expired deletes it, past its keep seconds if it has them: a mark with keep stays readable that long after its end, no longer holding, so its data (a proxy's doubling, last_wait) reaches whoever claims the resource next (linecaster.broker.Resource.last). A reader reads a mark's file once (it never changes) and keeps its end. The record is JSON: ttl, until (the end on the writer's clock, informational), worker, and the kind's data (status, last_wait, keep for proxies). A reader ignores the fields it does not know: a broker that does not know keep deletes a kept mark at its end (the doubling then starts again), and a mark without keep and last_wait is deleted at its end and starts the doubling at 60 s.

Fair share. Sharing them fairly (proxies with per_worker: share, the default), a worker holds ceil(free / live workers) resources of a kind (at least one if any is free), where the live workers are the valid heartbeats. Proxies count as free for a host when no mark blocks them there.

Worker identity. A worker is a datatrove worker slot of its machine, <machine>-<n>, not a process: on Ray every task is a new process, and the harvest runs one item per task, so leases tied to processes would change hands every few seconds. At its first use a process claims a free slot of its machine (slots/<machine>/<n>, a lease held by the process itself) and is that worker from then on. Its search starts at a slot of its own, so processes started together do not race for the same slots: the executor's worker index (linecaster.broker.set_worker_index: datatrove's local rank in a local run's pool, the rank modulo the tasks at once on Ray, the task's GPU in a multi-GPU Job), else a random place. From one listing of the machine's slots and one of the heartbeats it takes a handed-over slot first (a live heartbeat whose slot no process holds: its leases wait for a successor), then, with worker index k, the k-th free slot, then the free slots upward from there, past every valid lease. Free counts the slots not held since before this launch: those without a valid slot lease claimed more than a minute ago (SLOT_PEERS_SECONDS; a lease keeps its claim time across renews). The slots of a run stopped moments ago, whose leases are still valid, are left out of the count, so a relaunch takes the slots past them at one claim per process instead of racing upward through them; the slots its peers claimed meanwhile are not, so a pool whose processes look one after the other still takes slots 0 to n−1. Processes started together with distinct worker indexes need one claim each (tests/test_broker.py). A process that ends hands its slot over (Broker.hand_over: the slot's lease is deleted, the worker's other leases stay), and the next process on that machine claims that slot (handed-over slots come first), is the same worker, finds the worker's leases (named after it) and renews them. On Ray each task hands over at its end (linecaster.runtime.ray.RayExecutor); a local run's worker processes outlive their tasks and keep their slots, and a process that ends normally hands over at its exit. A slot whose process crashed expires like any lease, and so do the leases of a slot no process takes over.

docs.title: Proxies
docs.text:
A worker's proxy pool (linecaster.net.proxies.ProxyPool, used by linecaster.net.http.HTTPFetcher when a proxy list is set) works on the broker:

  • A fair share per worker (the default; an HTTP policy's proxies: {per_worker: share}). The worker claims at most 2 when it looks for proxies (FIRST_FILL) and grows toward its fair share of the proxies not blocked for its hosts at each check of its pool (every 10 s in use, REBALANCE_SECONDS, and after each renew; at most doubling each time), where it also gives back the ones beyond its share, those blocked for its hosts first. A worker that joins gets its part within seconds, one that leaves frees its part within the lease time, and the first workers of a launch do not take the proxies of those still starting. A few workers then use every proxy, which suits a run whose limit is not the proxies, such as one writing to object storage.
  • One proxy per worker (proxies: {per_worker: 1}). The worker claims one free proxy usable for the host it fetches, in an order of its own (so workers claiming at once try different proxies first), and sends every request through it. When the proxy is blocked or broken (below), the worker marks it, releases it and claims another free usable one at once. No fair share and no rebalancing: the host's rate limits per proxy are the worker's own. With several hosts, a worker whose proxy is blocked at one of them keeps it for the others and swaps it for a free proxy usable at every host it uses, if there is one. Using every proxy takes as many workers as proxies, which suits output on local disk or a short proxy list.
  • Up to N per worker (proxies: {per_worker: N}). As with one, the proxies claimed one by one: one when the worker holds none usable, then one more at each check of its pool, up to N and never more (more inherited from its slot's earlier process are given back).
  • Rate limits per proxy. With a proxy list the host's rate limits hold per proxy (per IP). The owner spaces the requests through a proxy to a host by the strictest limit and sends each request through the owned proxy whose turn comes first. One owner per proxy makes the limit hold across all workers and runs that share the broker.
  • Blocks. A status in the host's block_on (429 by default) and, with html there, an HTML page where another format was expected mark the proxy for that host (http): until the response's Retry-After, else for 60 s, twice the last wait on each repeat of that proxy at that host, at most the host's block_ttl (an hour by default). The mark records the status (429, html) and the doubling below. The owner stops using it there at once, and releases it once it is blocked for every host it uses; a worker that claims it later reads the mark with the claim, so no worker sends requests into another's block and starts the server's block window again. The request goes on through another proxy without counting as an attempt.
  • Broken proxies. A proxy error or no connection to the proxy, broken_after times in a row (3 by default), marks it for every host (*, status broken): first for broken_ttl (300 s), twice as long each time it breaks again before it carries an answer, at most block_ttl. Its doubling travels with the proxy as a block's does.
  • The doubling travels with the proxy. Each block or broken mark without Retry-After records its wait (last_wait; a mark with Retry-After the doubling's last wait unchanged) and is kept that long past its end (keep), so a worker that claims a released proxy continues the doubling where its last owner left it (60, 120, 240 s across workers) instead of starting at 60 s. While a worker holds a proxy it is the only one using it, so it keeps the doubling in memory from its claim on (and writes it into each mark). The doubling starts again at 60 s: after a successful response through the proxy from that host (any answer through it, for a broken proxy's), in that worker at once and for everyone else by deleting the proxy's ended marks there (in a thread; until then, or if that fails, the next owner doubles once more than it should, never less); or after a quiet period, when the next block comes more than its last wait after the last block there ended (linecaster.net.http.doubling; the kept mark is gone by then). An answer to a request sent before a block that still holds changes nothing. The rule is the direct path's too, where a worker keeps each host's doubling in memory. Why these two: a successful response is the only sure sign the host lets the IP in again, and the quiet period bounds how long a mark is kept, as long as the block before it, so a proxy that nobody tried for that long is not punished for an old episode.
  • No proxy usable. When every proxy the worker holds is blocked for a host and none is free to claim, the worker's requests to that host pause until a block it knows of ends or another worker gives a proxy back (it looks again at once when a block ends, else every 5 s, FILL_SECONDS) (one warning at the start, one at the end; the time is in the fetch records' pause_seconds). Once these waits since the host's last successful response would pass its max_pause (http), the run stops (StopRequests).

--broker PATH (or an HTTP policy's root key broker) names the folder; the default is OUT/logs/broker. Runs pointed at one path share the proxies and their blocks. A run's default worker count comes from the broker too (linecaster.runtime.run.allocate): from the proxies available at launch (the proxies in the file, less those with a live block or broken mark for the run's hosts and those leased by live workers of other runs, read with linecaster.broker.survey_kind), one per available proxy and at most one per CPU sharing them fairly, divided by N with per_worker 1 or N, and at most 64 with OUT on object storage (pipelines); on local and Ray runs only (on HF Jobs each worker is a Job, so a proxy list never sets their number).

docs.title: The command
docs.text:
linecaster broker reads and tidies a broker's folder (PATH: any fsspec path, e.g. OUT/logs/broker or s3://bucket/broker). The code is linecaster.broker.survey_all, clean and purge, usable from code with a now to judge liveness by.

Command Does linecaster broker status PATH [--json] from one listing: the format; the workers (machine, run, time since the last renew), live and stale; the worker slots per machine; per kind of resource how many there are, held by a live lease, held only by expired ones (stale), free, blocked per scope with the latest end, broken (*), and the expired marks. Ids only, no credential (proxies are hashes). --json: one JSON object with the same content linecaster broker clean PATH removes what has expired: heartbeats and leases (slots and resources) not renewed within the lease time, marks past their end and their keep (a kept mark holds a proxy's doubling). Safe while a run uses the broker linecaster broker clean PATH --leases also every heartbeat, slot lease and resource lease, live or not; the marks (blocks) stay linecaster broker clean PATH --marks also every mark, live, kept or not: blocked and broken proxies are tried again at once, and their doubling starts again at 60 s linecaster broker purge PATH resets the broker: removes every file of its layout, broker.json among them, so the next run starts as on an empty folder

clean and purge take --dry-run (list what would be removed, remove nothing) and -v (list each removed file); clean prints the counts per category otherwise. Confirmation: clean --leases or --marks that would remove something live (renewed within the lease time, a mark not expired), and purge always, list what they would remove and ask on a terminal; without one they refuse. --yes skips the question. Both refuse a folder that is not a broker's (clean: no broker.json of this format; purge: neither broker.json nor workers/ or slots/), and neither removes a file outside the broker's layout. Exit codes: 0 done (or nothing to do), 1 refused or aborted, 2 a usage error.

After a hard kill (kill -9, a crash, a local run whose worker processes are terminated) nothing hands over: the dead workers' heartbeats, slots and proxy leases look valid for up to the lease time (3 min). A run started again within that time gets new slot numbers, finds every proxy held and pauses until the leases expire. Once no process of the killed run is left, linecaster broker clean PATH --leases removes them, and the next run gets the slots of its worker indexes and claims the proxies at once; the blocks found before stay, so no worker sends requests into a block again. Add --marks only when the blocks themselves are wrong (a fixed proxy list, a host that lifted its block).

Which to use: plain clean any time, also as a cron job beside running workers (it only deletes what a worker would delete when it sees it); clean --leases after a hard kill; clean --leases --marks to start the proxies afresh while keeping the folder; purge to reset a broker completely (a test folder, a broker of an older format, a folder to hand over empty). clean --leases --marks and purge remove the same live files; purge also removes broker.json and the folders left empty.

docs.title: Guarantees and limits
docs.text:
• One owner per resource, as long as workers renew within the lease time. A worker stalled for longer than that (a frozen process, a storage outage) can briefly share a resource with the worker that claimed it meanwhile, until one of them renews and gives it up (at most a renew interval).
  • Per-proxy limits hold across workers, since only the owner sends requests through a proxy and it enforces the limits locally.
  • Liveness comes from storage modification times, compared with the reader's clock. The storage must list modification times (local folders and object stores do); a mark without one falls back to the end written in it.
  • Costs are listings and small writes: a renew rewrites the worker's leases and heartbeat and lists each kind it holds once a minute; a worker that looks for proxies lists the kind at most every 5 s (FILL_SECONDS), at once after it gave one up. Claims of many workers at once are spread by trying the free resources in an order of each worker's own, and slot claims by starting at each process's worker index.
  • What the broker does not do: no queue, no ordering of work, no exclusive create, no consistency stronger than the storage's own listings. Hugging Face buckets are not checked for the listing consistency the claims rely on.

docs.title: Future kinds (not implemented)
docs.text:
The same protocol fits other shared resources; these are examples, none of them exists:

  • direct/<machine>: a machine's own IP as a resource with its own rate limits and blocks, for direct connections.
  • servers/<endpoint>: a model server's capacity, leased by the workers that send it requests.
  • quotas/<host>: a host's request budget for a day, divided among workers.
  • items/<item id>: an item's work claimed by one worker at a time.

docs.title: The catalog: models, presets, recipes
docs.text:
The catalog describes every model Linecaster can run, how it runs it, and the tested combinations. Its entries live in one folder, src/linecaster/catalog/data/, shipped with linecaster; linecaster.catalog reads, validates and resolves them.

src/linecaster/catalog/data/
  models/<id>/model.yaml, model.md        # + upstream/<revision>/ (the upstream card, verbatim)
  presets/<step>/<id>.yaml, <id>.md       # one folder per step (STEPS)
  recipes/<id>.yaml, <id>.md
  catalog.lock
src/linecaster/catalog/schemas/<kind>-<n>.json    # generated from the Pydantic models

docs.title: What the catalog holds
docs.text:
The catalog and its docs are organized by five kinds: engines and pipelines (code, by versioned id) and three kinds of catalog entry (models, presets, recipes; a YAML file each).

Kind Is Named Lives in engine code that implements one step: runs a model, or applies rules versioned id: kraken.recognition.v1, typography.ratios.v1 engines/<engine>/ (a package each); chat.v1 and the rule-based engines in linecaster (linecaster.engines) model one upstream artifact at pinned revisions, with its card slug: kraken-ppocrv6-medium models/<id>/model.yaml preset an engine, a model pin and the engine's options, ready to use slug, with an edition: kraken-ppocrv6-medium@1 presets/<step>/<id>.yaml pipeline code: a shape with slots and the run-anywhere command line versioned id: transcribe_modular.v1 (the script's name) pipelines/<name>.py recipe a named combination: a pipeline, a preset edition per slot, options slug, with an edition: squiddle@1 recipes/<id>.yaml

Besides these: the lock (released editions) and the run record (OUT/run.yaml, and per page in each StepInfo: what a run resolved).

docs.title: Ids and versions
docs.text:
Term Whose Meaning Example version upstream what upstream calls it, verbatim, never parsed PP-OCRv6 medium, Chandra 2 revision upstream the exact identity of the files HF commit, version DOI, git commit, sha256 edition linecaster integer per preset or recipe, raised when outputs can change edition: 3 .v<n> linecaster the contract of an engine's options or a pipeline's slots and options transcribe_modular.v1 schema linecaster the format of a YAML file linecaster.preset/1 release linecaster the package version (run records only) 0.4.0
  • Slugs (models, presets, recipes): lowercase [a-z0-9.-]. They may contain upstream names (deepseek-ocr-2), never our versions. Ids are unique across presets and recipes, so a name means one thing.
  • Code ids (CODE_ID): lowercase dotted names ending in .v<n>. An incompatible change is a new id (.v2); the old one stays registered. Adding an option is compatible when its default keeps the old behavior; changing a default, removing or renaming an option is not.
  • A reference is id@edition; id alone means the current edition. Run records always store the explicit edition and its hash.
  • A tag or branch is resolved to a commit when a model is pinned; the tag is kept as tag: for information. Zenodo: the version DOI identifies the files, the concept DOI is information. Downloads without a commit: the file's sha256 is the revision.

docs.title: Files
docs.text:
A model, preset or recipe is a YAML file, the data, validated strictly by linecaster.catalog.schema (unknown keys are errors), and a Markdown file of the same name next to it, the prose for people (why these settings, limitations, changes), without front matter. Tools read only the YAML; the docs generator also includes the prose. The prose is optional, except for presets and recipes with support: core. The lock is YAML only, and so is an evidence record (kept outside the catalog, below). Bulk data (page records, exports) is JSON Lines or Parquet, not catalog data.

Format Schema id JSON Schema model linecaster.model/1 schemas/model-1.json preset linecaster.preset/1 schemas/preset-1.json recipe linecaster.recipe/1 schemas/recipe-1.json evidence (not catalog data; its schema ships here) linecaster.evidence/1 schemas/evidence-1.json lock linecaster.lock/2 schemas/lock-2.json run record (OUT/run.yaml, not catalog data; its schema ships here) linecaster.run-record/1 schemas/run-record-1.json

Every YAML file names its format twice: its first line is # yaml-language-server: $schema=<relative path to src/linecaster/catalog/schemas/<kind>-<n>.json> (for editors), and its field schema holds the schema id (for tools). The JSON Schemas are generated from the Pydantic models (linecaster catalog schemas); the test suite fails when a committed one differs from a fresh one.

YAML has 1.2 semantics, read with ruamel.yaml through linecaster.catalog.yamlio: only true / false are booleans (NO stays Norwegian), and a duplicate key is an error. Values that look like numbers or versions are quoted ("1.0"). Commands that write a file back (release, pin) keep its comments.

docs.title: Model (models/<id>/model.yaml)
docs.text:
Field Meaning id, version our slug; upstream's name, verbatim source kind (hf, zenodo, git, url) and ref (repo id, concept DOI, repository URL, download URL) pins one entry per upstream revision: revision, tag, doi, pinned (date), files (name → sha256:<hex>), card, card_sha256, license_file license SPDX id where there is one, else the license's own name languages, scripts ISO 639-3 (mul for many), ISO 15924 params parameter count, as upstream states it derived_from ref and relation (mirror, converted, quantized, finetuned)

The upstream card is always copied, verbatim, at the pinned revision, whatever its license: Hugging Face README.md, the HTRMoPo record, a repository README; a separate license file next to it. Its sha256 is in the pin. Cards are never edited; license, languages and scripts in model.yaml are taken from them where they say. A new upstream revision is a new entry in pins, with its own upstream/<revision>/ folder. Model entries are written by linecaster catalog pin.

docs.title: Preset (presets/<step>/<id>.yaml)
docs.text: Field Meaning id, edition, step the step must match the folder model id and revision of a model pin submodels further pins of a multi-model engine, by role engine the engine's id: engine: kraken.recognition.v1 options the engine's options (its Options model) settings prompts, sampling and other request settings (chat presets) labels native layout label → DoclingDocument label; unmapped labels are text by_script a by-script engine's strategies: ISO 15924 script code → preset id@edition of the same step, and "*" → the default for every other script (required) serve the server it was validated with: server (vllm, sglang, linecaster, vendor), version, image (with digest, for HF Jobs), flags, env, revision_flag, pin_ignore, server_packages, draft (speculative decoding); a vendor's service also command, health, weights_dir (page engines) capabilities unit (line, region, page, item) and produces (the parts it adds, vocabulary PARTS) provenance derived_from (sources of the settings, each at a commit or revision), authored_by, created support, superseded_by see Support

docs.title: Recipe (recipes/<id>.yaml)
docs.text:
Field Meaning id, edition pipeline the pipeline it fills: pipeline: transcribe_modular.v1 presets slot → preset id@edition (always an explicit edition) options the pipeline's options, by name provenance, support, superseded_by as for presets

A derivative's recipe lives in this catalog too (squiddle); the derivative names it by id.

docs.title: Measurements live elsewhere
docs.text:
linecaster is not a data repository: the catalog holds no measurements, and neither do the docs. An evaluation (a derivative's, an evaluation project's) keeps its own records, in its own repository, and names what it measured by edition and hash. linecaster provides the format and the tooling to produce them:

  • The evidence format (linecaster.evidence/1, linecaster.catalog.Evidence, schemas/evidence-1.json): one measurement per file, preset: id@edition or recipe: id@edition, context (for a preset measured inside a pipeline: the rest of it), source (own-run, card-claim, vendor-benchmark), dataset (repo@revision, or a description for claims), metrics, date, hardware, software (linecaster commit, server version, backend: in-process or served), run, notes. Claims are never measurements.
  • What a measurement names: the run record (OUT/run.yaml: the recipe edition and its hash, every block's parameters, pipeline_sha256) and the recipe and preset editions stamped on every step of every page.
  • What it measures: the page records (every transcription with its steps' measurements: seconds, tokens, device), the traces (linecaster traces OUT: time per block and page) and the per-page and per-item files.
  • Ground truth and reference transcriptions: ManifestReader(existing_ocr=True) and the TranscriptionConverter read a library's own ALTO, PAGE-XML, hOCR or text into a named transcription (ocr_original, ground_truth, ...) of the page record, next to ocr_new; the writers turn page records into datasets (JSON Lines or Parquet page records, ALTO, PAGE-XML, hOCR, text).

Scoring (CER and the like) is the evaluation's own; linecaster has no scorer.

docs.title: Released editions are immutable
docs.text:
linecaster catalog release <id> writes the current edition's resolved functional content and its sha256 into catalog.lock (per entry: sha256, previous_sha256 where a catalog migration changed it (a list, oldest first, after several), released, linecaster commit, resolved; a recipe edition also pipeline and pipeline_sha256, below).

  • A preset's functional content is what can change outputs: step, the model pin and every submodel pin (id, revision, files), engine, options, settings, labels, by_script (each strategy's edition with that edition's hash, as a recipe names its presets) and serve. A by-script preset is released only on released strategies. Only what the YAML file states counts, so a new optional schema field changes no hash. The Markdown prose, provenance, support level and capabilities are not part of it.
  • A recipe's functional content is its pipeline, each slot's preset edition with that edition's hash and the options it states. A recipe is released only on released preset editions, so one recipe edition pins a whole run down to the weights' files.

linecaster catalog verify (and tests/catalog/test_catalog.py) fails when a released edition's content changed; such a change is a new edition. Old editions stay resolvable from the lock after the file moves on. Unreleased editions are drafts.

docs.title: A recipe edition's expanded pipeline
docs.text:
A recipe names a pipeline id, presets and options; what runs is the pipeline its script builds from them. The lock keeps that too: release builds the recipe's pipeline (its pipeline script with --recipe id@edition on placeholder folders, in-process, one task) and records pipeline, every block with its class and its functional parameters (engines with their options, presets with their hashes; pipelines), and its pipeline_sha256, the hash a run record of that recipe names. verify builds every released recipe edition's pipeline again and reports drift: a block, a parameter or a default that changed in code changes the hash, and verify names the blocks that differ.

Building it needs no engine: the describe mode (linecaster.runtime.run.describe) builds the recipe's pipeline shape (linecaster.pipelines) in the current process, and blocks and backends import no engine before warm_up(); a preset whose engine is not installed names the engine's class from the repository's engine packages (catalog.code). So verify runs in the core environment, and its hash is the one a run of the pipeline script with its engines records.

Drift is resolved like any change of a released edition: a change that can change outputs gives the recipe a new edition; a change of the code that keeps behavior (a renamed parameter, a new option whose default keeps the old behavior) is recorded anew with linecaster catalog release <id> --migrate-pipeline. A recipe edition released before pipelines were locked gets its pipeline on its next release (a catalog migration: the edition and its sha256 stay). The lock format stays linecaster.lock/2: the two fields are optional, and only recipe entries have them.

docs.title: Catalog migrations
docs.text: A change of the catalog's own vocabulary or format that keeps every output as it was (a renamed step, a renamed pipeline id, a new file format) is a catalog migration: every released edition keeps its number, its resolved content is rewritten in the new terms and its hash recomputed, and the hash it had before stays in the lock as previous_sha256 (after a second migration a list of both, oldest first). A run record names id@edition and that edition's hash at the time; it resolves by either hash (Catalog.resolve(ref, sha256=...), resolve_recipe, by_sha256, linecaster catalog show sha256:<hex>). A change that can change outputs is never a migration: it is a new edition. A recipe that comes to name, as presets, what its pipeline already ran (squiddle@1 naming the rule-based presets its pipeline ran through the option text: reflow) is a migration too: the pipeline it expands to is the same blocks with the same parameters, so the edition keeps its number, and catalog release --migrate-pipeline records the expanded pipeline again (the recipe stamp carries the new hash).

docs.title: Steps, capabilities, labels
docs.text:
Steps (STEPS): layout, lines, recognition, tables, formulas, whose engines run models, and the rule-based steps (RULE_STEPS) image (the working image), normalization (character fidelity: as written → normalized), typography (the hierarchy from type sizes), recomposition (running text from the rows: paragraphs) and composition (the document). Recognition reads a unit (capabilities.unit): line (kraken, PaddleX, Tesseract), region (a VLM per layout region) or page (a VLM or a page engine reads the whole page: a page preset, which launch.py runs by name); a rule-based engine reads a page or an item (the pages of one item, in order). OCRD_STEPS maps the steps to OCR-D's functional steps for METS agents where OCR-D has one (image: preprocessing/optimization, typography: layout/segmentation/classification, composition: layout/analysis); the others are post-processing (recognition/post-correction).

What depends on the code belongs to the engine (capabilities on the class), e.g. kraken's word boxes with confidences. What depends on the weights belongs to the model or preset: languages, scripts, output format.

docs.title: Engines
docs.text:
An engine is a class registered under its id in the entry-point group linecaster.engines ("kraken.recognition.v1" = "linecaster_kraken:KrakenRecognitionEngine"), or one of linecaster's own (BUILTIN_ENGINES): chat.v1 (VLM presets, served only: SERVED_ONLY; the Chat backend), the single-region layout and the rule-based engines. It declares engine_id, step, Options (a Pydantic model whose fields have descriptions; the docs come from it) and capabilities, and takes the pin as weights (and submodel_weights), fetched and checked by linecaster.catalog.fetch. Engine packages carry code only; their presets and models are in this catalog.

Engine packages (engines/<engine>/: linecaster-kraken, linecaster-paddlex, linecaster-tesseract, linecaster-indra, linecaster-surya, linecaster-services) have versions of their own and a range of linecaster releases they work with (linecaster>=0.1,<0.6), and import from linecaster only the data model (linecaster.data) and the engine API (linecaster.engines.api): the Engine protocol, Capabilities, and the weight helpers weights_of (a model pin as weights), hf_file and hf_snapshot (a Hugging Face pin's files, checked) and model_entry (a model's catalog entry); tests/test_import_rule.py reads the packages with ast and fails on any other import. They are not on PyPI: a preset whose engine is not installed is a CatalogError that names the package that provides it and the pipeline scripts whose environments install it (catalog.code.install_hint). Each package has its tests in engines/<engine>/tests/ (conformance through linecaster.testing.check_engine, and its own units), run in an environment that has it (uv run tests/test_engines_catalog.py engines/<engine>/tests; the page engines' packages: uv run tests/test_page_engines_catalog.py engines/<engine>/tests, the environment of pipelines/transcribe_page.py).

docs.title: Page engines and their services
docs.text:
A page engine is an engine of the recognition step whose unit is the page (capabilities.unit: page): it gets the page image and returns the page's transcription, text-only, its raw output verbatim in extra["raw"], as a chat preset's completion is kept. PageRecognizer runs it like any model block (InProcess, or Served through linecaster serve); pipelines/transcribe_page.py is its pipeline. Where the engine talks to a service, its preset's serve block names it and ServiceServer starts it in the task:

serve.server The service Fields vllm vllm serve <the model pin, fetched> --host --port <flags> --served-model-name <the Hugging Face id>, for an engine package that attaches to vLLM (surya.recognition.v1) version, image, flags vendor a vendor's page pipeline in its own image (falcon.recognition.v1, oxr.recognition.v1): the image's entrypoint image (by digest), command (the entrypoint), env, health (loopback URLs that must answer 200, in order), weights_dir (where the model pin is downloaded first, when the image reads the weights from a folder)

The engine's endpoint option (where its service is) is operational: presets leave it to its default (the service's loopback port), a pipeline sets it for a running service (--recognition-endpoint), and the pipeline's hash leaves it out.

docs.title: The single-region layout
docs.text: layout.single-region.v1 (linecaster.engines:SingleRegionLayoutEngine, preset single-region@1) is a layout engine without a model: one region covering the page image (label text, id page, reading order 0; both options), recorded as a layout step. It has the model engines' call (__call__(image, transcription)), so LayoutDetector("single-region@1") runs it, and like the rule-based engines it is built in and runs in the pipeline's process only. pipelines/transcribe_modular.py --layout single-region reads a page as one region.

docs.title: Rule-based engines
docs.text:
The engines of the rule-based steps (strategies) live in linecaster.engines, are pure Python and run in the pipeline's process only (IN_PROCESS_ONLY; linecaster serve refuses them): image.webp-lossless.v1, normalization.latin-historic.v1, typography.ratios.v1, recomposition.unicode.v1, composition.docling.v1, and the by-script engines normalization.by-script.v1 and recomposition.by-script.v1. Each has no weights; its Options turn the rules' thresholds into options whose defaults are the values the rules have always had, and it declares scripts: the ISO 15924 scripts it covers (Latn, Hebr, ...), "*" for all. The rules themselves stay in linecaster.text, linecaster.images and linecaster.formats; the engines are thin.

The call per unit (linecaster.engines.base): page unit __call__(t: Transcription, **options) -> Transcription; item unit __call__(pages: list[Transcription], **options) -> list[Transcription] (an item's pages in order; a page is an item of one page); the image step takes and returns the image's bytes (__call__(data, **options) -> (bytes, info)). Options given to a call override the engine's for that call. Each records a StepInfo with its engine id, its options as settings and its counts as measurements; the block that runs it adds the preset edition and its hash, seconds and datetime. The item unit of the composition is item_document(pages, name, ...): an item's document is no transcription.

Their blocks take a preset (id@edition) or an engine spec (InProcess("module:Class", **options)), with options over either, like model blocks but without a backend choice: ImageConverter(output_folder, preset) (image), CharacterNormalizer(preset) (normalization), Typographer(preset) (typography), Recomposer(preset, unit="page"|"item") (recomposition), Composer(preset, unit="page"|"item") (composition). The presets of the squiddle recipe's rules: working-image@1, latin-historic@1, ratios@1, unicode-recomposition@1, docling-composition@1. Running text or the page as laid out is the presence of a Recomposer: the Composer composes from paragraphs when there are, else from lines (diplomatic composition).

docs.title: Scripts and dispatch
docs.text:
A preset whose engine is a by-script engine names its strategies in by_script: an ISO 15924 code per script that needs its own rules, "*" for every other script.

id: hebrew-latin-recomposition
step: recomposition
engine: recomposition.by-script.v1
by_script:
  Hebr: hebrew-recomposition@1
  "*": unicode-recomposition@1

engine_spec resolves them into the engine's strategies (each strategy's engine, options, edition and hash). The engine (ScriptDispatch) routes each decision to the strategy of the script around it: for a decision at a row end (a division mark, the separator between two rows) the script of the last character before the row end that has one, else of the first after it (characters of the scripts Common and Inherited, such as spaces, hyphens, digits and combining marks, have none); for a normalization, each run of a text in one script (Common and Inherited characters stay with the run before them). A script without a strategy of its own goes to "*". Scripts are Unicode's Script property, matched with the regex package's \p{Script=...}. verify checks that every strategy is an edition of the same step and covers its script.

docs.title: Pipelines, recipes and launch.py
docs.text:
Every pipeline script declares PIPELINE, its id: its file name with .v<n> (harvest.v1, transcribe_modular.v1, transcribe_vlm.v1, transcribe_page.v1, bind.v1). A script with slots also declares SLOTS (slot → option; the option is the step's name: --layout, --lines, --recognition, ...; the rule-based steps are slots too: transcribe_modular.v1 has --typography, --recomposition, --normalization (the readable item texts' normalization, for --item-texts) and --composition, bind.v1 --recomposition, --normalization and --composition; a slot left empty leaves its step out, e.g. no recomposition: the page stays as laid out). It has no default presets: the user fills every slot, or names a recipe (--recipe id[@edition]), with single flags on top recorded as overrides in the run record (recipe: the edition, the pipeline id, the hash and the overrides).

The recipes: squiddle (transcribe_modular.v1: PP-DocLayoutV3, PP-OCRv6 line detection and kraken's PP-OCRv6 recognition, tables, formulas and the rule-based steps; its recognition is kraken's, which pipelines/transcribe_modular.py leaves out, so it runs in an environment that adds kraken (a derivative's script), or with --backend served --endpoint against a server started from one) and item-texts (bind.v1: unicode-recomposition@1, latin-historic@1, docling-composition@1, the item stage's default combination).

uv run launch.py NAME IMAGES OUT [options] launches a recipe or a page preset by name: it finds the script whose PIPELINE the recipe names (transcribe_vlm.v1 for chat page presets, transcribe_page.v1 for page engines' presets) and runs it in that script's own environment with --recipe or --recognition. serve and ray pass through for recipes. A preset that is one step of a pipeline gets a hint instead: the pipeline, the flag and the recipes that use it.

docs.title: Support
docs.text: core (maintained, validated), experimental (works, may change), legacy (kept resolvable; superseded_by: names the replacement).

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Command Does linecaster models [--step STEP] lists the presets (and the recipes) linecaster catalog pin ID --hf REPO [--revision REV] pins a Hugging Face model: model entry, card, file hashes linecaster catalog pin ID --github OWNER/NAME --revision COMMIT --file F [--tag T] pins files of a GitHub repository linecaster catalog release ID [--commit SHA] [--migrate-pipeline] freezes the current edition of a preset or recipe in the lock, a recipe with its expanded pipeline linecaster catalog verify checks the files (schema lines, prose next to its YAML file), the JSON Schemas against the models, cards, pins, released editions and their hashes, recipes and their expanded pipelines linecaster catalog show REF the resolved functional content of a preset or recipe edition (id@edition, or a hash, today's or a previous one), with its hash linecaster catalog schemas [--out DIR] regenerates the JSON Schemas (default src/linecaster/catalog/schemas/) linecaster docs [--out docs] [--readme README.md] writes the generated docs (the catalog's pages among them; not in git, written before the site is built)

The catalog's generated pages are grouped by kind: docs/catalog/{engines, models, presets/<step>, pipelines, recipes}/ and an index. Engine and pipeline pages are read from the source (linecaster.catalog.code, with ast), so the engines need not be installed. The pages quote no measurements.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: What linecaster keeps stable for derivatives, pipelines and stored outputs, and how a change that breaks it is announced. Terms are the glossary's.

docs.title: What counts as a breaking change
docs.text:
A change is breaking when code, a command line, a stored file or a catalog reference that worked before stops working or starts to mean something else:

Surface Breaking Not breaking blocks a block renamed or removed; a constructor argument renamed, removed or made required; a default that changes what a run writes a new block; a new argument whose default keeps the old behavior backends InProcess, Served, Chat renamed or removed, or an argument as for blocks a new argument with a default that keeps the old behavior commands and flags a linecaster command or a pipeline script's option renamed, removed, or given another meaning or default a new command or option pipeline ids and slots a pipeline id or a slot renamed or removed, a slot's step changed a new pipeline script; a new slot that can stay empty page records and item records a field renamed, removed or given another meaning; a schema id (linecaster.page/2) whose records a reader no longer reads a new optional field; a new schema version that PageRecordReader reads together with the older ones the run layout a folder or file name under OUT (pages/, rejects/, logs/, traces/, run.yaml) or its format changed a new file or folder the catalog a catalog id (model, preset, recipe) renamed or removed; a released edition changed; the lock format changed without a migration a new entry or edition; a catalog migration that keeps every output engines an engine id removed; an option renamed or removed, or a default changed (a new code id, .v2, instead) a new engine; a new option whose default keeps the old behavior (the same id)

Internal modules and names with a leading underscore, log messages, stats and the generated docs are not part of it.

docs.title: While the version is 0.x
docs.text: There is no deprecation period and there are no aliases: a breaking change takes effect in the release that makes it, and every breaking change is an upgrade note in CHANGELOG.md (what changed, who is affected, what to do), listed first.

docs.title: Versions and releases
docs.text:
Versions follow semantic versioning, with the 0.x convention that the minor number does what the major one does from 1.0 on. What a change bumps follows from the table above:

Change While 0.x From 1.0 fixes, performance, corrections of the docs, dependency updates that change no output patch patch new blocks, options, presets, recipes, commands or features that keep the old behavior patch minor breaking (any surface above; it needs an upgrade note) minor, collected (0.4.0 → 0.5.0) major

A release bumps by its largest change; patches are the rule. Ranges such as the engine packages' linecaster>=0.1,<0.6 then hold: every release inside them keeps what worked.

  • Breaking changes are collected, not released one by one. They are made on a branch and released together as one minor when a coherent piece of work is finished, or when the maintainer asks for one. main carries only patch-level changes, so a fix can go out as a patch at any time.
  • A minor needs something users must change: its upgrade notes name it. A release with nothing to change is a patch.
  • When: at the end of a finished piece of work, once it is merged into main and CI is green; one release per piece of work, not per commit. A commit that changes only the README is no release; other docs wait for the next release unless they correct something wrong.
  • How: the version in pyproject.toml and linecaster.__version__ (tests/test_version.py checks they agree), CHANGELOG.md's Unreleased section as ## <version> (<date>), the scripts relocked, an annotated tag v<version>, pushed (the docs workflow publishes <major>.<minor>). A minor bump while 0.x (a major one from 1.0) also widens the engine packages' linecaster range to the next one and bumps each engine package's patch version.
  • Engine packages version on their own by the same table, applied to their engines (ids, options, defaults).
  • A derivative versions by its own interface, not by linecaster's numbers: moving to a linecaster release that leaves what the derivative documents unchanged is a patch for it.
  • 1.0.0 is the maintainer's decision: from then on breaking changes get a deprecation period. No release reaches it on its own.

docs.title: Released catalog editions
docs.text: A released edition never changes (catalog): a change that can change outputs is a new edition, and the old one stays resolvable from the lock. A catalog migration (a change of the catalog's vocabulary or format that keeps every output) recomputes an edition's hash and keeps the old one as previous_sha256, so run records written before it still resolve. Engine and pipeline code ids follow the same rule: an incompatible change of options or slots is a new id, and the old one stays registered.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text: Rules that hold across the repository. Each rule is followed by its reason. Terms are the glossary's.

docs.title: Names
docs.text:
