What Pattern Examples block <Object><RoleNoun>; readers and writers <Object><Format>Reader / Writer LineRecognizer, Typographer, Composer, Binder, ManifestReader, PageJsonlWriter composite block <Purpose><RoleNoun> ModularTranscriber block base classes <Kind>Block PageBlock, ModelBlock, RuleBlock engine class <Provider><Step>Engine KrakenRecognitionEngine, UnicodeRecompositionEngine engine id <provider>.<step>.v<n> kraken.recognition.v1, recomposition.unicode.v1 VLM adapter <Model>Adapter ChandraOCRAdapter pipeline script a verb, <verb>[_<kind>].py harvest.py, transcribe_modular.py, transcribe_vlm.py, transcribe_page.py, bind.py pipeline id the script's file name, .v<n> transcribe_modular.v1 slot and its flag the step's name --layout, --lines, --recognition catalog step a noun for the activity layout, recognition, recomposition transcription names ocr_new, ocr_original, ground_truth, or <source>

Reason: one pattern makes names guessable, and role nouns say what a block is in a pipeline. Pipeline scripts are verbs because they are what one runs.

docs.title: Spelling
docs.text:
American English everywhere: code, flags, docs, commit messages (normalize, recognizer, behavior, license, color, catalog). Upstream text copied verbatim (model cards) keeps its spelling.

Reason: one spelling for everything typed, matching Python and its ecosystem.

docs.title: YAML and Markdown
docs.text:
• Data that tools read is YAML; prose for people is Markdown. A catalog entry is <id>.yaml, optionally with <id>.md next to it; tools never read the Markdown. Reason: Markdown renders cleanly, data validates, and diffs of the two do not mix.
  • Every YAML file names its format twice: a first line # yaml-language-server: $schema=<relative path to src/linecaster/catalog/schemas/<kind>-<n>.json> (editors validate and complete) and a field schema: linecaster.<kind>/<n> (tools check it). Reason: mistakes show while editing, not at run time.
  • The schemas are generated from the pydantic models (model_json_schema()) into src/linecaster/catalog/schemas/ (shipped with the package; linecaster catalog schemas rewrites them), and a test fails when a committed schema differs from a fresh one. The pydantic models are the only source of truth. Reason: one definition, used by tools and editors alike.
  • YAML is YAML 1.2, read with ruamel.yaml: true/false are the only booleans (NO stays a string), duplicate keys are errors, and tools that write files back keep their comments.
  • An edition's hash covers its functional content (what changes behavior: step, engine, options, pins, settings, labels, serving), read from the YAML. The Markdown prose and descriptive fields (support, provenance) are not part of it, so they can be corrected without a new edition; git keeps their history.

Schemas: preset, recipe, model, evidence, run-record, lock. Stored page records name their format in a schema field of their row (linecaster.page/2).

docs.title: Docstrings
docs.text:
Google style, checked by tests/test_docstrings.py (with ast, no extra tool) for every public block, built-in engine, backend, serializer, build, run_pages, runtime.run.main, public function of linecaster.catalog and public name of linecaster.engines.api and linecaster.testing:

  • Summary line: what the block or function does, in the present tense, starting with a verb, one sentence: "Recognizes the text of every line with its engine." It may wrap; it ends at the first blank line. The block index and the README's block table show it.
  • Body: the contract in words (what it reads, adds and replaces), edge cases, what it records (step infos, stats, errors on the page).
  • Args: names every parameter of the signature (a class documents its constructor's), and no other: one entry each, name: meaning, the effect of the default, constraints., continuation lines indented. Several parameters may share an entry (data_folder, paths_file, ...: datatrove's BaseDiskReader arguments.), as datatrove's inherited reader and writer arguments do; **kwargs is an entry too. A class that keeps its base's constructor keeps its base's Args:.
  • Example: (indented Python code) is required for runtime.run.main, build(), the serializers (to_alto, from_alto, ...) and the public functions of linecaster.catalog; optional for blocks, whose generated pages show it.
  • Inline code in double or single backticks; the generated pages render both as code. Engine options are described in their Options model (Field(description=...)), not in a docstring.

Reason: the generated block pages come from the docstrings, so the reference is only as good as they are, and a test keeps them complete as signatures change.

docs.title: Contracts
docs.text:
• Every block declares its unit and what it reads, adds and replaces (pipelines). A part of the record is added by one block only, unless a later block declares that it replaces it. Reason: the builder can then check a pipeline before it runs and derive its graph.
  • Blocks are pure transforms of their unit; only readers and writers know about tasks, ranks and files. Reason: the same blocks run on any executor and in run_pages().

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
• Every built-in engine passes linecaster.testing.check_engine and every public block check_block (tests/testing/test_conformance.py); an engine package checks its engines the same way in engines/<engine>/tests/. Reason: the protocol and the contracts hold for every implementation, not only the ones a pipeline happens to run.
  • A test that needs a CUDA device is marked gpu, one that downloads weights or reaches the internet network, one over about 10 s slow (--strict-markers). Reason: the default run skips what a machine cannot run, and CI runs what a CPU can.
  • Tests use the fake engines, the fake chat server and the fake service of linecaster.testing, not copies of their own. Reason: one fake per step behaves the same in every test.

docs.title: Tracing
docs.text:
• Tracing (OpenTelemetry) is always on. Spans per task always; spans per page for a sample chosen by page id, plus every page that failed. Reason: where a run loses time is only visible per page and across processes.
  • A page carries its trace context from the reader on; blocks open spans as children of the page's context, never of "the current span". Reason: pages are interleaved in the stream.
  • Attributes are identifiers and numbers under linecaster.*, never content (text, images). Reason: content belongs in the rows, which the page id links to.
  • Traces are written to OUT/traces/ and, when the standard OTEL_* variables are set, exported to a backend (tracing).

docs.title: Telemetry
docs.text: linecaster sends nothing to anyone that the user did not configure. No usage data, no phoning home, not even opt-in. Reason: libraries and archives run it on their own infrastructure under their own rules.

docs.title: Logging
docs.text: loguru (datatrove's), with {placeholder} templates and named values, never formatted strings: logger.warning("page {page_id} failed in {block}: {error}", page_id=..., block=..., error=...) (the values land in the record's extra). JSON lines on Jobs: the pipeline scripts set LINECASTER_LOG_JSON=1 in their Jobs, where the tasks (linecaster.runtime.jobs.JobsExecutor) and linecaster serve log with loguru's serialize=True (linecaster.runtime.logs). Log records carry trace_id and span_id. Reason: logs can be filtered and joined to traces.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: Library code raises the classes of linecaster.errors (PipelineConfigError, CatalogError, PageError, ServerError, all LinecasterError), never SystemExit; only the command line (linecaster, a pipeline script's main) turns them into exit codes, and a test fails on any other exit. Pure functions of the data model, the formats and the text transforms keep Python's own ValueError for a wrong argument. Reason: a derivative that embeds linecaster can catch what went wrong, and a run's exit code says whether anything was launched.

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text: A credential is never a value in a pipeline: it is an EnvVar("NAME") (linecaster.runtime.secrets), read in the task. Reason: datatrove pickles the pipeline for every executor, and the run record lists every block's parameters.

docs.title: Changes
docs.text: CHANGELOG.md in the Keep a Changelog format, with upgrade notes first. NOTES.md is the log of measurements and decisions; reference documents (docs/reference/) describe what is, without history.

docs.title: The data model
docs.text: linecaster.data holds what a page's text recognition produces; linecaster.data.page the page record it travels in. Importing either needs neither datatrove nor saturate nor an engine.

docs.title: Classes
docs.text: Class Is Key Item any multi-page unit: book, issue, manuscript, file item_id Page one page record: the page image and its named transcriptions page_id = item_id + sequence PageImage the image's location, size, format and hashes Transcription OCR, HTR or ground truth of one page Text one text per item and variant (linecaster.text.variants)

docs.title: A page in a pipeline
docs.text: A page is one datatrove Document: id is the page id, text the primary transcription's text, media[0] the image bytes, metadata["page"] the page record.

docs.title: Transcription
docs.text:
Part Holds regions the layout: id, label (a DoclingDocument label), raw_label (the producer's), polygon, bbox, score, reading_order, heading_level, extra lines id, region_id, reading_order, row, bbox, polygon, baseline, score, text, normalized, confidence, alternatives, words, extra paragraphs the running text recomposed from the rows (Paragraph, below), in reading order docling the page's composed DoclingDocument, as docling-core dumps it language steps one StepInfo per step that worked on it, in order (below) source kind (produced, converted, ground_truth), format, uri, image size derived text (as written, as laid out, full page; tables as Markdown), confidence (line confidences weighted by length)
  • regions are the contract between steps. Lines and recognizers need the layout (label, polygon, reading order, score) long before a DoclingDocument can be built, so regions are a primary part next to lines; docling is composed from regions, lines and tables. Region ids are the producer's own (PP-DocLayout: <raw label>_<index>; rows outside every region: orphan_<n>); lines refer to them with region_id.
  • Words are the finest level; there is no glyph level. Engines with character positions turn them into words by the engine's own rule (kraken: split at whitespace, a word's box the bounding box of its cuts).
  • A line's text is None until a recognizer ran; an empty string is a line recognized as empty. Its normalized is None until the CharacterNormalizer ran; text is never overwritten.
  • Text-only transcriptions (a delivered plain text) are lines without geometry (bbox and polygon None), one per text line, source.kind = "converted", source.format = "text". They cannot be written as ALTO, PAGE or hOCR.

docs.title: Steps (StepInfo)
docs.text:
Every step that worked on a transcription adds one StepInfo, model steps and rule-based steps alike:

Field Holds step the step: layout, lines, recognition, tables, formulas, unicode, typography, recomposition, normalization, composition, ... name the model (kraken-ppocrv6-medium, PP-DocLayoutV3); for a step without a model, what ran (unicodedata, retyper, the engine's id) engine the engine's code id (kraken.recognition.v1, typography.ratios.v1); None for a step no engine ran (unicode) revision the model's revision preset, preset_sha256 the preset edition it ran as, and its hash recipe, recipe_sha256 the recipe edition the run followed, and its hash (RecipeStamper) backend in-process, or served with the server's address settings what decided the output besides the preset: the engine's options, a VLM's prompt and sampling measurements numbers of this page, in the measurements vocabulary (below)

The model blocks and linecaster serve fill engine from the engine's engine_id, preset from the backend, and seconds and datetime. The page files (ALTO, PAGE, hOCR) carry every field but measurements (datetime aside) and read them back (serialization).

docs.title: Measurements
docs.text:
linecaster.data.MEASUREMENTS is the vocabulary of StepInfo.measurements, key → meaning; linecaster code writes no other key (a test reads the code for every place that writes one). Values vary from run to run.

Key Meaning seconds wall time of the step on the page (the engine's call, in-process or in the server) datetime when the step started on the page, ISO 8601 in UTC device the device the step ran on prompt_tokens, completion_tokens a VLM's tokens, summed over the page's requests finish_reason why generation stopped: stop, length, content_filter, tool_calls, function_call, abort (FINISH_REASONS), or None regions, failed regions sent to a VLM one by one, and those whose request failed tables, formulas table regions given a structure, formula regions read changed strings a normalization changed body_size, leveled, demoted, split, drop_capitals, numbers_dropped typography: the body type size in pixels, headings given a level, section headers made text, headlines split off, drop capitals joined, page numbers removed paragraphs, continuations, marks_removed, marks_kept recomposition: paragraphs made, paragraphs continued into the next region or page, division marks removed, hyphens kept

A new key is added to the vocabulary before code writes it. Page records of other producers are read with whatever keys they carry (unknown_measurements lists them).

docs.title: Paragraphs (Paragraph)
docs.text:
Running text recomposed from the rows of one region (the Recomposer), with the decisions that made it.

Field Holds id, region_id <region id>_p<n>, and the region rows one ParagraphRow per visual row with text: lines (the ids of every line on the row, as Line.row groups them, empty ones too) and start, end (the row's characters in text) text as written, flowed: the rows joined, the division marks the recomposition removed gone normalized the same text normalized (the CharacterNormalizer), else None continues, continues_from the paragraph it runs on into, and the one it continues (ParagraphRef: id, and page_id for a paragraph on another page of the item) decisions Decisions: kind and reason (DECISIONS), row (the index into rows), separator (for a continuation: what joins it to the paragraph it runs on into)

The rows are what a document's provenance needs: an item made from a paragraph has one provenance entry per row, whose box is the union of the row's lines' boxes (derived from their polygons, geometry.bbox_of) and whose charspan is start, end, shifted by the text before it when the item continues a paragraph of an earlier region or page. Rows without text belong to no paragraph; text-only transcriptions have rows without boxes (each line a row of its own, a region one paragraph; a page without regions is one region).

Decision kind Reasons mark_removed letter_follows: the next row starts with a lowercase or caseless letter hyphen_kept capital_follows, digit_follows, no_letter_follows, script_change (a mark after a Hebrew letter before a row in another script), attested (the document has the hyphenated form and not the joined one) paragraph_break indent, gap (about a blank line), short_row (justified text: the row before stopped short of the end margin) continuation division_mark, end_margin (the last row reaches the end margin), without sentence-final punctuation

docs.title: Geometry
docs.text: Every bbox is [x, y, width, height] in pixels of the received image. Polygons and baselines are float lists exactly as the engine returned them. Algorithms derive boxes from the polygon (geometry.bbox_of), so their arithmetic matches the engine's (no x + width rounding). Transcription.scaled(sx, sy) moves every coordinate to another image size.

docs.title: Order
docs.text:
• Processing order is the list order of Transcription.lines after the line steps: regions in the layout step's order, orphan rows last, rows within each region. A recognizer processes and batches lines in this order.
  • Reading order is separate: reading_order ranks the lines on the page (regions by their reading order, then rows); row is the visual row within a region.

docs.title: Unicode
docs.text: The as-written layer is NFC, made by a step of its own: UnicodeNormalizer (linecaster.text.unicode) right after recognition, recorded as StepInfo(step="unicode", name="unicodedata", settings={"form": "NFC", "unicode_version": ...}). Each engine's raw output stays exactly what the engine produced. Only canonical forms (NFC, NFD) are allowed; never NFKC, whose folding is the readable variants' job (linecaster.text.variants).

docs.title: Typography (linecaster.text.typography)
docs.text:
The retyper edits regions and lines in place:

  • A split-off headline is region <region id>_head (raw label <raw>/split); its lines keep their ids and get the new region_id.
  • Removed regions (drop capitals, uncertain page numbers) leave regions with their lines and are recorded in Transcription.extra["retyper_dropped"] (id, labels, text, line ids, reason, confidence).
  • A drop capital's letter is prepended to the target line's text (line.extra["drop_capital"]); words are not touched.
  • Regions are re-ranked and lines re-ordered afterwards.

docs.title: Documents (linecaster.formats.docling)
docs.text:
• Page composition (Composer, DocumentBuilder): docling from regions, paragraphs or lines, and tables; page headers and footers always in Docling's furniture layer. Exports choose whether to include them (furniture=True). A text region with paragraphs (a Recomposer ran) is one item per paragraph, one provenance entry per row; a paragraph that continues another (continues_from) is appended to that one's item, its rows' character spans after the text before it (a division mark removed at the continuation stays in the span of the row it ended); a region of one paragraph without a letter (a page number) is an item of its own. Without paragraphs a text region is one item, one row per line, with the region's box (diplomatic composition).
  • Item composition (Composer(unit="item"), DocumentBuilder): an item's pages composed into one DoclingDocument whose page n is the item's n-th page (by sequence, then page id). Recomposed as an item (a Recomposer(unit="item") before it), paragraphs continue across page breaks; sections are optional (options={"sections": True}); region_of (item ref → "<page_no>:<region id>") travels with the document for Markdown dividers.

docs.title: Item records (linecaster.blocks.base.item)
docs.text: An item travels as one datatrove Document: id is the item id, metadata["item"] the item record, {"item_id": ..., "pages": [...]}, its page records (as JSON-compatible dicts) in order (sequence, then page id), without the image bytes. The Binder makes it from a page stream (gather: an item is complete when its metadata["item_page_count"] pages have arrived, or when the input ends; a task must see whole items, so the run layout buckets page records by item, and with several tasks the builder writes them in item shards first). The item-unit blocks change the page records inside it: Recomposer(unit="item") (the paragraphs of the whole item, a ParagraphRef.page_id naming the other page of a continuation), CharacterNormalizer(unit="item") (normalized), Composer(unit="item") (the item's document next to the record: metadata["docling"], ["region_of"], ["item_id"]; text its plain text). The ItemTextWriter renders the text variants from it, the ItemDocumentWriter writes the document's exports, and the Splitter passes its pages on as page documents again, each with what the item-level blocks added.

docs.title: Text variants (linecaster.text.variants)
docs.text:
The vocabulary is era-neutral, on three independent dimensions: character fidelity (as written, normalized, expanded, regularized), flow (as laid out, flowed) and scope (full page, body only). Each transform moves one step on one dimension; the as-written layer is never overwritten. All text is NFC; the normalization folds ſ, ligatures, r rotunda and superscript e over a, o, u by an explicit mapping table, and keeps æ, œ, ø, å and ß; never NFKC; spelling is never modernized.

Three variants per item:

Variant Made from verbatim_txt as written, as laid out, full page: each page's Transcription.text (lines in reading order, tables as Markdown or HTML tables), pages joined with a form feed readable_txt normalized, flowed, body only: the item recomposition's paragraphs (Paragraph.normalized; a paragraph continued from another, also across a page break, appended to it with the continuation's separator), tables one row per line with tab-separated cells (each cell's normalized), a formula region's LaTeX; page headers, page footers, pictures and charts left out readable_md the same as Markdown: # title, ## section header (by heading level), - list item, tables as pipe tables (HTML when a cell spans)

The normalization engine (normalization.latin-historic.v1) sets normalized on every line, paragraph and table cell (Region.extra["table"]["cells"][i]["normalized"]); the as-written texts stay.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text: The terms linecaster uses, one meaning each. Where a word means something else elsewhere (in datatrove, Haystack, everyday use), the not column says so. Code, docs and commit messages use these terms and no others; a new term is added here before it is used.

docs.title: Running things
docs.text: Term Meaning Not block One processing unit of a pipeline: a datatrove PipelineStep. Blocks are named as role nouns (LineRecognizer, Composer, PageJsonlWriter). An HTTP server's refusal is a block too, always named with its host or proxy (below, block (HTTP)). not a "step" (that is a catalog term), not a "component", not a "module" role What a block does, defined by its contract; implementations and strategies of one role are interchangeable. family A group of roles of one kind: readers, layout, lines, recognition, conversion, text, composition, binding, validation, servers, writers, composites. One subpackage of linecaster.blocks each. contract What a block reads, adds, replaces and removes in the page record (or item record), and its unit. The builder checks contracts before a run. not a Python type signature part One named piece of the page record (or item record) a contract names: page-level (image, metadata), or of one transcription (ocr_new:lines); the vocabulary is PARTS (below). not a datatrove Document field unit What one call of a block or engine processes: line, region, page or item. per-unit transform, stream transform The two shapes of a block: a per-unit transform processes one unit per call and its base class owns the loop; a stream transform takes the whole stream and passes each unit on when it is done, possibly out of order (served model blocks). condition A picklable predicate on the page record with a describe(); a block with one (when=) processes only the pages it accepts, the others pass unchanged. Blocks sharing a group are alternatives: each page goes through one of them. composite block A named group of blocks with its own outward contract (e.g. ModularTranscriber). The builder expands it into its blocks. pipeline An ordered list of blocks that a stream of pages (or items) passes through, run by an executor. datatrove's sense. not a graph of components as in Haystack graph The dependencies between a pipeline's blocks, derived from their contracts by the builder: for checking, drawing, and cutting into stages. It is not executed as a graph. builder The code that turns a pipeline definition into stages: derives the graph, checks it, expands composites, cuts it at unit changes. stage One datatrove pipeline run as part of a longer computation; stages run one after another and hand over through files (e.g. page records written in item shards, read by the next stage). not a "phase" pipeline shape One way of putting blocks together, with slots for presets: the code in linecaster.pipelines.<name> that adds its options, names the engines they ask for and builds its blocks, with its help text, pipeline id and slots. Named like its pipeline script and its pipeline id; a derivative's script imports it the same way. not the blocks of one run (that is the pipeline) pipeline script A self-contained uv script in pipelines/ (PEP 723 metadata, a lock next to it) that gives one pipeline shape its environment and its command line, and runs it on every executor. Named as a verb: harvest.py, transcribe_modular.py, transcribe_vlm.py, bind.py. pipeline id A pipeline script's versioned id, its file name plus .v<n>: transcribe_modular.v1. Recipes name the pipeline they run by it. workflow The sequence of pipeline scripts for a collection: harvest → transcribe → bind. not one pipeline; not a GitHub Actions workflow (say "CI workflow" for that) executor, job, task, worker, shard datatrove's terms: the executor runs a pipeline as tasks; a job is one launch (one HF Job, one Slurm job); a task is one unit of work with its own rank; workers are tasks running at once; a shard is the part of the input one task reads. item shard A folder of page records holding every page of a set of items, so that a later stage reads whole items. not a datatrove shard backend Where a model block's engine runs: in-process, served (a server reached through saturate), or chat (an OpenAI-compatible VLM server). not the executor server A process that hosts models: linecaster serve for engines, vLLM or SGLang for VLMs, a service for a page engine. Started by the server blocks ModelServer, ChatModelServer and ServiceServer, which go last in a pipeline. service The server a page engine talks to that is neither linecaster serve nor a chat server: a vendor's page pipeline behind its own HTTP API, in the vendor's image (Falcon-OCR, OXR-1.0), or the vLLM a vendor's package attaches to (surya-ocr). A page preset's serve block names it; ServiceServer starts it. not an operating-system service observer A callback at block boundaries (before and after a unit): taps, sampling, progress, tracing. not a Haystack "hook" boundary step The step the builder puts after a block when a stage has observers: it tells them that each unit left that block and entered the next. It adds no stats. not a block tap An observer that writes the page records as they pass a given block (--tap-after). partial run A run of part of a pipeline: up to a block (--until), or from page records after one (--after). run folder The output folder of a run (OUT): pages/ (the page records), rejects/, logs/, traces/, run.yaml, and the files the writers produce. run record OUT/run.yaml: the pipeline as run (every block's parameters, to_dict()), the recipe, the command line, the executor and the software, with pipeline_sha256 (the hash of the functional parameters). resource A remote file of an item or of one of its pages (a catalogue record, an API's item JSON, a manifest, OCR, an image), with a kind (marcxml, item-json, ...): fetched as served by ResourceReader and kept as a raw copy, <kind>/<item>/<name>.<ext>, with a fetch record. not a datatrove Media HTTP policy, host entry How a run's requests go out, from one YAML file (--http-policy, linecaster.net.policy, http), in three levels: settings for every request at its root (rate limits, retries, deadline, User-Agent, what blocks and what stops the run, max_pause), the proxy path's own section (proxies:: the list, proxies per worker, how long a blocked or broken proxy is left out), and a host entry under hosts: for each host that differs, whose fields replace the root's. The run's own options go between the root and the host entries; each host's settings get their own fetcher. not several policies broker A shared folder (any DataFolder: local, S3, ...) through which workers across tasks, runs and machines agree on who uses which shared resource and what is unavailable until when, with leases and marks (linecaster.broker, --broker, default OUT/logs/broker; broker). Proxies are its first kind of resource. not a message broker (no server, no queue) lease A worker's claim on one resource in the broker (<kind>/<id>/leases/): it holds the resource while it renews the lease within the lease time (180 s); one worker holds a resource at a time, and a crashed worker's leases expire on their own. not a lock with a server mark A note in the broker that something holds for a resource in a scope until a time (<kind>/<id>/marks/<scope>/), written once and never changed, deleted by whoever sees it expired (past its keep, if it has one: kept readable that long after its end, for a proxy's doubling): a proxy's block at a host (scope the host), a broken proxy (scope *). worker identity, worker slot Who holds leases in the broker: a datatrove worker as a slot of its machine (<machine>-<n>), not a process. A process claims a free slot of its machine at its first use (its search starting at its executor's worker index, so processes started together do not race) and hands it over when it ends; the next process in the slot is the same worker and goes on with its leases (on Ray every task is a new process). not a process, not a task proxies per worker How many proxies of a list a worker holds at a time (per_worker in an HTTP policy's proxies: section, per host or at the root, linecaster.net.proxies): by default share, a fair share of the proxies not blocked (the free ones divided by the live workers), rebalanced as workers come and go; 1, one, swapped for a free one when it is blocked; or up to N, claimed one by one. The run's default worker count follows it (sharing them, one worker per available proxy up to one per CPU; with 1 or N one per available proxy, divided by N; at most 64 with OUT on object storage). not proxies per task block (HTTP) A host turning an IP away: a response in the host's block_on (429 by default; with html there, an HTML page where another format was expected), whether through a proxy or direct, since the server only sees an IP (http). Through proxies the proxy is left out for that host (a mark in the broker, until Retry-After, else 60 s doubling up to block_ttl) and the request goes on through another; direct the worker's requests to the host pause. A block is never an attempt. not a block of a pipeline, not a failed attempt broken proxy A proxy that failed attempts itself (a proxy error, no connection to it) broken_after times in a row (3 by default): left out for every host (a mark with scope *), first for broken_ttl (300 s), doubling, at most block_ttl. A slow server's timeout does not count. not a blocked proxy (that is the host's refusal) pause A time in which a fetcher (one per worker and host settings) sends no request to a host, or with the breaker none at all, and its requests wait instead of failing. Three things start one: a block on a direct connection, for that host, until the response's Retry-After has passed, else 60 s doubling while the blocks repeat, after which the request that got it is tried again (linecaster.net.http.Pause); the breaker during an outage; and, with a proxy list, no proxy usable for the host (every one the worker holds blocked there, none free to claim) until a block ends or another worker gives one back. The blocks' pauses and the waits for a proxy count toward the host's max_pause since its last successful response, and beyond it the run stops (http). Other hosts' requests and other workers' fetchers go on. not a stop of the run unexpected HTML A successful response (2xx) with an HTML page where an image, XML, JSON or a manifest was expected (an error page served with 200, a soft 404, a login page after a redirect): by default a failed attempt, retried and traced 200-html (linecaster.net.http.UnexpectedHTML); a block or a stop where the host's policy has html in block_on or stop_on. not an error status with an HTML body (a 503 page is a 503) breaker A fetcher's guard against an outage (linecaster.net.http.Breaker): when most recent attempts got a server error it pauses the fetcher's requests, sends a probe now and then, and ends the pause with the first answer that is not a server error. not the pause after a block reject A page that failed a check or a step, written to rejects/ with the reason; it stays in the page records with its errors. warm-up What a block loads before its first unit (warm_up()): an engine, a server, a client's secrets. Timed as its own stat. error budget The share of a task's pages a block may fail on before the task fails (--max-page-errors, default 1 % of at least 100 pages). functional parameter, operational parameter A block parameter that can change what a run writes (functional), or only where things are and how the work runs (operational: folders, ports, endpoints, windows, worker counts). pipeline_sha256 covers the functional ones. describe mode Building a pipeline shape's blocks in the current process without its engines, for its description and hash (linecaster.runtime.run.describe). not --dry-run, which runs in the script's environment secret reference EnvVar("NAME"): a credential named by its environment variable, read in the task, never stored in a pipeline or a record. trace, span OpenTelemetry's terms: a trace is one page's (or one task's) path through a run, made of spans, one per operation, with times and attributes. not telemetry sample The pages that are traced: a fixed share chosen by page id, plus every page that failed. trace context A page's W3C traceparent (doc.metadata["trace"]), given at the reader's boundary: the page's spans are its children, and a served block sends it with the page's request. not "the current span" task span A span of the task's own work, traced for every task: the task, a block's warm-up, a server start, a reader's file, a writer's flush. gap The time a block had no page in it between its first page and its last: it waited for its input (linecaster traces).

docs.title: Parts
docs.text:
What contracts name besides the parts presets produce (PRODUCES in linecaster.catalog.schema: regions, reading_order, lines, baselines, text, words, ...); PARTS holds them all.

Part Meaning image The page image's bytes, as the reader brought them (page-level). metadata The page record's own fields: ids, sequence, the image's record, the metadata (page-level). transcription_file A library's own transcription delivered with the page, as a file's bytes (a document media: ALTO, PAGE-XML, hOCR or text; page-level); the TranscriptionConverter reads it into a transcription. line_regions Lines assigned to the layout regions and ordered within them (the LineAssigner). hierarchy Heading levels, headline splits and drop capitals (the Typographer). nfc The as-written layer in one Unicode normalization form (the UnicodeNormalizer). paragraphs The running text recomposed from the rows, with its decisions (the Recomposer). normalized The normalized texts of lines and paragraphs (the CharacterNormalizer). document The DoclingDocument of a page (the Composer) or of an item (Composer(unit="item")).

docs.title: The catalog
docs.text: Term Meaning Not catalog linecaster's register of models, engines, presets and recipes, in src/linecaster/catalog/data/. not a data repository: it holds no measurements catalog entry One registered thing: a model, a preset or a recipe; a YAML file, with a Markdown sidecar for its prose. not a "component", not a "document" step A catalog step: what an engine does, e.g. layout, lines, recognition, tables, formulas, image, normalization, typography, recomposition, composition. A preset belongs to one step. not a block engine Code with a versioned id (kraken.recognition.v1, recomposition.unicode.v1) that implements one step: a class with Options, capabilities, load() and a call per unit. Built-in engines live in the core; engine packages (linecaster-kraken, ...) add more. not saturate's Engine class (its server launcher) strategy An engine of a rule-based step (normalization, typography, recomposition, composition, image). A strategy declares the scripts it covers. script A writing system, named by its ISO 15924 code (Latn, Hebr, Arab): Unicode's Script property. A by-script engine routes each decision to the strategy for the script around it; * stands for every script. not a pipeline script model An upstream artifact with weights (or learned data such as hyphenation patterns), pinned by revision, with its upstream card copied verbatim. not an engine, not a preset, not a VLM adapter preset A named configuration of one engine for one step: engine id, options, capabilities, and the model it loads if any. Referred to as id@edition. page preset A preset whose unit is page: one model reads the whole page (a VLM, or a page engine). launch.py can run one directly. not "a model" page engine An engine of the recognition step whose unit is the page: it reads the whole page and returns its transcription, in the pipeline's process or behind a server (indra.recognition.v1, surya.recognition.v1, and the clients of a vendor's service, falcon.recognition.v1, oxr.recognition.v1). PageRecognizer runs it. not a chat preset (chat.v1) recipe A tested combination: a pipeline id, a preset edition per slot, and options. slot A place in a pipeline script that a preset fills; its name is the step's (--layout, --lines, --recognition, ...). adapter The code that talks to one VLM family over the OpenAI-compatible API: its request, its prompt handling, its parsing (linecaster.adapters). not an engine package evidence A measurement of a preset or recipe edition with its source (own run, model card, vendor benchmark), as an evidence record (linecaster.evidence/1), kept by an evaluation in its own repository. not a catalog entry version Upstream's name for a release of a model (v6, 3.5). not an edition revision The exact upstream commit a model is pinned to. edition linecaster's release number of a preset or recipe: kraken-ppocrv6-medium@1. A released edition never changes; its hash covers its YAML. not a version code id The versioned id of an engine or a pipeline: <name>.v<n>. An option added later keeps the id if its default keeps the old behavior. schema id The format of a YAML file: linecaster.preset/1. lock catalog.lock: the hash of every released edition, and the expanded pipeline of every recipe edition.

docs.title: Pages, items and text
docs.text: Term Meaning Not item Any multi-page unit: a book, an issue, a manuscript, a file. Key item_id. not "book" in generic code, flags or docs page One page of an item, with its image and its named transcriptions. page_id is <item_id>_<sequence:04d> unless the source has stable ids of its own. not the step page (there is none) page record A page with its image reference, its transcriptions and its metadata (Page): what a block reads and adds to while the page passes, and what is stored in OUT/pages/ as JSONL or Parquet (everything but the image bytes). not a "page row" item record An item with its pages in order, as the Binder passes it on (doc.metadata["item"], linecaster.blocks.base.item); the item-unit Recomposer, CharacterNormalizer and Composer read it, the item writers write from it, the Splitter turns it back into pages. manifest An item's list of its pages and their files, in order: an IIIF Presentation manifest or a METS document (also inside OAI-PMH). not a BagIt checksum manifest page image The image a page's coordinates refer to (PageImage): its URI, format, size, hash. working image The working-image preset of the ImageConverter: lossless WebP at full resolution, 8-bit sRGB. not a role transcription Everything read from a page by one source (Transcription): regions, lines, words, paragraphs, the document, the steps that made it, and its source. Named per page: ocr_new (linecaster's), ocr_original (the library's own), ground_truth. not "OCR" (it also holds HTR and ground truth) region An area of a page with a label (text, title, table, ...) from layout. reading order The rank in which a page's regions are read (Region.reading_order), from the layout model when it learned one (PP-DocLayoutV3), otherwise computed by linecaster. not the order of Transcription.lines, which is the processing order XY-cut, XY-Cut++ The two ways linecaster computes a reading order for a layout model that has none: XY-cut splits the page recursively at whitespace gaps; XY-Cut++ (Liu et al., 2025) first masks titles, visuals and cross-layout regions, cuts the rest, then matches the masked regions back to their neighbours (linecaster.data.geometry, the layout option reading_order). cross-layout region A text region that spans several columns (longer than 1.3 × the median region and overlapping two or more others horizontally), which XY-Cut++ masks before cutting. not a region label line One printed or written line: its geometry and, once recognized, its text and words. row The lines of one region that sit side by side at the same height (Line.row), as in typesetting; detection often splits one printed line into several lines on the same row. never a stored record word The finest unit: its text, box and confidence. linecaster has no glyph level. paragraph Running text recomposed from a region's rows, with the decisions that made it. Added by the Recomposer. document A DoclingDocument: the composed structure of a page or an item. Added by the Composer. not a datatrove Document (say "datatrove document"), not a catalog entry step info One entry per step that worked on a transcription (StepInfo): step, engine, preset edition, backend, settings, measurements. measurements Numbers a step records for a page: seconds, tokens, device, finish_reason, in a fixed vocabulary. not trace attributes text variant A named point on the three text dimensions, written per item: verbatim_txt, readable_txt, readable_md. not a "version" character fidelity, flow, scope The three text dimensions: as written → normalized (fidelity); as laid out → flowed (flow); full page → body only (scope). Each transform moves one step on one dimension. not "axes" composition Building a document from regions and paragraphs (the Composer). not "assembly" recomposition Turning lines back into running text: paragraphs, removed division marks, separators, continuation (the Recomposer). not "reflow" (the old name) binding Gathering an item's pages in order into one item (the Binder). splitting Passing an item record's pages on as pages again, with what the item-level steps added (the Splitter). division mark A hyphen the typesetter added where a word was divided at a line end. not a hyphen that belongs to the word decision One choice a recomposition made at a row end, with its reason from a fixed vocabulary: a division mark removed, a hyphen kept, a paragraph break, a continuation. Recorded on the paragraph.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text: Term Meaning Not engine API What an engine package may import from linecaster besides the data model: linecaster.engines.api (the Engine protocol, Capabilities, the weight helpers). not the HTTP routes of linecaster serve fake engine A deterministic CPU engine of linecaster.testing for tests, one per model step, registered under fake.<step>.v1 by register_fakes() only. never in a catalog preset conformance check check_engine (the engine protocol) or check_block (a block's contract against what it does, its to_dict(), pickling, warm_up() and failed pages), from linecaster.testing. not a parity check marker A pytest marker of linecaster's tests: gpu, network, slow. Tests marked gpu or network skip where the device or the network is missing. CI workflow .github/workflows/ci.yml: the core's tests and checks on a CPU, on every push and pull request to main. not a workflow

docs.title: Docs and changes
docs.text: Term Meaning Not derivative A project built on linecaster: its own pipelines, blocks or engines, and its project-specific code, defaults and names. not a fork generated docs The files linecaster docs writes from code, docstrings and the catalog when the site is built: the catalog's and the blocks' pages, the site's index and changelog, and llms.txt. Never edited by hand and not in git. not the reference docs (docs/reference/, hand-written) block page The generated page of one block (docs/blocks/<family>/<Block>.md): its contract, backends, catalog step and presets, position, options, behavior and example. breaking change A change after which code, a command line, a stored file or a catalog reference that worked before stops working or means something else (compatibility). upgrade note The entry in CHANGELOG.md for a breaking change: what changed, who is affected, what to do.

docs.title: The print shop
docs.text:
The block names follow the roles of a hot-metal print shop, in the order they work. linecaster makes a new, digital edition of a printed item:

Print shop linecaster Does the linecaster (casts whole lines) LineRecognizer casts the lines anew, as text typographer Typographer determines the hierarchy: headings and their levels, initials, what is text at all compositor Recomposer, Composer recomposes the running text; makes up the page or item document binder Binder binds the pages into the item (the Splitter takes them apart again)

docs.title: HTTP
docs.text:
How linecaster's readers fetch over http(s) (linecaster.net.http, linecaster.net.proxies, linecaster.net.policy): the defaults, what a block is and how each path answers it, unexpected HTML, retries, and the HTTP policy file that changes all of it per host. Terms are the glossary's; how workers share the proxies is in the broker, how runs choose their workers in pipelines.

The principle: the defaults follow the HTTP standards (a 429 with its Retry-After, the retryable statuses, Retry-After as seconds or an HTTP-date); anything learned from one site or CDN (a block page served with 200, a 403 that means "this IP", a block that lasts three days) is opted into per host in an HTTP policy.

docs.title: The defaults
docs.text: Setting Default What it does user_agent HF-Research/1.0 (datatrove's, USER_AGENT) the User-Agent of every request; random_user_agent (--random-user-agent) a random browser one per task instead timeout 300 s each phase of a request (connect, read, write, pool) max_keepalive_connections 16 idle connections kept open for reuse max_retries 4 retries after the first attempt (5 attempts; 0: one) retry_wait_min, retry_wait_max 2 s, 60 s the wait after the n-th failed attempt: retry_wait_min * 2**(n-1), at most retry_wait_max (2, 4, 8, 16 s) retry_after_max 300 s the longest Retry-After a retry honors on the direct path attempt_timeout, attempt_min_rate 15 s, 50,000 bytes/s the deadline per attempt: 15 s plus 1 s per 50 kB the response declares retryable statuses 408, 425, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504, 520-524 (RETRYABLE_STATUS_CODES) tried again; every other 4xx and 5xx fails at once rate_limits none N/S windows, at most N requests in any S seconds, all at once: per worker direct, per proxy through proxies block_on [429] (BLOCK_ON) what is a block (statuses and html) stop_on [] what stops the run at once (statuses and html) max_pause 6 h (MAX_PAUSE) the most a worker's requests to a host wait in all since the host's last successful response: in pauses direct, for a usable proxy through proxies (below) first wait of a block 60 s (BLOCK_FIRST_WAIT) a block without Retry-After: 60 s, then twice the last wait on each repeat shortest block 1 s (PAUSE_MIN_WAIT) whatever Retry-After says (0, a date gone by) proxies: block_ttl 3600 s (BLOCK_TTL) the longest a blocked proxy is left out without Retry-After: the ceiling of the doubling, and of a broken proxy's proxies: broken_after 3 (BROKEN_AFTER) proxy errors in a row before a proxy is broken proxies: broken_ttl 300 s (BROKEN_TTL) a broken proxy's first time out, doubling, at most block_ttl proxies: per_worker share how many proxies of the list a worker holds (broker)

docs.title: Blocks
docs.text:
A block means "this IP was turned away", through a proxy or direct: the server only sees an IP. What counts as a block is declared once for both paths (block_on: statuses, and html for an HTML page where another format was expected). The connection decides the reaction:

direct (one IP) through proxies a response in block_on the worker's requests to that host wait (a pause) for Retry-After, or else 60 s, doubling on each repeat; requests to other hosts go on; the run stops when the wait would be too long (past max_pause since the host's last successful response) the proxy is marked for that host (Retry-After, or else 60 s doubling up to block_ttl) and the request goes on at once through another proxy, without using up an attempt a response in stop_on the run stops at once the run stops at once no usable proxy (none) the requests to that host wait for a block to end or a proxy to free up; the run stops when the waits would pass max_pause since the host's last successful response connection errors the host's errors: retries and the breaker the proxy's errors: they count toward broken_after, then the proxy is left out for every host

How long a block lasts is one function for both paths (linecaster.net.http.block_wait): with Retry-After (seconds or an HTTP-date) exactly that, at least 1 s; without it 60 s, then twice the last wait for each block that repeats (for that host, and through proxies for that proxy at that host), at most block_ttl through proxies and max_pause direct. Direct, the worker keeps each host's doubling in memory (it owns its IP); through proxies the doubling travels with the proxy in the broker's marks, so a worker that claims a released proxy continues it (broker). The doubling starts again at 60 s after a successful response from the host (through proxies: through that proxy), or after a quiet period: when the next block comes more than the last wait after the last block there ended (linecaster.net.http.doubling). A response to a request sent before a block that still holds changes nothing. A block is never an attempt: the request that got it is tried again after the pause (direct) or at once through another proxy, with all its retries left.

A broken proxy fails attempts itself (a proxy error, no connection to the proxy, PROXY_ERRORS) broken_after times in a row: it is left out for every host, first for broken_ttl, twice as long each time it breaks again before it carries an answer, at most block_ttl. A timeout reading the server's answer is a slow server, not a broken proxy: it is retried and leaves the proxy in. Blocks and broken proxies are marks in the broker, so every worker that shares it leaves the proxy out, and continues their doubling when it claims the proxy.

docs.title: max_pause
docs.text: max_pause is one count on both paths, per worker and host (linecaster.net.http.PauseTotal): the time the worker's requests to the host have spent waiting since the host's last successful response, direct in pauses (the length each block adds), through proxies waiting for a usable proxy (the time no proxy was usable there). Once the next wait would take it past max_pause (a block whose wait is known, the first proxy block that ends), or it has passed it (waiting for proxies other workers hold), the run stops with StopRequests, whose message says how long the host's requests waited. A successful response from the host starts it again, through any proxy. Each host counts for itself: a pause at one host neither holds nor counts against the requests to another. The breaker's waits (a server that fails) do not count: each request waits one out a few times, then fails.

docs.title: Unexpected HTML
docs.text:
A successful response (2xx) with an HTML page where an image, XML, JSON or a manifest was expected is unexpected HTML: an error page served with 200, a soft 404, a login page after a redirect, a CDN's challenge. The readers say what they expect (HTTPFetcher.submit's expect: images, manifests, ALTO files, resources whose kind or URL names a format). A body is HTML (linecaster.net.http.is_html, read after a UTF-8 byte order mark, whitespace and <!-- --> comments) when it starts as an HTML document (<!doctype html, <html), whatever its Content-Type says; or when it is labelled text/html and is empty, plain text (an error message), XHTML, or starts with an HTML element (<head>, <body>, <div>, ...: HTML_ELEMENTS). A body labelled text/html that starts as data is data a server mislabelled and passes: JSON, an XML declaration or another root element (ALTO, METS, MODS without a declaration), an image (DATA_MAGIC). ResourceReader checks its resources with the same rule. An error status with an HTML body is that status: a 503 maintenance page is a 503, retried as one.

By default unexpected HTML is a failed attempt, on both paths: it counts, is retried after the backoff, and is traced 200-html. After the last attempt the fetch fails with UnexpectedHTML, whose message names the expected format and the content type (an HTML page (text/html; charset=utf-8, 1234 bytes) where an image was expected: URL); through proxies as the cause of MaxRetriesExceeded (after 5 attempts: an HTML page ...). With html in block_on it is a block instead (above), with html in stop_on it stops the run.

docs.title: Retries and deadlines
docs.text:
A request is tried up to max_retries + 1 times (HTTPFetcher._attempts, one loop for both paths). A transport error (a timeout, a broken connection, a proxy error, an attempt past its deadline), a retryable status and unexpected HTML are tried again after retry_wait_min * 2**(n-1) seconds (at most retry_wait_max); on the direct path at least as long as the response's Retry-After asks (at most retry_after_max); through proxies the next attempt goes out through another proxy, without it. Any other status fails at once (httpx.HTTPStatusError); a 404 first tries the page's fallback URL, if it has one, with attempts of its own. Retries used up raise the last error (direct) or MaxRetriesExceeded naming it (through proxies). Each attempt must be done within its deadline: attempt_timeout plus 1 s per attempt_min_rate bytes the response declares, counted from when it goes out, after the rate limits; one that takes longer is cut and retried.

Each fetcher also has a breaker (linecaster.net.http.Breaker): when most recent attempts got a server error, its requests pause, a probe goes out now and then, and the first answer that is not a server error ends the pause. Unexpected HTML is not an answer for it (it would keep the breaker closed while a host serves only error pages); a resource that fails as unexpected HTML counts once as a server error.

docs.title: Trace entries
docs.text: Every fetch records its attempts (the fetch record's tries, the http.tries of a page's linecaster.http.fetch span, tracing): 200 (or another status) for a response read whole, 200-cut for one cut by the deadline per attempt, 200-html for unexpected HTML, no-response for none (a timeout, a connection or proxy error). A block is traced with its status (429) but does not count among the attempts a failed fetch names. The record also has the time spent waiting for the rate limits (wait_seconds) and in pauses (pause_seconds).

docs.title: The HTTP policy
docs.text:
--http-policy FILE (linecaster.net.policy.HTTPPolicy) gives a run's requests their settings from one YAML file, in three levels, each inheriting from the one above. It holds for every reader that fetches over http(s), the same way (linecaster.net.policy.Fetchers): --items, --parquet with http(s) image URLs, --manifests (the manifests, their images and OCR files) and --pages (the images it fetches again).

# 1. general: every request, direct or through a proxy
rate_limits: ["100/60", "2/1"]     # per worker direct, per proxy through proxies
attempt_timeout: 120
max_retries: 6
random_user_agent: true            # or user_agent: TEXT
block_on: [429]                    # default [429]; 4xx/5xx statuses and `html`
stop_on: []                        # statuses and `html`; never also in block_on
max_pause: 6h
# 2. proxies: only for requests through the proxy list; inherits level 1
proxies:
  file: proxies.txt
  per_worker: share                # share | 1 | N
  block_ttl: 3600                  # a blocked proxy without Retry-After: the ceiling of the doubling
  broken_after: 3                  # proxy errors in a row before it is left out
  broken_ttl: 300                  # a broken proxy's first time out, doubling, at most block_ttl
# 3. hosts: per host, the same two levels; each field overrides the one above
hosts:
  catalog.example.org:
    direct: true
    rate_limits: ["25/60"]
    stop_on: [html]
  images.example.org:
    proxies: {block_ttl: 72h}
broker: s3://bucket/broker         # root only

Durations are seconds or a number with s, m, h or d (72h). A host's settings are, from the lowest precedence up:

  1. linecaster's defaults (above);
  2. the file's level 1, at its root;
  3. the run's own options: --rate-limit, --proxies (the proxy list's file), --user-agent, --random-user-agent;
  4. the host's level 1, under hosts:.

The proxies: section applies only on the proxy path: the root's, then the host's, field by field (a host's proxies: {block_ttl: 72h} keeps the root's file). A field at a host replaces the root's, it does not merge into it (stop_on: [403] at a host drops the root's stop_on). direct: true at a host means no proxies there, neither a list nor the environment's (HTTPS_PROXY); direct: false undoes a direct root. broker is the folder through which the workers share the proxies and their blocks, at the root only (default OUT/logs/broker). The checks at startup: something in both block_on (or its default) and stop_on is refused (to stop on a 429, write block_on: [] with stop_on: [429]); hosts that use one proxy list must agree on its per_worker; an unknown field is an error. Each host's settings get their own fetcher, so each host its own rate limits, breaker, pause and window.

A run states the rules that hold per host and path before it starts (HTTPPolicy.describe, in the run's notes), defaults and opt-ins alike, e.g. catalog.example.org: direct, 25/60 per worker, 4 retries, blocks on 429: the worker waits Retry-After, else 1 min doubling, and stops when the wait would pass 6 h, stops on html.

docs.title: Fields of earlier versions
docs.text:
Fields of earlier versions are refused at startup with a PipelineConfigError that names the line to write instead:

Field Write instead pause_on: [429, 503] block_on: [429, 503] blacklist_on: [403] block_on: [429, 403] (with the statuses of pause_on, if any) blacklist_ttl: 72h proxies: {block_ttl: 72h} blacklist_threshold: 2 proxies: {broken_after: 2} proxies: proxies.txt proxies: {file: proxies.txt} proxies_per_worker: 1 proxies: {per_worker: 1}

docs.title: A CDN-protected host
docs.text:
A host behind a CDN that answers a turned-away IP with a challenge page (HTML with 200) and keeps an IP blocked for an hour, where one proxy error already means the proxy is unusable, gets the strict reaction back per host:

proxies: {file: proxies.txt}
hosts:
  images.example.org:
    block_on: [429, html]          # a challenge page is a block: the proxy is left out, the request goes on
    proxies:
      block_ttl: 3600              # left out up to an hour without Retry-After
      broken_after: 1              # one proxy error in a row: broken

Direct, the same block_on: [429, html] makes the worker wait on a challenge page as on a 429, or stop when the wait would be too long.

docs.title: Pipelines: contracts and the builder
docs.text: A pipeline is a list of blocks (datatrove PipelineSteps) and composites. Before it runs, the builder (linecaster.runtime.builder) checks the blocks' contracts, expands the composites, and cuts the pipeline into stages. Every pipeline script goes through it (linecaster.runtime.run). Terms are the glossary's.

docs.title: Contracts
docs.text:
Every block returns its contract from contract() (linecaster.blocks.base.contract):

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Part:
    name: str                  # a name of PARTS, or "*" (every part)
    transcription: str | None  # ocr_new, ocr_original, ...; None: page-level (image, metadata, transcription_file)
                               # or the item record's

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Contract:
    unit: str                  # "page", "item" (what the input stream carries) or "any" (servers)
    unit_out: str | None       # set when the block changes the stream's unit (binder: page -> item, splitter: back)
    reads: frozenset[Part]
    adds: frozenset[Part]
    replaces: frozenset[Part]
    removes: frozenset[Part]   # parts the block does not pass on (gone for every later block)
    role: str                  # reader, writer, server, model, transform, binder, splitter, validator, composite
  • The vocabulary is PARTS in linecaster.catalog.schema: image, metadata and transcription_file (a library's own transcription delivered with the page, as a document media) (page-level), what presets produce (PRODUCES: regions, reading_order, lines, baselines, text, words, word_confidences, line_confidences, tables, formulas, markdown, html, doctags, layout_json, latex), and line_regions, hierarchy, nfc, document. A part is written transcription:name (ocr_new:lines); ocr_original:* is every part of a transcription.
  • Simple blocks declare class attributes (unit, role, parts_read, parts_added, parts_replaced, parts_removed) that the default contract() of Contracted reads; page-level names stay page-level, the others belong to the block's transcription. Blocks whose parts depend on their options compute contract().
  • Model blocks read the page image (recognition also lines, tables and formulas regions) and add their preset's capabilities.produces: the preset of the InProcess backend (preset), of the Served backend (preset, set by runtime.run.engines) or of the Chat backend; without a preset the engine class's capabilities (read from its source in the repository, else from the class); without either the step's default. The chat recognizers add text too, RegionRecognizer also lines (and replaces lines and text: the transcription's earlier lines are replaced).
  • Readers add image and metadata; ManifestReader(existing_ocr=True) also transcription_file, which the TranscriptionConverter reads (adding ocr_original:*); PageRecordReader what provides= declares (["ocr_new:lines", ...]), or anything (*, reads after it are not checked) when it declares nothing. With fetch_images=False it brings no image.
  • Writers read what they write and add nothing (ImageFilesWriter replaces metadata: the image's URI then names its copy; PageFileWriter: lines for hOCR, ALTO and PAGE, text for md and txt, document for HTML, DocLang and JSON, image for plots). Servers have role server and unit any.
  • The Binder changes the unit from pages to items, the Splitter back: an item record holds its page records, so what the pages carried stays available across either (the checks carry the parts over), apart from the page image's bytes (image: an item record has none) at the binder and the item's document at the splitter.
  • Item-unit blocks (Recomposer(unit="item"), CharacterNormalizer(unit="item"), Composer(unit="item")) read item records: one datatrove document per item, doc.metadata["item"] holding the item id and its page records in order (linecaster.blocks.base.item); they read and add the parts of the pages' transcriptions, the item Composer adds the item's document next to the record. Item writers: ItemTextWriter reads lines for verbatim_txt and paragraphs and normalized for the readable variants, ItemDocumentWriter the document. RecipeStamper has unit any: before an item writer it stamps the pages of each item record.
  • A step without a contract (a plain datatrove step) passes pages and touches no part.
Block Reads Adds Replaces, removes LineAssigner lines, regions line_regions regions, reading_order, lines UnicodeNormalizer text nfc text CharacterNormalizer text normalized Typographer regions, lines hierarchy regions, lines Recomposer regions, lines paragraphs paragraphs (made anew where they exist) Composer regions, lines (and paragraphs when there are) document ImageFetcher metadata image ImageConverter metadata metadata (with keep_bytes also image; without it removes image) TranscriptionConverter metadata, transcription_file (with source="media") <transcription>:* RecipeStamper

docs.title: Block shapes
docs.text:
• Per-unit transform (shape = "unit"): process_page(doc, page) -> page | None; PageBlock owns the loop and the stats. In-process model blocks have this shape.
  • Stream transform (shape = "stream"): overrides run(data) and yields each page when it is done, possibly out of order (served model blocks, PageRecognizer, RegionRecognizer). It reports what happens to each page inside it with notify(doc, event): prepare when a request is built, done when its result came back. The served model blocks share one streaming loop (ModelBlock): a block names its requests (_rows: one per page, one per region for RegionRecognizer), builds and parses each (_request, _parse) and says which pages a finished one completes (_done).
  • Only readers and writers see rank, world_size and files (a test walks every block class, with no exceptions): a block that rejects a page records why on the page, and the RejectWriter names the task's file.

docs.title: Backends
docs.text:
A model block's backend (linecaster.backends) says where its engine runs:

  • InProcess("pkg:Class", **options) (or InProcess.from_preset(ref); a model block given a preset ref, LayoutDetector("single-region@1"), builds one): the engine loads in the worker;
  • Served(endpoint, model=name, ...): linecaster serve (or a server speaking its routes) hosts it, reached through saturate on /v1/linecaster/{step};
  • Chat(preset, endpoint=None, served_name=None, max_window=32, initial_window=4, read_timeout=600.0, api_key=None, headers=None, prefer="page"): a chat preset's VLM behind an OpenAI-compatible server (vLLM, SGLang, a hosted endpoint) on /v1/chat/completions; preset is a preset ref, a model's Hugging Face id (its preset with unit prefer) or a configured adapter (chat_model); without an endpoint, the task's ChatModelServer on port 8000. PageRecognizer(backend) and RegionRecognizer(backend, labels=..., pad=None) (pad: the adapter's region_pad, else 8) take it (or a chat preset's ref). PageRecognizer also takes a page engine's InProcess or Served backend (or its preset's ref): a stream transform served, a per-unit transform in-process; it reads the page image and adds text and what the preset produces. A page engine's endpoint option (where its service is) is operational.

The built-in engines (layout.single-region.v1 and the rule-based steps') run in the pipeline's process only: runtime.run.engines keeps a preset of one in-process when the other models are served, and linecaster serve refuses them.

docs.title: The builder
docs.text:
plan = build(blocks, tasks=8, until=None, after=None, taps={"LineAssigner": "OUT/taps/lines"},
             run_folder="OUT", recipe=("squiddle@1", "sha256:..."))
plan.check()          # PipelineConfigError listing every problem
plan.stages           # [Stage(name, tasks, blocks, pipeline)]: one datatrove pipeline each, run in order
plan.graph            # nodes (blocks; composites expanded, their group kept), edges (part -> the block reading it)
plan.mermaid()        # the graph as a Mermaid flowchart: stages and composites as subgraphs
plan.describe()       # stages with each block's contract, the edges, the problems

Checks, all collected: a stage starts with a reader; every part a block reads is added earlier in its stage (or by the stage's reader) and not removed since (removes, even after a reader that provides anything); a part is added by one block only, unless a later block declares it in replaces; units fit (a page block cannot follow an item stream, an item block needs a binder before it); the parts carry across a binder and a splitter (apart from image and the item's document); server blocks go last; a served model block whose endpoint is a server block of its stage (same loopback port) finds its model in that server's list; the alternatives of a group add the same parts, sit next to each other, each with a condition, OTHERWISE last; names given to until, after and taps fit exactly one block.

Order is the given one; the builder checks it and does not reorder. It inserts a TranscriptionConverter (into ocr_original) right after a block that adds transcription_file when no later block reads it, the RecipeStamper before the first writer when the run follows a recipe, a RejectWriter into <run_folder>/rejects before the first writer (or binder) when there is a run folder and the pipeline has none, and moves the server blocks at the end into the stage of the model blocks when it cuts. build(..., max_page_errors=SHARE) sets every page block's error budget.

Branches: branch(block, when=Condition, group=None) gives a block a condition, a picklable predicate on the page record with a describe() (MetadataEquals(key, value), OTHERWISE). The block processes the pages the condition accepts; the others pass unchanged. Blocks with the same group are alternatives: each page goes through the first one whose condition accepts it. A per-unit block gets its pages one by one; any other block one stream of them, the pages it does not take passed on as it yields.

Composites: Composite(name, blocks, contract=None) expands into its blocks (nested composites too); its outward contract is derived (what its blocks read that none of them adds, what they add and replace) unless given. ModularTranscriber(lines, recognition, layout, formulas_separately=False, transcription="ocr_new") is layout ("single-region@1": the page as one region) → lines → line assignment → line recognition; each step a block, a backend or a preset.

Stages: with tasks > 1, the first binder (a block whose stream changes from pages to items) cuts the pipeline, unless the reader already gives each task whole items (ManifestReader, PageRecordReader(item_shards= True)). The first stage writes its page records in item shards into <run_folder>/pages/ (the pipeline's own PageJsonlWriter there, now with item_shards=N, N = tasks unless it set its own); the second starts with PageRecordReader(item_shards=True, fetch_images=False) declaring the parts the first stage added, runs the binder and what follows, as N tasks. A Splitter after the binder needs no cut of its own: the items are whole in the task, so its pages are too. One stage logs to OUT/logs/, two to OUT/logs/pages/ and OUT/logs/items/; the run record lists the stages. Each stage gets its own executor, and the later one depends= on the earlier one:

--on Executors Stages local LocalPipelineExecutor the second starts when the first is complete ray RayGPUExecutor for stages with servers, RayExecutor for the item stage and pipelines without engines (CPUs only) the same, through depends= hf-jobs JobsExecutor (datatrove's JobsPipelineExecutor with JSON-lines logs; GPUJobsExecutor for multi-GPU flavors on stages with servers) consecutive launches: the second launches when the first's Jobs are complete; both on --flavor

Partial runs (blocks named by their datatrove name, their class name, or a composite's name for its last block):

  • until=BLOCK (--until): the blocks up to and including BLOCK, then a PageJsonlWriter into <run_folder>/pages (and the server blocks);
  • after=BLOCK (--after, with --pages DIR): the pipeline's PageRecordReader, then the blocks after BLOCK; the reader declares the parts the blocks up to BLOCK add;
  • taps={BLOCK: DIR} (--tap-after BLOCK DIR, repeatable): a Tap observer writes every page record as it leaves BLOCK into DIR/<rank>.jsonl.gz.

In this process: run_pages(blocks, docs) checks the blocks and runs them on docs (datatrove documents) as task 0 of 1, without an executor (a leading reader reads its own input after them); run_plan(plan) runs a plan's stages that way. A pipeline script's --page IMAGE OUT runs its pipeline on one image like that, and linecaster page IMAGE OUT [--recipe R | --pipeline ID] [pipeline options] finds the script (the recipe's pipeline, else transcribe_modular.v1) and runs it so.

--dry-run prints the plan (describe() under plan, with the run record) and the Mermaid graph, and fails like a run would when there are problems; a run with problems exits with code 2 before it writes anything.

docs.title: Observers
docs.text:
linecaster.runtime.observers.Observer has on_task_start(rank, world_size), on_warm_up(block, seconds), on_enter(block, doc), on_exit(block, doc, error=None), on_unit(block, doc, event, **attributes) (from stream blocks' notify: prepare and request in saturate's prepare threads, request with a carrier dict for the trace context, done with error, tokens and finish_reason; region for a request per region), on_task_event(block, event, start_ns, end_ns, **attributes) (from Block.report: a reader's file, a writer's flush), on_leave(doc) (a page leaves the stage's last block), on_task_end(error=None) (also when the task fails) and environment() (variables for a server a block starts in the task). When a stage has observers (build(..., observers=[...]), taps, tracing), the builder puts a Boundary after every block: the boundary between block i and i + 1 calls on_exit(i) and on_enter(i + 1) for each page, so a block's time per page includes waiting in a served window; error is the entry the block added to doc.metadata["errors"]. Boundaries are plain callables, not datatrove steps, so they add no stats; a stage without observers has none.

Every stage with a run folder (or an OTLP endpoint) is traced: the builder adds a linecaster.tracing.Tracing observer (build(..., trace_sample=SHARE), --trace-sample; tracing).

docs.title: Warm-up
docs.text: Every block has warm_up() (idempotent): engines load there (InProcess.warm_up()), servers start there (ModelServer, ChatModelServer), a served backend reads its secrets there; blocks with nothing to load keep the no-op. A block's __call__, which datatrove's executors call, warms it up before its run starts: blocks warm up as the stream reaches them, the last one first (the servers before the blocks that call them). The time is the block's own stat, warm_up_seconds (per task), and goes to the observers (on_warm_up(block, seconds)); a page's measured seconds never include loading. An error in a warm-up fails the task (a server that does not start: a ServerError).

docs.title: Failures
docs.text:
• Per page. An exception in a per-unit transform's process_page (other than a PipelineConfigError, CatalogError or ServerError, which fail the task) becomes an entry in the page's doc.metadata["errors"]: {"block": class, "step": a model block's step, "preset": its edition or null, "type": the exception's class, "error": the message}; a failed request of a served block is the same with type ServerError; checks (PageValidator, ImageConverter) add field and raw_value. The page goes on as it was.
  • Later model blocks pass it by (skip_on_error, the default for model blocks; stat skipped_after_error), at once: in-process the page leaves the block before the next one enters, served it is put straight onto the block's results (it never waits for the window, nor for the end of the input).
  • Rejects. The RejectWriter writes every page that carries errors to OUT/rejects/<rank>.jsonl, one line per error (key, field, error, raw_value, and the entry's block, step, preset, type), and passes it on: the page records keep failed pages with their errors, so a later pipeline reading them passes them by too. PageFileWriter(skip_failed=True) writes no per-page files for them (the modular pipeline's --files), so a file is never what the blocks before the failure made of a page.
  • The error budget. A block may fail on max_page_errors of a task's pages (--max-page-errors, default 0.01), judged from the 100th page on: from then, more errors than share × pages fail the task with a PageError (with the default: two failures in the first 100 pages, three in 300). Fewer pages are too few to judge. datatrove reruns a failed task whole.
  • Errors (linecaster.errors): library code raises PipelineConfigError (a pipeline, option or input that cannot work; problems lists them), CatalogError, PageError(page_id, block) and ServerError, all LinecasterErrors, never SystemExit; the linecaster command and a pipeline script's main turn them into exit codes (2: nothing was launched).

docs.title: The run record
docs.text:
OUT/run.yaml (schema linecaster.run-record/1, the pydantic model linecaster.runtime.record.RunRecord, JSON Schema catalog/schemas/run-record-1.json) records the script, the recipe, the command line, the options, where it ran and the software, and:

  • pipeline: per stage its name, tasks and blocks in order, each block as its to_dict() (below) with its contract, composite, group and condition;
  • pipeline_sha256: the hash of the pipeline's functional parameters.

to_dict() gives a block as it was built: {"block": class name, "class": "module:Class", "params": {...}}, every constructor parameter with the value it was given or its default (**kwargs flattened), JSON-compatible: backends as {"backend": "in-process", "engine", "options", "preset", "preset_sha256"}, {"backend": "served", "endpoint", "model", "max_window", ..., "preset", "engine"} or {"backend": "chat", "adapter", "preset", "preset_sha256", "model", "revision", "served_name", "endpoint", "max_window", ...} (a chat adapter's dict plus where its server is), nested blocks as their dicts, secrets as {"env": NAME}, folders as paths, callables as module:name. A block keeps the arguments it was constructed with; live_params names those the builder may change afterwards (a page record reader's provides). A composite's dict is its group: its parameters and its blocks' dicts.

Functional and operational parameters. A parameter is functional when changing it can change what a run writes for a page or an item (its page records, files and texts) or how they are partitioned (item_shards); it is operational when it only changes where things are read and written, how the work is spread and paced, or how a server is reached. pipeline_sha256 covers the functional ones (provenance.functional_pipeline):
