Operational (left out) Why folders and file names: data_folder, output_folder, output_filename, image_folder, manifest_folder, ocr_folder, folder, suffix, bucket_by_item, prefix where things are which input files a task reads and how: paths_file, glob_pattern, recursive, limit, skip, shuffle_files, batch_size (a reader's), http (rate limits, the IIIF format asked for), uri_map, progress bars the pages themselves are recorded per page servers and clients: port, host, python, script, vllm, outside_venv, boot_timeout, max_queue, prepare_workers, gpu_memory_utilization, extra_args; an in-process engine's endpoint and timeout (ENGINE_OPERATIONAL: where its service is); a served backend's endpoint, model (the name it is hosted under, unless nothing else names its engine), max_window, initial_window, read_timeout, api_key, headers; a chat backend's served_name and the same (it counts by its adapter, preset edition and hash, model and revision) how a server is started and reached name (datatrove's display name), compression, max_file_size, ImageConverter.keep_bytes presentation, file handling, memory server blocks (ModelServer, ChatModelServer, ServiceServer) as a whole their models count through the blocks they serve the backend (in-process or served) a model block counts by its engine, the engine's options and the preset edition with its hash, wherever it runs

Everything else is functional: block classes and their order, transcription names, engine options, presets and their hashes, the recipe stamp, conditions and groups, writers' formats and options, item_shards. The base list is OPERATIONAL in linecaster.blocks.base.block; a block class adds its own in operational. So a resumed run, a run on another executor or backend, or into another folder has the same hash; another preset, option or block has another.

Resume. A run into an OUT that holds a run record is checked against its newest record (run.yaml, or a later run-<time>.yaml): another pipeline_sha256 is refused with a PipelineConfigError (finished tasks would be skipped and the folder would mix two pipelines' outputs) unless --new-pipeline (the new record is written next to the earlier one and is the one the next resume is checked against); another --tasks is always refused (each task would read other input). The same hash and tasks: a resume, as datatrove's completion markers make it. --dry-run reports the same problems.

Describe mode. linecaster.runtime.run.describe(shape, argv) builds a pipeline shape's plan in the current process without its engines: its options parsed, presets resolved without checking that their engines are installed, nothing loaded or started. describe_recipe(ref) describes a recipe edition that way (the shape of the recipe's pipeline id, linecaster.pipelines.shape(id), with --recipe REF and placeholder folders): what linecaster catalog release records in the lock and verify compares (catalog).

docs.title: Tasks, workers and rate limits
docs.text:
--tasks and --workers are chosen when the command line leaves them open (linecaster.runtime.run.allocate):

Pipeline --tasks --workers with engines 1 every task without engines, every rate-limited host through proxies (--proxies, an HTTP policy's proxies: {file}), local or Ray (--on hf-jobs: as below) the reader's auto_tasks (from the input), else 1 sharing them fairly (proxies: {per_worker: share}, the default): one per available proxy, at most one per CPU; with per_worker 1 or N: one per available proxy divided by N (ceil(available / N)), not capped by the CPUs; either way at most the tasks and, with OUT on object storage, at most 64 (OBJECT_STORAGE_WORKERS) without engines, with --rate-limit (a host with rate limits and no proxies) the reader's auto_tasks, else 1 1 without engines, without --rate-limit the reader's auto_tasks, else 1 one per CPU, at most the tasks

The available proxies are counted once at launch from one listing of the broker (linecaster.runtime.run.available_proxies): those in the file, less those with a live block or broken mark for the run's hosts (any host when the hosts are not named in an HTTP policy) and those leased by live workers of other runs (the run's own earlier leases count as available); on a first launch, without a broker yet, all of them. Sharing the proxies fairly, a few workers use them all, so their count stops at the CPUs; with one proxy per worker (or up to N) using them all takes a worker per proxy (per N), and the workers mostly wait on the network, so their count is not capped by the CPUs. With OUT on object storage (any fsspec protocol but a local one: s3://, gs://, hf://, az://, ...) the count stops at linecaster.runtime.run.OBJECT_STORAGE_WORKERS (64) in both modes: in one setup, 250 workers writing to S3-compatible object storage hung in their listings of OUT/images and fetched less than 64 did, which ran cleanly; an observation from that setup, not a guarantee for others. The run states the count and why (linecaster.runtime.run.workers_note, e.g. 250 proxies available, OUT on object storage → 64 workers, a fair share each, or 250 proxies available → 250 workers, 1 proxy each). --workers overrides it (each worker is a process with its own memory).

auto_tasks is about 1,000 pages per task for ImageParquetReader and about 5 items per task for ManifestReader (linecaster.blocks.readers.tables.PAGES_PER_TASK, ITEMS_PER_TASK), so a resume repeats little. The harvest (pipelines/harvest.py) asks its reader for one item per task (task_per_item): the tasks divide the items, an item's rows wherever they are in the table (tables.item_runs), so every item is whole in its task and a task that fails costs one item. With --reuse (off by default: on some object storage a listing is slow even for an empty folder, and only the items a stopped launch was in, or with --retry-failed the finished items with failed pages, have anything to reuse) its reader also gets reuse_folder (OUT/images): when it reaches an item it lists the item's folder once (an fsspec listing) and reads a page whose image file is already there from the storage instead of fetching it from the source (linecaster.blocks.readers.existing); only pages of interrupted items (and of the items --retry-failed runs again, whose failed pages alone are then fetched) are read back, so egress stays small. The reader waits at most LISTING_TIMEOUT (60 s) for a listing (on object storage fsspec cancels it then on its IO loop): one that times out or fails is a warning and a stat (reuse_listing_timeouts, reuse_listing_errors), and the item's pages are fetched again, their files overwritten. Such a record is complete and says image.extra.reused; the console counts it as done but not in the rate. On a restart the console's size starts with the finished tasks' media_size from datatrove's stats files (linecaster.runtime.local.size_before, read in the background). Parquet tables are divided over the tasks by rows in equal shards, not by files, so a table never needs splitting for a task count. --max-pages N (--parquet, IMAGES; the readers' max_pages) reads the input as if it ended after its first N pages, in the same automatic tasks: a smoke test of the real setup. --limit counts per task, as in datatrove.

--rate-limit holds per worker: each worker process has one fetcher with its limits (HTTPFetcher.shared), so a server sees the workers running at once times the limits; the run states it before it starts (linecaster.runtime.run.rate_note, e.g. rate limits per worker: 150/60, 3/1 · 1 worker → up to 150/min at a server). One worker keeps any rate limit busy: a reader's requests ahead grow while none waits for the limits (linecaster.net.http.prefetched, at most MAX_AHEAD), and the fetcher, with its limits and the window it has grown to, is shared by the tasks a worker runs one after the other (HTTPFetcher.shared). With --proxies the limits hold per proxy instead (below), and the run states that (rate limits per proxy: 150/60 · 100 proxies → up to 15,000/min at a server; with fewer workers than proxies · 10 of 100 proxies in use (1 proxy per worker)).

Proxies. --proxies FILE sends the http(s) requests through a list of proxies, shared by the workers through the broker (--broker PATH, any fsspec folder, default OUT/logs/broker; runs pointed at one path share the proxies and their blocks too). Each proxy has one worker at a time, the one that holds its lease, and each worker holds a fair share of them (linecaster.net.proxies.ProxyPool, per_worker: share, the default): of the proxies not blocked for the host, divided by the live workers, claimed at most 2 at a time and grown by rebalancing, which also gives back what is beyond it when another worker joins. An HTTP policy's proxies: {per_worker: ...} (per host or at the root; hosts that share a list share the setting) gives a worker one proxy instead (1: it claims a free one usable for the host and, when that one is blocked or broken, releases it and claims another at once), or up to N, claimed one by one; with output on local disk or a short list, one per worker and a worker per proxy is the simplest way to use them all. The host's rate limits hold per proxy, so per IP, as servers count them: the owner spaces the requests through a proxy to a host by the strictest limit, and each request goes through the owned proxy whose turn comes first. A proxy is left out when the failure is its own (http). A block (a status in the host's block_on, 429 by default, and with html there an HTML page where another format was expected) is a mark in the broker for that host, until its Retry-After, else for 60 s, doubling on each repeat up to the host's block_ttl (an hour by default): the owner stops using the proxy there at once, releases it once it is blocked for every host it uses, and whoever claims it later sees the mark, so no worker sends a request into another's block, and a restarted run none into a block it found before. A broken proxy (a proxy error, no connection to it, broken_after failures in a row, 3 by default) is marked for every host, first for broken_ttl (5 minutes), doubling up to block_ttl. A block does not count as an attempt and the request goes on through another proxy at once, so max_retries (retries after the first attempt) counts only the attempts that reached the server and failed there; a block does not count toward the breaker either. A timeout is mostly a slow server: it is retried and leaves the proxy in. When none of a worker's proxies is usable for a host and none is free to claim, its requests to the host pause until a block ends or another worker gives a proxy back (one warning when the pause starts, one when it ends; the wait is in the fetch record's pause_seconds); once the waits since the host's last successful response would pass its max_pause (6 hours; http) the run stops (StopRequests) and says when the first proxy returns. An HTTP policy can set proxies: {block_ttl: 72h, broken_after: 1} and further statuses that block at the host (block_on: [429, 403], block_on: [429, html]). The console shows the proxies the worker holds, those blocked and those free. On Ray each task is a process of its own; the next task on a machine takes over the worker slot the last one handed over, and with it its proxies. The file holds one proxy per line, a URL or host:port[:user:pass] as Webshare lists them; the run record keeps its name, logs show proxies without credentials (linecaster.net.http.redact), and the broker names them by a hash of host and port.

Failures. Each fetcher has a breaker (linecaster.net.http.Breaker): when most attempts of the last minute got a server error (5xx, Cloudflare's 520-524 among them), its requests pause, a probe goes out now and then (waits doubling from one to ten minutes), and the first answer that is not a server error lets them go on; the pages wait instead of failing. A single server error is retried (with a proxy list without counting against the proxy it came through). A block on a direct connection (a status in the host's block_on, 429 by default) pauses the worker that got it (linecaster.net.http.Pause): its requests to that host wait until the response's Retry-After has passed (seconds or an HTTP-date; without one a minute, doubling while blocks keep coming), then the request that got it is tried again, without using up one of its retries; blocks for requests already in flight extend the pause, never shorten it. The pages wait instead of failing, and the requests to other hosts and other workers go on. The log says when a pause starts (host, status, how long, until when) and when the requests go on, and a page's fetch record has the time paused (pause_seconds). A worker that would pause more than the host's max_pause (6 hours) since its last successful response stops the run: the worker waits, or stops when the wait would be too long (http, one count for both paths). Through proxies a block leaves that proxy out at the host instead (above). An HTML page where an image, XML or JSON was expected is a failed attempt, retried like a server error, unless the host's policy makes it a block or a stop (http). A local task that fails is logged and the others go on (LocalExecutor); it runs again on the next launch. An error that is not the pages' (NOT_THE_PAGES) or FAILED_IN_A_ROW failed tasks in a row in one worker stop the run. --retry-failed runs the finished tasks that left rejects again; kill -USR1 <pid> dumps every thread's stack. On Ray (linecaster.runtime.ray.RayExecutor) the same error stops the run through a marker in the logging folder (stopped.json): every task after it ends before its pipeline starts, so none sends a request into the block that stopped the first, and the launch fails with that task's error; a launch that left tasks unfinished fails too, so the Ray job does not end as succeeded. A new launch removes the marker. Before it submits a task, a Ray launch checks that a live node has what a task reserves (--cpus-per-task; --mem-per-task-gb, else --mem-per-cpu-gb per CPU; one GPU for a stage with models) and stops with a PipelineConfigError if none has, where Ray would keep the tasks waiting without an error; --no-fit-check leaves the check out, for a cluster that adds nodes on demand. A task sizes the native thread pools to the CPUs it may use (linecaster.runtime.cpus: its Ray CPUs, else the cgroup's CPU quota), and so do the worker counts a launch derives "one per CPU".

Resources. pipelines/harvest.py --items TABLE --item-key COL fetches items' remote files other than page images (ResourceReader): from URL templates per kind (--resource marcxml=https://catalog.example.org/{item}/marcxml) or a table with one row per resource (--url-key, --kind-key, --name-key). Each is checked (XML, JSON or an image must parse; an HTML page where another format was expected is retried, and a resource that fails with it counts toward the breaker) and kept as a raw copy, OUT/<kind>/<item>/<name>.<ext> (ResourceFilesWriter), the reference later stages link to, with its fetch record in OUT/resources/<rank>.jsonl.gz (ResourceRecordWriter: source and final URL, status, type, size, sha256, ETag, Last-Modified, time). One item per task, --max-items for a smoke test, copies already there read back. --http-policy FILE gives the run's requests their settings from one YAML file (linecaster.net.policy, http): for every host at the root, and under hosts: an entry for each host that differs, whose fields replace the root's; the run's own options go between the two. The settings: rate limits (per proxy through proxies), retries (max_retries), deadline, User-Agent, what blocks (block_on, default [429]; with html an HTML page where another format was expected) and what stops the run without a retry (stop_on: statuses and html; something in both block_on, or its default, and stop_on is refused, so block_on: [] with stop_on: [429] stops on a 429), max_pause, direct, the proxy path's own section (proxies: {file, per_worker, block_ttl, broken_after, broken_ttl}) and the broker (root only). The run states the rules that hold per host before it starts. For every input fetched over http(s): --items, --parquet with http(s) image URLs, --manifests (the manifests, their images and OCR files) and --pages (the images it fetches again); with rate limits in the file for a host without proxies a run keeps one worker, with proxies for every rate-limited host its workers follow the available proxies (above).

The default User-Agent is datatrove's, HF-Research/1.0 (linecaster.net.http.USER_AGENT), deliberately: datatrove is integral to linecaster, and its media fetcher (HTTPFetchReader) sends the same, so a run that fetches through both presents itself as one client to every host. --user-agent or an HTTP policy's user_agent sets another.

docs.title: The console
docs.text: A local run (--on local, linecaster.runtime.local.LocalExecutor) shows on the terminal: one line naming the pipeline (its blocks, without the builder's boundaries; pages, tasks and workers; what an earlier launch finished), a live progress line (pages done of the total, rate over the last five minutes, size, failed pages, the task, the time left) pinned to the terminal's top row, with everything else scrolling below it (a scroll region, Pinned), a line per finished task and a summary, in human units (linecaster.runtime.console). The Progress observer, which the runtime puts on every stage, counts the pages that leave the pipeline; with several workers each worker process reports its counts to the console about every second. Off a terminal the progress is a log line every 30 s instead. datatrove's own console output (its pipeline listing and stats block per task, the merged stats) goes only to the task logs (OUT/logs/logs/task_<rank>.log, in its full line format) and the stats files, which keep it whole. A launch lists the completion markers once instead of looking them up task by task.

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text: linecaster.runtime.secrets.EnvVar("NAME") names an environment variable; the value is read in the task (resolve()), never stored: an EnvVar pickles by name, to_dict() writes {"env": "NAME"}. Served(endpoint, model, api_key=EnvVar("NAME"), headers={"X-Team": "ocr", "X-Token": EnvVar("TOKEN")}) (and Chat(preset, endpoint, api_key=..., headers=...) alike) sends Authorization: Bearer <key> and the headers with every request through saturate's AdaptiveClient(headers=...); a key given as text is refused. A missing variable fails the block's warm-up.

docs.title: Pipeline shapes
docs.text:
A pipeline script's code is a pipeline shape in linecaster.pipelines (harvest, transcribe_modular, transcribe_vlm, transcribe_page, bind): its docstring (the help text), options(ap), models(a), pipeline(a, script), PIPELINE and, where recipes fill it, SLOTS. linecaster.pipelines.shapes() lists them by pipeline id and shape(id) finds one; importing one imports no engine. The script in pipelines/ is its PEP 723 block, a docstring and the call that runs the shape:

from linecaster.pipelines import transcribe_modular as shape
from linecaster.runtime import run

if __name__ == "__main__":
    run.main(__file__, shape.__doc__, shape.options, shape.models, shape.pipeline, shape.PIPELINE, shape.SLOTS)

A derivative's script runs a shape the same way, in its own environment (the engine packages its slots need), and may lay its own defaults over the shape's options: an options that calls the shape's and then ap.set_defaults(...) (--recipe too, which run adds before the script's options), and a pipeline that fills a default depending on other options before it calls the shape's. Its run records name its script; its pipeline_sha256 is the shape's for the same options.

docs.title: The item stage
docs.text:
The item-level steps follow a Binder; the usual shape (pipelines/bind.py, and --item-texts of pipelines/transcribe_modular.py):

[PageRecordReader(pages, fetch_images=False, item_shards=True),
 Binder(),                                                  # page records -> item records
 Recomposer("unicode-recomposition@1", unit="item"),        # paragraphs continued across page breaks
 CharacterNormalizer("latin-historic@1", unit="item"),      # normalized lines, paragraphs, table cells
 Composer("docling-composition@1", unit="item"),            # the item's document
 ItemTextWriter(f"{out}/texts"),                            # texts/<variant>/<rank>.jsonl.gz (format="files": <item>.txt|md)
 ItemDocumentWriter(f"{out}/documents", formats=("md", "txt", "json"), by_format=True)]   # documents/<format>/<item>.<ext>

A Splitter after the item-level blocks passes each item's pages on as pages (e.g. to a PageJsonlWriter), with the paragraphs of the item recomposition.

docs.title: Page records
docs.text: Stored page records are rows {"schema": "linecaster.page/2", "id", "text", "page", "errors"} (PageJsonlWriter, PageParquetWriter; PAGE_SCHEMA in linecaster.data.page). PageRecordReader brings older rows to today's format (UPGRADES, keyed by the row's schema, one version at a time): a linecaster.page/1 row names a transcription's steps model (read as steps); a row without schema (the oldest format) names its transcription ocr, read as ocr_new; a .../pages folder without records is read from its sibling rows/ (the folder's earlier name).

docs.title: HF Jobs helpers
docs.text:
A launch with --on hf-jobs names --namespace, the Hugging Face user or organization the Jobs run under and are billed to, and --commit, the linecaster commit the Jobs install (pushed). Neither has a default, and the namespace is not taken from the logged-in account, so the account a run spends is always the one its command line and run record name. --commit is required for linecaster's own scripts; a derivative's script outside the linecaster checkout that takes linecaster from a git tag, branch or rev runs without it (jobs.needs_commit), since its Jobs install what its sources name.

linecaster.runtime.jobs.dependencies(commit, script=None, engines=True) spells out what a Job installs from a pipeline script, linecaster's or a derivative's, as Dependencies:

  • requirements: the script's dependencies with their sources as PEP 508 URLs (url as it is; git with its tag, branch or rev and its subdirectory, as git+URL@REF#subdirectory=DIR; a path into the linecaster checkout as GitHub's source archive of linecaster at commit, any other path an error), then every package reachable from them in the script's lock that comes from no index (the sources the packages declare themselves: the kraken fork at its locked commit, the OpenCV stub);
  • constraints: every package reachable from them that the lock takes from an index, at the lock's version (name==version; a package the lock holds at several versions with its resolution markers), so a Job resolves the versions of the lock; none for a script without a lock;
  • overrides: the script's [tool.uv] override-dependencies (a lock that resolves only with them, such as transcribe_page.py's pillow==12.3.0 over surya-ocr's pillow<11).

linecaster's ray extra is left out. engines=False keeps linecaster with its extras and the sources they need, and the constraints of what those reach; without a script it raises unless engines=False (linecaster alone). A derivative's pipeline runs on Jobs from its own script (its sources pinned to a linecaster tag), read as it is on disk.

uv run --with (datatrove's way of installing a Job's dependencies) ignores constraints and overrides, whether given as UV_CONSTRAINT, UV_OVERRIDE or a uv.toml; only a script's own [tool.uv] brings them to uv run. So JobsExecutor given Dependencies uploads, in place of datatrove's launch_pickled_pipeline.py, a uv script of the same name whose inline metadata holds the requirements, constraint-dependencies and override-dependencies (Dependencies.script) and which then runs datatrove's launcher. Constraints only bound what the requirements bring: a package the lock holds for another platform is not installed. --dry-run prints the three lists; the run record keeps them (dependencies, constraints, overrides).

docs.title: Serialization and working images
docs.text: linecaster.formats.{alto,pagexml,hocr} write and read the three XML formats on lxml; linecaster.images.convert turns any page image into the working image. Neither imports datatrove, saturate or an engine.

docs.title: Common rules for ALTO, PAGE and hOCR
docs.text:
1. Native first, extension for the rest. Every value goes into the format's own vocabulary where it has a place. What it cannot hold, or what a reader would infer differently, goes into a small JSON extension on the element: ALTO OtherTag[@TYPE="linecaster"]/@DESCRIPTION referenced by TAGREFS; PAGE UserDefined/UserAttribute[@name="linecaster"]/@value; hOCR @data-linecaster. Writers compute what their own reader would infer and only write the extension when it differs, so ordinary pages carry few (ALTO: line confidences and scores; PAGE: usually only {"polygon": null} for box-only lines). extensions=False writes pure files; they then round-trip only what the format holds natively. Foreign files have no extensions and readers fall back to the inferred values.
  2. Semantic round trip (from_x(to_x(t))): regions, lines and words with their ids, text, geometry, confidences, alternatives, the hyphen flag, region label, raw label, score and heading level, line score, reading_order and row. Not serialized: docling (export only), paragraphs, Line.normalized, extra dicts, the steps' measurements other than datetime, source (readers set kind="converted", format, uri, image size). Readers return regions and lines in document order, which may differ from the original list order; tests compare by id. Provenance round-trips: every StepInfo (step, name, engine, revision, preset, preset hash, recipe, recipe hash, backend, settings; datetime as ALTO processingDateTime and PAGE MetadataItem/@date) is written as ALTO Processing, PAGE MetadataItem type="processingStep" with Labels, and hOCR linecaster-step-<n> metas next to ocr-system and ocr-capabilities (computed from what the file contains). Other tools' provenance is read too (ALTO OCRProcessing, OCR-D PAGE steps, hOCR ocr-system). METS agents per step: linecaster.runtime.provenance.mets_agents.
  3. Writing order. Regions are written by reading_order (regions without one after the others, in list order), each region's lines by reading_order. A line without a region goes before the first region whose first line comes after it; consecutive ones share one block. Readers assign line reading_order = position in document order and row = position in its block, and region reading_order = rank in the format's reading order; the writers record the original value in the extension whenever that differs (gaps, a running head read last, a region without an order), so irregular orders survive too.
  4. Lines without a region. ALTO and PAGE need a block around every line: they get a synthetic TextBlock/TextRegion (id lc_block_<n>, extension {"synthetic": true}) that the reader drops again (with extensions=False it comes back as a text region). In hOCR such lines sit directly in the ocr_page. The synthetic blocks are part of the format's reading order, so consumers that follow it do not lose those lines.
  5. Rounding. ALTO coordinates are floats in the schema: to_alto writes them exactly (shortest repr) by default, precision=0 writes integers. PAGE and hOCR hold integers only: points are rounded half up (floor(v + 0.5), deterministic); boxes are rounded by their corners (x0 = r(x), x1 = r(x + w), w = x1 - x0) so edges agree with the rounded polygons; PAGE clamps negative values at 0 (its schema forbids them). Rounding happens once: a second round trip is the identity (tested).
  6. Confidences. ALTO WC and PAGE TextEquiv/@conf / Coords/@conf are floats in 0..1 and written exactly. hOCR x_wconf is an integer percentage: confidences come back to 0.01. ALTO has no line confidence: a reader derives it as the length-weighted mean of the words' WC (as for foreign files); the writer stores the real line confidence in the extension when it differs from that mean.
  7. Line text vs. words. Words are joined with one space; when a line's text is not that join (double spaces, None with words), the text goes into the extension. A line without words is written as a single ALTO String carrying the line text and confidence (extension {"wordless": true}), as a PAGE TextLine with only a line TextEquiv, as an hOCR line with the text directly in the span. text=None (not recognized) and text="" (recognized as empty) stay distinct in all three.
  8. Output is deterministic: same input, same bytes (PAGE Created/LastChange default to 1970-01-01T00:00:00; pass created= for a real timestamp).
  9. Ids are written as they are. Schema-valid output needs ids that are XML NCNames (letters, digits, _ - ., not starting with a digit); the producers' ids (text_2, orphan_0, ...) are. Ids the writers make up themselves (synthetic blocks, tags, the page) avoid every existing id.
  10. Known limits. Characters XML cannot carry (C0 controls other than tab/newline) make the writers raise lxml's ValueError; text is not silently altered. Language is written to hOCR lang only.
  11. Tests cover the fixture in tests/conftest.py (polygon regions, baselines, box-only lines, empty and unrecognized lines, a region-less line, hyphenation, alternatives), irregular orders, 300 seeded random transcriptions per format (every tenth also validated against the XSD), and foreign files (ALTO v2 mm10, v3 without namespace, eScriptorium v4; PAGE 2010 and Transkribus 2013; Tesseract hOCR and tag-soup HTML).

docs.title: ALTO (writes 4.4, reads v1 to v4)
docs.text:
Transcription ALTO region TextBlock (Illustration TYPE=<label> for picture/chart regions without lines); Shape/Polygon only when the polygon is not the box region label LayoutTag TYPE="label" LABEL=<docling label>, one per distinct label, in TAGREFS raw label LayoutTag TYPE="raw_label" LABEL=<raw> region order ReadingOrder/OrderedGroup/ElementRef (regions with an order + synthetic blocks); without ReadingOrder readers use document order (ALTO's implicit order) line TextLine with BASELINE="x,y x,y ..." (4.2+ points syntax), Shape/Polygon word String (WC, ALTERNATIVE), SP between words; a hyphen word that ends in - ¬ ⸗ ‐ soft hyphen = is split into String + HYP (reader re-joins: word text and line text unchanged) score, heading level, line confidence extension

Reading foreign ALTO: namespaces v1–v4 or none; blocks anywhere under Page (margins, PrintSpace, nested ComposedBlocks, which are transparent); raw label = the LABEL of the first referenced tag (Transkribus StructureTag, eScriptorium OtherTag), Docling label mapped from it; BASELINE as a single number (ALTO < 4.2) becomes a horizontal line across the line box; SUBS_TYPE/SUBS_CONTENT are ignored (the word keeps its CONTENT); missing ids are generated (line_<rank>, <line>_w<k>, block_<n>); GraphicalElements are not read. Units: pixel is read as is; with image_width/image_height and Page/@WIDTH/@HEIGHT every coordinate is scaled to the image (also corrects pixel ALTO made on a master of another size); mm10 and inch1200 without the image size need dpi= (px = v * dpi / 254 resp. / 1200); otherwise from_alto raises ValueError rather than guessing.

docs.title: PAGE (writes 2019-07-15, reads 2009–2019)
docs.text:
Transcription PAGE region TextRegion with @type from the label (below); ImageRegion, ChartRegion, TableRegion, MathsRegion for picture, chart, table, formula regions without lines (PAGE does not allow lines in them) raw label @custom="structure {type:<raw>;}" (Transkribus convention; ; { } \ escaped as \uXXXX) region score / line score Coords/@conf region order ReadingOrder/OrderedGroup/RegionRefIndexed (nested groups read recursively, index sorted) line TextLine: Coords = polygon (the box when there is none, extension {"polygon": null}), Baseline, TextEquiv/@conf; alternatives as TextEquiv/@index 2.. (primary 1) word Word: Coords = box, TextEquiv bbox not in PAGE: readers take the bounds of Coords; the writer stores the box when it differs

Label mapping, Docling → TextRegion/@type: text, paragraph, list_item, handwritten_text, reference → paragraph; title, section_header → heading; page_header → header; page_footer → footer; caption → caption; footnote → footnote; document_index → TOC-entry; others → other (or paragraph). Reading: structure {type:...} wins when it is a known name, then @type: paragraph → text, heading → section_header, header → page_header, footer, page-number, signature-mark, catch-word → page_footer, footnote(-continued)/endnote → footnote, TOC-entry → document_index, list-label → list_item, everything else → text; the raw label is the structure type, else @type, else the element name (TableRegion). The writer adds the Docling label to the extension when the reverse mapping would not return it (e.g. title → heading → section_header). The same name table (_xml.RAW_TO_DOCLING) also maps eScriptorium/SegmOnto zones and PP-DocLayout names. Old PAGE Coords/Point children are read; text on glyphs only is joined into the word.

docs.title: hOCR 1.2
docs.text:
Transcription hOCR region div of class ocr_carea (page_header → ocr_header, page_footer → ocr_footer, picture/chart → ocr_photo, table → ocr_table, formula → ocr_math) with one p.ocr_par; bbox, poly when not the box line span.ocr_line: bbox, baseline slope offset (hOCR's straight line from the box's bottom-left), poly, x_wconf baseline that baseline cannot express (polyline, vertical) also x_bline x1 y1 x2 y2 ... (custom property) word span.ocrx_word: bbox, x_wconf raw label, region score, heading level, hyphen, alternatives extension

Reading foreign hOCR: XHTML or tag-soup HTML (lxml.html fallback); regions are the top-level float/area classes, lines are ocr_line, ocr_textfloat, ocr_caption and ocr_header/ ocr_footer spans inside a region (Tesseract's line classes); word text includes nested <strong>/<em>; image "..." may contain ;.

docs.title: Working images (linecaster.images.convert)
docs.text:
The working format for converted images is lossless WebP at full resolution (the block ImageConverter, preset working-image); lossy output is never produced. Delivered images used as they are (an access derivative) stay as delivered. Pages larger than the size limit go to rejects/.

  • Size limit (check_size): width ≤ 16,383 and height ≤ 16,383 (WebP) and width × height ≤ 2 × PIL.Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS, read at call time, never changed. 2× is exactly where Pillow's Image.open raises DecompressionBombError; that error is turned into ImageTooLarge with the same kind of reason. Checked from the header (Image.open without load), so oversized pages are never decoded; between 1× and 2× Pillow's warning is silenced and the page converted.
  • Color: embedded ICC → sRGB (LittleCMS, perceptual); a profile that cannot be applied is reported (icc_error) and the plain conversion used. 16-bit grayscale → 8 bit as round(v·255/65535); Pillow reads 16-bit RGB as 8-bit itself. Grayscale/bilevel/palette → RGB. Alpha is composited onto white (alpha_flattened); fully opaque alpha is just dropped. CMYK without a profile: Pillow's conversion. EXIF orientation is not applied (coordinates refer to the stored pixels) but reported as exif_orientation.
  • Encoding: always lossless WebP (VP8L), full resolution, method=0, exact=True; effort (Pillow's quality for lossless) defaults to Pillow's 80.
  • info: format, width, height, source_format, source_mode, pixels_sha256 (sha256 of the decoded 8-bit RGB bytes, row-major, what the WebP decodes to), sha256 (of the WebP), decoder (Pillow x / <source library> y / libwebp z), webp_settings, icc_applied, alpha_flattened; the keys match PageImage where they overlap.

docs.title: Tracing
docs.text: Every run is traced with OpenTelemetry (linecaster.tracing): spans per task always, spans per page for a sample chosen by page id plus every page that failed. Traces go to the run folder and, when the standard OTEL_* variables say so, to an OTLP endpoint; nothing is sent anywhere else. Terms are the glossary's.

docs.title: What is traced
docs.text:
Task spans, for every task:

Span What it covers Attributes (besides linecaster.block) linecaster.task the task, from its first page to its end (failed: status error, linecaster.error.type) task, tasks, sample, stage, units.failed_exported linecaster.warm_up a block loading its engine or client (warm_up()), per block that loads something block.name, preset, edition, engine, model, backend, server linecaster.server.start a server block's warm-up: starting linecaster serve or vLLM/SGLang until it answers server, model, preset, port linecaster.reader.file a file a reader is through: a Parquet file, a file of page records, a manifest (wall time, while its pages also passed the later blocks) file, pages, seconds.own (the time spent reading) linecaster.writer.flush a page record writer closing its files (a remote file is uploaded then) files

An image folder's file is one page: its reading is the page's, not a task span.

Unit traces, one per page (or item):

Span Parent What it covers linecaster.page (linecaster.item for items a binder makes) none: the trace's root from the reader (or the earliest fetch for it) to the end of the stage's last block linecaster.http.fetch the page each http(s) request a reader made for it: http.host, http.status, http.attempts, http.retries, http.wait_seconds (the rate limits' and the breaker's wait), http.pause_seconds (the time paused after a block such as a 429, or waiting for a usable proxy, when there was a pause), http.tries (each attempt: a status such as 200 or 429 for a response read whole, 200-cut for one the deadline per attempt cut, 200-html for an HTML page where another format was expected, no-response for a timeout or a connection or proxy error; http), http.what (image, ocr) linecaster.block the page one per block, from the boundary before it to the one after it: for a served block it includes the time the page waited in the window linecaster.request.prepare the served block's span building the request (image encoding), in saturate's prepare threads linecaster.request the served block's span from the built request to its result: the wait for a window slot, the HTTP call, retries; tokens.prompt, tokens.completion, finish_reason linecaster.serve.decode, linecaster.serve.queue, linecaster.serve.model the request in linecaster serve: the image decoded and the transcription read, the wait for the model's worker, the model call (lines, regions, words of its result)

A page's spans are children of its context explicitly, never of "the current span": pages are interleaved in the stream. A page that leaves the stage's blocks through a binder ends its trace there; the items get their own. A page that never reaches the end of the stage (a block dropped it) is ended when the task ends (linecaster.unfinished).

A failed page (an entry added to doc.metadata["errors"] in this stage) has status error on its root and on the block's span, with linecaster.error.type.

Attributes are identifiers and numbers under linecaster.*, never text or images: block (class), block.name (datatrove name), block.family, unit, page.id, item.id, step, preset and edition (of id@edition), engine, model, backend (in-process, served), server (the endpoint), counts on a block's span as the page leaves it (lines, regions, words of the block's transcription), tokens.prompt, tokens.completion, finish_reason, error.type, region (a region recognizer's request). The resource of every span: service.name (linecaster), service.version, host.name, linecaster.process (pipeline, serve), linecaster.run (the run folder's name, or LINECASTER_RUN), linecaster.task, linecaster.tasks, linecaster.stage, linecaster.gpu and linecaster.gpus (from the NVIDIA driver, when there is one); OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES adds to them.

Log records carry trace_id and span_id in extra (JSON lines on Jobs show them): the page a record names by page_id, else the span of the per-unit block running in the thread, else the task's span.

docs.title: Sampling
docs.text:
--trace-sample SHARE (build(..., trace_sample=), default 0.01): a page is sampled when a hash of its id (BLAKE2b, 64 bits) is below SHARE, so the same pages on every rerun and machine, and a larger sample contains a smaller one. 0 traces only failed pages and the task spans; 1 traces every page. A sampled page's record carries its trace id (page.metadata.trace_id), so the page records lead to the trace.

Every page gets a trace context (doc.metadata["trace"]["traceparent"], W3C, flags 01 for a sampled page, 00 otherwise). The spans of an unsampled page are recorded but not sampled and held per page in a span processor (linecaster.tracing.export.PageBuffer) until the page's root ends: if the page failed in the stage they are exported, otherwise dropped. The memory this takes is bounded by the pages in flight: about 3 KB per ended span, one per block and two per request (about 40 KB per page for the twelve blocks of the squiddle recipe). In-process a page or two are in flight; a served block holds at most its window and its result queue (max_window + 4 × max_window pages), so with the default window of 32 and five served blocks about 800 pages, some 30 MB. A page dropped by a block is held until the task ends. linecaster serve records nothing for an unsampled page: a failed unsampled page's trace has the pipeline's spans, not the server's.

docs.title: Where traces go
docs.text:
• The run folder, always: OUT/traces/<rank>.jsonl.gz per task (OUT/traces/<stage>/<rank>.jsonl.gz with several stages), any fsspec folder like the logs; linecaster serve started by a task (ModelServer) writes <rank>.serve.jsonl.gz next to it (the task gives it the file in LINECASTER_TRACES). The format is OpenTelemetry's file exporter format: one ExportTraceServiceRequest per line in the OTLP JSON encoding, gzipped. Spans are written in batches (every 2 s), each flushed to the file, which is closed (uploaded, for a remote folder) when the task ends, also when it fails; a process killed outright loses its last batch, and linecaster traces reads such a file as far as it goes. A rerun of a task replaces its file. linecaster serve closes its file when it is stopped (the first SIGTERM or SIGINT ends it gracefully; its handlers are set again after the engines load, since an engine's library may replace them).
  • An OTLP endpoint, when OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT or OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT is set (and OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER is not none): OTLP over HTTP (protobuf), configured by the standard variables (headers, timeouts). linecaster serve exports there too; ChatModelServer starts vLLM with --otlp-traces-endpoint and OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_PROTOCOL=http/protobuf.

Without a run folder (run_pages, tests) and without OTLP nothing is traced.

The trace context and the servers. saturate sends the same headers with every request, so a served block puts the page's traceparent into the request body ("traceparent"), which linecaster serve reads (as it reads the header, if a client sends one). An OpenAI-compatible chat server reads it from the headers only: vLLM continues a traceparent header when started with --otlp-traces-endpoint, so with OTLP configured its spans reach the backend, but as traces of their own, not joined to the pages'.

docs.title: The command
docs.text:
linecaster traces OUT [--by block|preset|task] [--slowest N] [--json]

reads OUT/traces/**/*.jsonl.gz (a task still running: what its file has so far) and prints:

  • per block (or preset edition, or task) the duration of its linecaster.block spans over the traced pages (n, p50, p90, p99, errors); for served blocks the split: prepare, request (as the pipeline saw it), and the server's queue, decode and model;
  • the gaps: per block the time it had no page in it between its first page and its last (it waited for its input), when every page was traced (--trace-sample 1);
  • the N slowest traced pages (default 10) with their id, seconds, lines, slowest block and trace id;
  • per task its duration, GPU and sample, the warm-up of each block and the server starts, the reader's files (pages, seconds reading) and the writers' flush.

--json gives the same as data.
